author: oliver-ni
body: ## Summary Adds a JWKS-validated OAuth resource server to the Python API. The Next.js OIDC provider (PR contestdojo/contestdojo#41) issues JWT access tokens (`aud=`); this API verifies them against the provider's `/api/oidc/jwks` and serves the authenticated user's data. **Routes** (mounted at `/v1alpha1/me`): - `GET /v1alpha1/me/events` — list all events the user is registered for - `GET /v1alpha1/me/events/{event_id}` — single event participation Each returns `{event, registration, team}` where `team` is a **reference (id + name only)** — no teammate PII is exposed. Scope: `read:events`. **Key design decisions** (anchored on GitHub/Spotify/Stripe conventions): - Event-centric (no flat `/me/teams`); team is a nested reference, not a peer resource - Single `read:events` scope with `read:` prefix to signal read-only - `TeamRefSchema` keeps other students' data private — one user's consent doesn't expose their teammates - Custom `on_error` handler returns 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` for auth failures (per RFC 6750) **Auth middleware flow:** ``` Bearer JWT → verify sig via JWKS → check iss/aud/exp → OAuthUser(uid, scopes) → @require_scope("read:events") gates each route (403 if missing) → FirebaseUser (legacy admin) on /me routes → 401 (wrong principal type) → OAuthUser on legacy admin routes → 403 ``` Tested E2E: 12/12 checks pass (JWT structure, data responses, 401/403 enforcement, legacy-route regression). Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/50c37599d8654d40abd0c67341b0ee41 Requested by: @oliver-ni ---

author: lastfat00-ux
body:
This PR implements memoization for external command execution in `src/cache-utils.ts`. 

In monorepo environments, `setup-node` may execute shell commands (like `yarn config get cacheFolder` or `yarn --version`) multiple times across different project directories. Spawning these external processes is expensive and often redundant. By caching the resulting Promises (keyed by command and working directory), we eliminate unnecessary process spawns.

Additionally, this PR:
1. Fixes a bug in `getCommandOutputNotEmpty` where the "not empty" check was incorrectly evaluating a Promise instead of the resolved string.
2. Unifies cache resetting by integrating the new command cache into `BaseDistribution.resetCache()`, ensuring all internal caches are cleared during tests.
3. Updates the `dist/` directory to ensure the latest source optimizations (including existing ones like Schwartzian transforms in `BaseDistribution`) are included in the build artifacts.

Benchmarking results:
- Baseline: ~14.4ms per call (20 iterations of `node --version`)
- Optimized: <0.1ms per call
- Performance Gain: >99% for cached execution paths.

author: waylandyang
body:
## Phase A — recipes/README.md reorg

The recipes/ directory already had non-AI use cases (postgres-fixture for DB testing, playwright-browser for browser farms, nodejs for generic JS) — but the top-level README only categorized by AI agent framework. New \"By problem you're solving\" table makes the breadth explicit:

| Problem | Recipes |
|---|---|
| AI agent fan-out | langgraph-react, crewai-fanout, autogen-branch, openai-swarm, mcp-agent, speculative-agent, coding-agent-fork |
| **CI test parallelism** | postgres-fixture, **ci-parallel-pytest (new)** |
| **Database test fixtures** | postgres-fixture |
| **Browser automation farms** | playwright-browser |
| Notebook / code interpreter | jupyter-kernel, e2b-codeinterpreter |
| Generic compute | python-numpy, coding-agent, nodejs, agent-workbench |

The AI agent lens stays prominent (first row) — this isn't a rebrand, just a widening of the discovery surface.

## Phase B — new recipe \`ci-parallel-pytest\`

\`\`\`
                 ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │  parent snapshot ci-pytest           │
                 │  python:3.12-slim + pytest + numpy   │
                 │  + pandas + sklearn + your tests     │
                 │  (heavy imports already paid)        │
                 └────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                  │  mmap MAP_PRIVATE (CoW)
       ┌──────────┬───────────────┴───────────┬─────────┐
       │ worker 1 │   worker 2   │ worker 3   │ worker N│
       │ pytest   │   pytest     │ pytest     │ pytest  │
       │ slice 1  │   slice 2    │ slice 3    │ slice N │
       └──────────┴──────────────┴────────────┴─────────┘
\`\`\`

A typical Python ML CI re-pays ~1.5 s of \`import numpy/pandas/sklearn\` on every fresh worker container. With forkd, those imports live in the warmed parent's snapshot; every fork inherits them via mmap CoW. Per-worker fixed cost drops from ~3.5 s (container cold-start + imports) to ~80 ms (forkd spawn) + 0 ms (warmed imports).

Ships:
- \`build.sh\` — wraps python:3.12-slim + pinned deps + the demo test project + a prewarm step
- \`test_project/\` — ~30 representative tests across 5 files (arithmetic, numpy, pandas, sklearn, text)
- \`demo.py\` — fan-out driver: slices tests across N workers, runs each in a child sandbox, reports per-worker spawn/exec + total wall-clock + sequential baseline
- \`README.md\` — story, when-to-use / when-not, quickstart, GitHub Actions snippet, comparison vs sequential / pytest-xdist / docker

## Numbers

The README quickstart shows projected numbers (i7-12700 / ext4):

| Approach | Wall-clock 4 workers |
|---|---|
| Sequential, fresh container | ~4-5 s |
| pytest-xdist -n 4 in one container | ~3 s |
| docker × 4 fresh containers | ~5-7 s |
| **forkd fan-out (this recipe)** | **~1.6 s** |

Real dev-box measurement is the follow-up commit before merge — keeping this PR as **draft** until those land.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` n/a (no Rust changes)
- [x] \`cargo test\` n/a (no Rust changes)
- [ ] Real numbers from dev box (pending; will be follow-up commit)

author: lispc
body:
## Summary

This PR modernizes multiple parts of the codebase and adds a round of matching-engine performance optimizations.

### Modernization Changes
- **Auto-generate gRPC code** via `tonic-build` in `build.rs` instead of hand-copied `src/rpc/exchange/` and `src/rpc/rollup/`
- **Replace `BaseProducer`** manual thread with `FutureProducer` + `tokio::sync::mpsc` channel
- **Simplify `message/` trait hierarchy**: replaced `RdConsumerExt`, `MessageHandlerAsync`, `TypedMessageHandlerAsync`, `TypedMessageHandler`, `SyncTyped`, `Simple`, `TopicBuilder`, `ChainedTopicBuilder` with a clean `MessageHandler` trait + `TypedHandler`/`SimpleHandler`
- **Remove `fluidex-common`** git dependency entirely; inline crypto traits (`FrExt`, `DecimalExt`, `PubkeyExt`, `SignatureExt`) into `src/utils/crypto.rs`
- **Add direct deps**: `babyjubjub-rs`, `ff_ce`, `poseidon-rs`, `num-bigint`, `num-traits`
- **Update GitHub Actions CI**:
  - Rust: 1.53.0 → 1.90.0
  - actions: checkout@v2 → v4, action-rs → dtolnay/rust-toolchain, cache@v2 → Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
  - Node.js: 16 → 20
  - docker-compose path: `orchestra/docker` → `docker/`
  - Install `protobuf-compiler` for `tonic-build`

### Performance Optimizations
Profiling under pair-trade load revealed the engine was bottlenecked by Kafka producer backpressure and JSON serialization.

- **Kafka producer channel capacity**: 100K → 1M to avoid `try_send().unwrap()` panic under load
- **`Trade` struct**: `market`/`base`/`quote` from `String` to `InternedString`, eliminating per-trade heap allocations
- **Kafka message serialization**: replace `serde_json::to_string` with `simd_json::to_string`
- **`BalanceMapKey`**: `asset` from `String` to `InternedString`; hash on the interned pointer for O(1) `HashMap` lookups
- **`InternedString`**: add `From<&str>`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, and `Hash` impls needed by the new callers

### Known Limitations / Notes
- The matching engine core remains single-threaded (all writes route through one `mpsc` consumer). The measured single-market throughput ceiling is ~10K orders/s with the current client setup.
- `simd-json` is used only for Kafka producer serialization, not for REST/gRPC payloads, so downstream JSON consumers remain compatible.
- CI is currently pinned to Rust 1.90.0 because that was the latest stable at the time the modernization started.

body:
## Summary
Phase 3 of the backup-assurance reporter — turns the Phase 2 `compliance` view into a **customer-facing branded report** and adds a computed **3-2-1-1-0 backup-rule badge**.

- **`rule_321110` SQL view** — per-asset 3-2-1-1-0 verdict (3 copies, 2 media, 1 offsite, 1 immutable, 0 errors) computed live, parallel to `compliance`. The `2 media` / `1 offsite` checks ride provisional copy fields and are labelled best-effort in every output.
- **`internal/report/render`** — one shared `ReportData` (assembled from `ReportSummary`/`ComplianceRows`/`Rule321Rows`) rendered two ways: branded **HTML** (`html/template`, auto-escaped) and **pure-Go PDF** (maroto v2 — no headless browser, static multi-arch build preserved).
- **Two surfaces** — a `report render --tenant X --format html|pdf --out FILE` CLI subcommand, and a read-only `GET /report?tenant=&format=` HTTP endpoint served by the capture process when `report.listen` is set (GET-only, localhost-default, optional constant-time bearer auth, security headers, render-to-buffer).
- **Config** — optional `report:` block (`listen`, `authToken`, `brandName`).
- **Demo/docs** — Grafana already shows compliance; the demo gains the report endpoint, `docs/report.md` documents both surfaces.

The exporter binary and image are untouched (maroto/pgx confined to `cmd/report`). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-06-backup-report-phase3-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-06-backup-report-phase3.md`.

## Test Plan
- [x] `make ci` green — gofmt, vet, golangci-lint (0 issues), `go test -race ./...`, govulncheck (0 affecting; bumped x/crypto → v0.52.0 for GO-2026-5013), build
- [x] TDD per task; testcontainers cover the `rule_321110` view, `Build`, and the HTTP handler (200/401/400/404/405 + headers); `html/template` XSS-escape asserted; PDF `%PDF` asserted
- [x] Semgrep clean (no inline suppressions — `ResponseWriter.Write` restructured to `writeBytes(io.Writer, …)`)
- [x] Security review of the HTTP surface (timing-safe bearer via sha256, WWW-Authenticate, no tenant oracle) + final holistic review: READY TO MERGE
- [ ] `make demo` then `curl 127.0.0.1:9103/report?tenant=acme-corp` — visual check of the branded report (optional)

body:
## Summary

Methodology review of 11 new SKILL.md files (9 skills + 2 agents) added in the June 2026 batch.

Reviewed by @migmcc — quality engineering practitioner, 25+ years, claims manager, 8D specialist.

## Files corrected — per-file score and corrections

| File | Score before | Score after | Corrections made |
|------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|
| `skills/planning/ppap/SKILL.md` | 6/10 | 9/10 | Added mandatory 300-consecutive-part production trial run minimum (AIAG PPAP 4th ed §4.0) — critical gap, automatic rejection at most OEMs without this |
| `skills/planning/apqp/SKILL.md` | 8/10 | 9/10 | Added 300-part production trial run to Gate 4 criteria and Common Mistakes (aligned with PPAP correction) |
| `skills/planning/control-plan/SKILL.md` | 8/10 | 9/10 | Added OEM-specific special characteristic symbol conventions (Ford CC/SC, GM ★/Δ, VW D/E/I, BMW G-SC/G-CC, Stellantis) — using the wrong symbol is an immediate PPAP/IATF finding |
| `skills/planning/dvp-test-plan/SKILL.md` | 7.5/10 | 9/10 | Added handling for tests still in progress at PPAP submission (customer deviation process); added requirement that DVP revision must track DFMEA revision |
| `skills/measurement/msa-gauge-rr/SKILL.md` | 7/10 | 9/10 | Added root cause investigation and improvement actions when %GRR > 30% (separate tables for high-EV and high-AV root causes) — was missing entirely |
| `skills/measurement/spc-control-charts/SKILL.md` | 8/10 | 9/10 | Added 100-part minimum requirement for valid capability study as inline requirement in Step 4 (not only in Common Mistakes) |
| `skills/audit/vda-6-3-audit/SKILL.md` | 7/10 | 9/10 | Expanded weighting system explanation (critical: equal-weight averaging is a calculation error); added auditor qualification and independence requirements; improved score-4 vs score-6 distinction; added B-rating 3-month follow-up requirement |
| `skills/problem-solving/dmaic/SKILL.md` | 8/10 | 9/10 | Added hypothesis test selection guide (t-test / ANOVA / chi-square / regression decision table); clarified Control phase monitoring criteria (production data required, not pilot data) |
| `skills/supplier-quality/supplier-scar/SKILL.md` | 7.5/10 | 9/10 | Added AP revision check in D7 evaluation; added warranty cost recovery / debit note risk (critical business risk in OEM supply chains); added CS1/CS2 controlled shipping reference |
| `skills/agents/control-plan-builder/SKILL.md` | 7.5/10 | 9/10 | Added MSA qualification follow-up per measurement method (Q7); added AP revision check in D7 update mode; added poka-yoke suggestion for H-AP inspection-only controls |
| `skills/agents/ppap-checker/SKILL.md` | 7/10 | 9/10 | Added production trial run check (300-part minimum, blocking condition); OEM customer question at opening; corrected Element 11 Cpk thresholds (1.00–1.33 requires 100% inspection + customer waiver); added PSW form OEM blocking condition |

## Items outside scope (not changed — for @RBraga01 to decide)

- VDA 6.3: OEM-specific variant differences (BMW AFDS, VW PPF) — structural addition that would need a new section
- DMAIC: project selection criteria / financial threshold guidance — structural addition

## Overall assessment

All 11 files are methodologically sound and well-structured. The corrections address:
- **1 Critical gap** (PPAP production trial run minimum — industry-standard requirement that was missing)
- **3 Major gaps** (MSA improvement actions for >30%, VDA 6.3 weighting calculation, SCAR warranty cost recovery)
- **7 Minor gaps** (OEM symbols, test-in-progress handling, capability data volume, hypothesis test selection, monitoring criteria, AP revision in agents, PSW form blocking)

Quality score: 7.5/10 average before corrections → 9/10 average after corrections. No file had a methodological error that would mislead a practitioner; all gaps were missing information rather than incorrect information.

author: 12vethamithran
body:
## Summary

Full-stack audit follow-up (frontend, backend, Docker, dependencies). No security vulnerabilities were found in either dependency tree; these changes harden build reproducibility, bring tooling current, and reduce image bloat. Frontend's two biggest rewrites (React 19, Tailwind 4) were **deliberately deferred** to dedicated PRs.

## Changes

### Infra / Docker
- **Node 20 → 22** (active LTS) in CI and `docker-compose.yml`
- **Backend lockfile**: added `backend/requirements.lock` (441 pinned transitive deps) and applied it as **pip constraints** in CI + `Dockerfile` for reproducible builds (`pyproject.toml` still drives *what* installs; the lock only pins *which version*)
- **Pinned nikto** clone to release tag `2.6.0`
- Dropped obsolete `version:` key from `docker-compose.yml`
- **New `backend/.dockerignore`** — `COPY . .` was baking `.env` secrets, a 75 MB `.venv-test/`, caches and logs into the image; now excluded

### Frontend dependency upgrades (low-risk majors)
- vite 7 → 8, `@vitejs/plugin-react` 5 → 6
- eslint 9 → 10, `@eslint/js` 10, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 5 → 7, `eslint-plugin-react-refresh` 0.4 → 0.5, globals 15 → 17
- framer-motion 11 → 12, zustand 4 → 5
- **Held back:** React 18, Tailwind 3, and tailwind-merge v2 (its v3 targets Tailwind v4)
- Fixed new `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` findings: lazy clock init in `Landing`; justified disables for reset-on-change effects in `ChainReplay`/`CommandPalette`
- Lint cleanup: `useForceGraph` exhaustive-deps warning

## Verification
- Backend: `pip install --dry-run -e ".[dev]" -c requirements.lock` → resolves cleanly, no conflicts
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `eslint` → 0 errors ✅ · `vite build` (Vite 8) ✅ · `npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities

## ⚠️ Before merging
`requirements.lock` was resolved under Python 3.13 (only local interpreter); CI/Docker run 3.12. Risk is low (dry-run clean, all standard PyPI pins), but **let CI go green on this PR first** — it validates the lock on real 3.12/Linux. Note `cd.yml` deploys to Render on push to `main` without waiting for CI.

author: ubxty
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes for OAuth-authenticated providers (`minimax-oauth`, `xai-oauth`, future variants):

1. **Stale-stream client rebuild no longer crashes for OAuth providers.** The stale-stream detector in `run_agent` kills stuck HTTP connections after 300s of no chunks. The cleanup path calls `_replace_primary_openai_client` which rebuilt the OpenAI client from `self._client_kwargs`. For API-key providers the kwargs carry a valid static key. For OAuth providers the live bearer lives in a credential pool / singleton resolver — kwargs are empty for `api_key`. The rebuild raised:

    ```
    openai.OpenAIError: The api_key client option must be set either by
    passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY
    environment variable
    ```

    User-visible symptom: 5-min freeze, then "Interrupted during API call" on next user input, with `agent.log` showing:

    ```
    Stream stale for 300s (threshold 300s) — no chunks received. model=MiniMax-M3 ... Killing connection.
    Failed to rebuild shared OpenAI client (stale_stream_pool_cleanup) ... The api_key client option must be set
    ```

    **Fix:** `_replace_primary_openai_client` now calls `_refresh_kwargs_for_oauth_provider` first, which re-resolves the bearer via the provider-specific resolver before building. Generic dispatcher over all OAuth providers — not just minimax — so xai-oauth and any future OAuth provider get the same fix for free. Resolver failure is best-effort: log at debug and fall back to cached kwargs (a stale token beats a dead client).

2. **`minimax-oauth` auxiliary tasks no longer fall through to "unhandled auth_type".** `hermes_cli.auth.ProviderConfig` defines `minimax-oauth` with `auth_type='oauth_minimax'` (a third OAuth variant alongside `oauth_device_code` and `oauth_external`). The auxiliary-client dispatch in `agent/auxiliary_client.resolve_provider_client` only knew about the first two, so every auxiliary call (vision, session_search, compression, curator) hit:

    ```
    WARNING resolve_provider_client: unhandled auth_type oauth_minimax for minimax-oauth
    ```

    and returned `(None, None)`, forcing a fallback to openrouter (which minimax users typically don't have configured). Result: auxiliary tasks silently fail or bill to the wrong provider, and `agent.log` fills with `marking openrouter unhealthy for 60s (payment / credit error)` cycles.

    **Fix:** widened the dispatch set to include `'oauth_minimax'`, added a `_build_minimax_oauth_aux_client` helper that mirrors the existing `_build_xai_oauth_aux_client` pattern, and added a new early-return branch in `resolve_provider_client` for `provider=='minimax-oauth'` before the catch-all OAuth arm.

## Reproduction (before the fix)

From a real `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` on a `minimax-oauth` session (model `MiniMax-M3`, 200k+ token context):

```
12:38:15  Stream stale for 300s (threshold 300s) — no chunks received. model=MiniMax-M3 context=~193,044 tokens. Killing connection.
12:38:15  Failed to rebuild shared OpenAI client (stale_stream_pool_cleanup) ... error=The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable
12:39:30  Stream stale for 300s ... Killing connection.                       (same pattern, repeats)
12:39:30  Failed to rebuild shared OpenAI client (stale_stream_pool_cleanup) ... error=The api_key client option must be set
12:44:30  Stream stale for 300s ... Killing connection.
12:44:30  Failed to rebuild shared OpenAI client (stale_stream_pool_cleanup) ... error=The api_key client option must be set
```

Each cycle = 5 minutes of "waiting for model response" for the user.

```
12:49:09  WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: resolve_provider_client: unhandled auth_type oauth_minimax for minimax-oauth
12:49:09  WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary: marking openrouter unhealthy for 60s (payment / credit error).
12:49:09  WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary Nous client unavailable: no Nous authentication found (run: hermes auth).
```

…repeating dozens of times per session.

## Test plan

- 8 new tests, all passing (RED → GREEN confirmed):
  - `tests/run_agent/test_minimax_oauth_stale_rebuild.py` (4 tests): rebuild succeeds for minimax-oauth, falls back to cached bearer on resolver failure, also works for xai-oauth, no-op for api-key providers
  - `tests/agent/test_minimax_oauth_auxiliary_dispatch.py` (4 tests): `ProviderConfig` contract pin, no-credentials path doesn't trigger the "unhandled auth_type" warning, with-credentials path returns a real client pointed at `api.minimax.io/v1`, base URL gets the `/anthropic` → `/v1` rewrite
- 314/314 existing tests pass across the most relevant suites: `tests/run_agent/` (create_openai_client_reuse, streaming, anthropic_third_party_oauth_guard), `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client*.py`, `tests/agent/test_minimax*`, `tests/agent/test_anthropic_oauth_pkce`, `tests/test_minimax_oauth.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_xai_oauth_provider.py`
- Independent reviewer subagent (fresh context) passed: no security issues, no logic errors, 4 non-blocking suggestions, 3 of which were addressed in this PR (flattened 1-tuple to a plain string, added the xai-oauth regression test)

## Files changed

- `run_agent.py` — `_refresh_kwargs_for_oauth_provider` + dispatch in `_replace_primary_openai_client` (66 lines)
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py` — `_build_minimax_oauth_aux_client` + dispatch branch (58 lines)
- `tests/run_agent/test_minimax_oauth_stale_rebuild.py` (new, 275 lines)
- `tests/agent/test_minimax_oauth_auxiliary_dispatch.py` (new, 187 lines)

Total: 4 files, 581 insertions, 1 deletion.

author: akarras
body:
💡 What: Replaced `Memo::new` with `Signal::derive` in `ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/routes/welcome.rs` for `has_homeworld`.
🎯 Why: In Leptos, `Memo` creates a new reactive node that incurs allocation overhead. The `has_homeworld` operation is a very cheap check (`homeworld.with(|w| w.is_some())`). Wrapping this in a reactive `Memo` creates unnecessary overhead because maintaining the memoization node is more expensive than simply recomputing the condition on demand. `Signal::derive` is a better fit for lightweight derivations and removes the reactive allocation overhead.
📊 Impact: Removes the allocation and tracking overhead of an unnecessary `Memo` node on component mount.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by running the application and observing no regressions in functionality on the welcome page, while having marginally lower memory and processing overhead.

author: szymonstolarski
body:
GARCH evaluation layer — supervisor feedback fixes (proxy, MCS cross-check, reproducibility)

Context

This branch addresses three methodological concerns raised by the PhD supervisor after reviewing the initial GARCH out-of-sample results:

  1. MCS returning p-value = 1 for all 15 models — needed to verify whether this was an implementation bug or a substantive result
  2. Squared returns used as variance proxy — known to be noisy and to reduce DM/MCS test power
  3. Expanding vs sliding window not surfaced as an explicit user choice

Changes to the pipeline

New file — volatility_pipeline/evaluation/proxies.py

Implements three realized-variance proxy estimators:

  • garman_klass(open_, high, low, close) — Garman-Klass (1980), uses full OHLC range, 5–8× less noisy than squared returns; now the default proxy
  • parkinson(high, low) — Parkinson (1980), uses High/Low range only
  • squared_returns(returns) — original r² proxy, kept for reference and backwards compatibility

volatility_pipeline/evaluation/mcs.py

Added arch_mcs() — a cross-check wrapper around Kevin Sheppard's arch.bootstrap.MCS (T_max statistic, stationary bootstrap, arch 8.0.0). Runs alongside the custom MCS implementation and produces a side-by-side comparison table, making it possible to distinguish implementation bugs from substantive results.

volatility_pipeline/evaluation/rolling_forecast.py

  • ForecastResult gains a proxy field recording which estimator was used
  • RollingEvaluator.evaluate() and evaluate_many() accept an optional actuals_series parameter — pass any pre-computed proxy series and it is used as the evaluation target instead of squared returns; falls back to r² if omitted (fully backwards compatible)

volatility_pipeline/evaluation/__init__.py

Exports arch_mcs, garman_klass, parkinson, squared_returns.

main_pipeline.ipynb

  • Section 2 (settings): added VARIANCE_PROXY, WINDOW_TYPE, RANDOM_SEED, N_BOOT as explicit top-level variables — all randomness in the pipeline now flows from RANDOM_SEED in one place; previously seed=42 and n_boot=2000 were hardcoded in the MCS call cells
  • Section 3 (data import): extracts full OHLC from yfinance and computes the selected proxy before converting to PeriodIndex
  • Section 4.2 (evaluator): passes window_type=WINDOW_TYPE and actuals_series=variance_proxy through to the evaluator
  • Section 5.2.1 (new): arch MCS cross-check cell with side-by-side comparison table and interpretation guide

Experiments

Four runs stored in experiments/6.06.2026/ covering the full 2×2 grid:

  | r² proxy | Garman-Klass proxy -- | -- | -- Expanding window | 6_06_2026_expanding_rsquared.ipynb | 6_06_2026_expanding_garmanklass.ipynb Sliding window | 6_06_2026_sliding_rsquared.ipynb | 6_06_2026_sliding_garmanklass.ipynb

Settings: Brent (BZ=F), train 2010-01-05 → 2022-06-30 (3110 obs), test 2022-07-01 → 2026-05-29 (984 obs), QLIKE loss, MCS alpha = 0.05, RANDOM_SEED = 42, N_BOOT = 2000.

Key findings from the experiments

MCS — All 15 models survive in every configuration under both implementations. The earlier p = 1 result was a coding convention (early-stopping assigns 1.0 to all survivors), not a bug — arch's full-tournament implementation confirms the same set membership with actual bootstrap p-values. The result is substantive: at a 1-day-ahead horizon, GARCH-family models on daily Brent data are statistically indistinguishable as a group. GJR-GARCH-NORMAL is the weakest model (arch MCS p-value = 0.062 in the sliding/GK run — closest to exclusion).

Window type — Negligible effect. RMSE differences are in the 4th decimal place and rank ordering is identical across expanding and sliding for both proxies.

Proxy effect on RMSE — Rankings are robust. EGARCH family (especially EGARCH-T, EGARCH-GED) consistently leads; GJR-GARCH family consistently trails. RMSE magnitudes are not comparable across proxies (different target variable).

Proxy effect on QLIKE — More informative than RMSE. The GK proxy reveals two calibration problems invisible under r²: (1) EGARCH-NORMAL, which looks top-3 by RMSE, drops to rank 10–12 by QLIKE — the Normal distribution systematically underestimates tail variance; (2) the FIGARCH family, unremarkable under r², collapses to the bottom of the QLIKE ranking under GK — long-memory slow mean-reversion causes large proxy/forecast ratio mismatches on spike days that r² noise was masking. Best models by QLIKE across all four configurations: GARCH-T, EGARCH-T, APARCH-T.

DM test — Slightly more rejections with GK proxy (2 significant pairs at 5%) than with r² (0–1), confirming the expected power increase. Overall rejection count remains low, consistent with the MCS finding.

author: rocknroll17
body:
## What

Adds in-browser inference to the static GitHub Pages demo: the trained QR-Bloom UNet runs on tf.js's **WebGPU** backend. A full generation takes a few seconds, and it works on plain static hosting (no COOP/COEP needed).

## Why this engine

ONNX Runtime Web's WebGPU EP supports only 2-D conv, so the UNet's 3-D Conv/ConvTranspose fell back to WASM (CPU): ~17–48 s/run. tf.js *does* have WebGPU conv3d kernels, but they're ~8× slower than conv2d. So the ported model runs every 3-D conv as a stack of 2-D convs over depth slices — numerically identical to the PyTorch model (max|diff| 3.8e-4) but on the fast conv2d kernels (~0.3 s/forward).

## Changes

- `docs/qrbloom-model.js` — tf.js UNet3D port (conv2d depth-unroll), NDHWC layout
- `docs/qrbloom-inference.js` — tf.js WebGPU engine; multi-version download from HF (`tfjs/` weights); net build + WebGPU warmup deferred to first use so streaming on load doesn't stutter the UI
- `docs/index.html` — model-driven gallery UI: bottom-right progress bar + `Ready` status; view/export buttons revealed after the first generation (no layout jump); **Copy embed** yields a one-line `<iframe>` with the frozen tree packed (gzip + base64url) into the URL hash
- `docs/embed.html` — self-contained embed viewer (reuses the shared Viewer; turntable until touch, drag to rotate, Tree/QR scannable toggle)
- `scripts/export_for_tfjs.py` — export EMA weights to tf.js format for the HF `tfjs/` folder

## Hosting

tf.js weights for v2–v5 live on Hugging Face (`rocknroll17/QR-Bloom`, `tfjs/`); not committed to the repo, same as the ONNX path.

## Notes

- The embed is isolated inside its own iframe document, so it can be pasted into any page without import-map / global conflicts.
- Browsers without WebGPU fall back to the tf.js WASM backend (slower).

author: vbv-nyk
body:
## Summary

Out-of-band credential entry previously relied on spawning a terminal that runs `apra-fleet auth <member>`, with detection limited to `gnome-terminal`, `xterm`, and `x-terminal-emulator`. On many setups (kitty/alacritty/foot/konsole, or environments with no spawnable terminal such as the VSCode integrated terminal or tmux) this failed and dead-ended at a "run this manually" message.

This PR:

1. **Broadens terminal detection** — `findLinuxTerminal()` now checks `$TERM_PROGRAM` and probes a wider, ordered list of emulators (kitty, alacritty, foot, wezterm, ghostty, gnome-terminal, konsole, xfce4-terminal, mate-terminal, x-terminal-emulator, urxvt, xterm, st), each with its correct exec-flag convention.
2. **Adds a browser fallback** for `password`/`api-key` entry when no terminal is found — a hardened, loopback-only, single-use HTTP form opened via `xdg-open`/`open`/`start`. The submitted value flows through the same `submitPassword` path as the terminal/socket route, is encrypted immediately, and is never logged or exposed to the LLM.
3. **Extracts `submitPassword()`** so the socket (CLI) and browser paths deliver credentials identically.

The existing manual `apra-fleet auth <member>` message remains as the universal floor for headless/SSH.

Security hardening of the browser fallback:
- binds to `127.0.0.1` only (never `0.0.0.0`)
- 256-bit random token in the URL path; any other path → 404
- `Host`-header validation (DNS-rebinding defense)
- single submission then teardown; 2-minute TTL backstop
- submitted value and live URL never logged

Known limitation: the browser fallback is same-machine only (loopback) and does not help a remotely-hosted server — that would need a secure tunnel or MCP elicitation (out of scope).

Closes #290.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Testing

- [x] Ran `npm test` — all tests pass (1080 passing, incl. new `auth-web` hardening + `submitPassword` tests)
- [x] Ran `npm run build` — build succeeds (0 errors)
- [x] Manually tested the affected functionality — registered a password-auth member with no terminal available; browser form opened, value submitted, encrypted, and the flow continued

New tests:
- `tests/auth-web.test.ts` — loopback server hardening: token-path 404, non-loopback `Host` → 403, single-use teardown, empty-value rejection, failed-submit retry
- `tests/auth-socket.test.ts` — `submitPassword` unit coverage

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the existing style and patterns in this codebase
- [x] I have updated documentation where necessary
- [x] Breaking changes are noted above and in the commit message
- [x] No new linting errors introduced

author: kkroo
body:
## TL;DR

The long-reported *"PATCH `blockedByIssueIds` returns 200 but no-ops"* is **not a server bug** — the edge persists correctly. It's a **write/read field-name asymmetry** plus a docs gap, so agents that verified the wrong way concluded it failed.

## What's actually happening

- `blockedByIssueIds` is **write-only**. The service persists it correctly (`syncBlockedByIssueIds` → `issueRelations type:"blocks"`, with self/company/cycle checks), from both create and update.
- On **read**, `blockedByIssueIds` comes back **null**; the persisted edges surface in the hydrated **`blockedBy`** array (and the reverse side under **`blocks`** / `relatedWork`).
- Agents (e.g. `WAKE-PREFLIGHT.md`, which does `currentBlockedBy = response.blockedByIssueIds`) re-read `blockedByIssueIds`, saw `null`, and reported a "no-op" — even though the write landed.

Reproduced live against PEN issues: every child had a populated `blockedBy`, `blockedByIssueIds` null. So: write works, read field differs, docs never said so.

## Fix (descriptions + test only — no behavior change)

- **`packages/shared/src/validators/issue.ts`** — `.describe()` on `blockedByIssueIds`: write-only, full-set-replaces (`[]` clears), and *"verify via `blockedBy`, NOT by re-reading `blockedByIssueIds`."* This surfaces in both the create and update MCP tool param schemas.
- **`packages/mcp-server/src/tools.ts`** — spell it out in `paperclipUpdateIssue`, `paperclipGetIssue`, and `paperclipCreateIssue` descriptions (set via `blockedByIssueIds`; read via `blockedBy`/`blocks`).
- **`server/src/__tests__/issue-blocked-by-update-routes.test.ts`** — route test locking the contract: PATCH persists + surfaces both sides; full-array replace removes stale edges; `[]` clears all; dependency cycle → `422`.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/shared` + `packages/mcp-server` ✓
- new route test: **4/4 pass** (against `master`'s route code) ✓

No server logic changed — this removes the foot-gun that made a working feature look broken.

body:
This submission introduces `soft_sensor_pipeline.py`, a robust Python script designed to process soft sensing data. It automatically detects timestamp columns in laboratory and real-time `.xlsx` datasets, aligns them using `pandas.merge_asof(direction='backward')`, and performs data cleaning (dropping missing matches, forward/backward filling). The data is then sequentially split into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% testing sets. It features correlation-based feature selection (pearson correlation > 0.1) on the training set to prevent data leakage. The script trains and hyperparameter-tunes SVR and PLS models using `GridSearchCV` with standard scaling, and includes a PyTorch-based LSTM model with sliding-window processing and early stopping. Finally, it calculates the RMSE for each model and outputs the predictions and evaluation metrics to an Excel file. Testing confirmed that the implementation works end-to-end flawlessly.

author: deblasis
body:
## Problem

The MSL backend (`src/spirv_to_msl.zig`) never declared array `OpConstantComposite`s, so a runtime index `a[i]` referenced an **undeclared identifier** — silent-wrong (glslpp exits 0, but the MSL does not compile in Metal). Two shapes were affected:

- **Function-local** `const T a[N]` → emitted `T v[N]; v = vC;` — `vC` (the array composite) was never declared, *and* a whole-array C-array copy `v = vC;` is itself invalid in Metal.
- **Module-scope** `const T a[N]` → a Private `OpVariable` with a constant initializer (after #158) whose name was never declared.

Repro: `glslpp msl tests/spirv-cross/lut-promotion.frag --stage fragment` previously referenced `LUT`, `v15`, `v18` with no declaration anywhere.

## Fix

Mirrors the GLSL/HLSL Design-A handling, adapted to Metal's rule that a C array is not assignable:

1. Emit each array `OpConstantComposite` referenced by name as a module-scope `constant T name[dims] = {…};` (Metal requires the `constant` address space for a program-scope array used from a function). Nested array/struct constituents are inlined into the brace initializer.
2. **Promote** read-only const arrays — const-initialized Private globals *and* read-only function-local const arrays — by aliasing the variable to its initializer constant (declaration eliminated; reads resolve to the module constant). This matches `spirv-cross --msl`, which promotes both to module scope.
3. **Brace-initialize** a *mutated* local const array in place (`T a[N] = {…};`) so it stays a mutable local without the invalid copy.
4. Skip the now-redundant whole-array initializer `Store`.

Mutation analysis follows a store's pointer **transitively** through nested `AccessChain`/`CopyObject` to the root variable, so a partial write hidden behind an unmerged nested chain still keeps the variable a mutable local rather than wrongly promoting it (which would silently drop the write). *(This hardening came out of code review.)*

### `lut-promotion.frag` after the fix
```
constant float  v4[16] = { 1.0, 2.0, … };          // module-scope LUT
constant float4 v15[4] = { float4(0.0), … };        // read-only `foo` → promoted
constant float4 v18[4] = { float4(20.0), … };       // `baz` → promoted
…
    float4 v20[4] = { float4(0.0), … };             // mutated `foobar` → brace-init local
    v20[1].z = 20.0;                                // partial write preserved
```
Structurally matches the spirv-cross oracle (3 module constants + 1 mutable local).

## Tests / verification (local — CI is billing-blocked)

- New `tests/msl_tests.zig` regressions: function-local + module-scope const arrays indexed at runtime (`int(gl_FragCoord.x)&3`) are declared and resolve; a mutated local is brace-initialized (not array-copied); a partial write via an unmerged nested chain is not promoted.
- `zig build test-msl`, `test-msl-argbuf`, `test-cross-compare` — green.
- `zig build conformance` — **2076 PASS / 0 FAIL** (unchanged).

author: teng-lin
body:
## What

Adds **depth-2** value-correctness assertions to the `cli_vcr` suite for the two richest list outputs (`source list --json`, `artifact list --json`). Every new assert is cassette-derived or an invariant — no pinned recorded literals — so they survive a re-record against a different notebook and pass the widened re-record-safety lint (`test_no_pinned_cassette_values`).

Implements **PR-B** of the cli_vcr reality-based plan (`.sisyphus/plans/2026-06-06-vcr-cli-reality-based.md`, #1452). Keeps Phase-1's structural tiers; these are additive depth.

## The projection-helper independence rule (load-bearing)

New `tests/integration/cli_vcr/_cassette_expectations.py` is a `_`-prefixed non-`test_*` module (so the #1445 cross-test-import gate stays green). It reads a cassette with **stdlib + `yaml` ONLY** — it does **not** import `notebooklm.rpc.decoder`, `notebooklm._row_adapters`, `notebooklm._types`, the cli services, or any client code.

Why: a cassette-derived assertion is a **projection layer, not a decoder oracle**. If the helper imported the production decoder, the assert would be a tautology ("the CLI's decode == the decoder's decode" proves nothing). Instead it re-implements just the batchexecute envelope walk as its own code — XSSI `)]}'` strip, chunked `wrb.fr` frame extraction, and the **second** `json.loads` of slot `[2]` — copied from the patterns in `tests/_guardrails/test_cassette_shapes.py` (not imported). The projection is a coarse, **shallow** read (id/url tokens + top-level type/status codes) and never replicates the adapters' deep positional field-mapping. It catches **fabrication / drop / duplicate / miscount**, not field-position (that's a separate adapter-level follow-up).

`load_rpc_payload(cassette, rpc_id, occurrence=0)` selects the interaction by request `rpcids=`, then the `wrb.fr` envelope by id (ignoring `di`/`af.httprm`/`e` housekeeping), and supports an `occurrence` index for repeated rpc ids.

## The two new tiers

**Tier 2b — cassette-derived value correctness.** The CLI's emitted ids/urls/count are checked against the independent projection of the *same* cassette:
- `source list --json` (`test_sources.py`): `count == proj.count`; id-set **EQUALITY** (`{i["id"]} == proj.ids`, sources are reliably UUID-shaped); every CLI url ∈ `proj.urls`.
- `artifact list --json` (`test_artifacts.py`): id **CONTAINMENT** + count floor (`proj.ids ⊆ cli_ids`, `len(cli) >= proj.count`). The CLI artifact list merges note-backed mind maps from a *separate* RPC (so the CLI output is a superset of the `gArtLc` projection), and artifact ids are **not** all UUID-shaped — so uuid-anchoring / set-equality don't hold here. Type/status code-histogram in-range consistency too.

**Tier 2c — per-field semantic invariants** (`assert_semantic_invariants(item, kind)` in `conftest.py`): a `url` parses (`urllib.parse`, scheme + netloc); `type`/`type_id`/`status` ∈ the known enum value sets; `created_at` parses; a source `id` is UUID-shaped. The enum value sets are read from `notebooklm` types **only as an allowed-membership definition** (a `value in <set>` check, not a decode). Catches "valid type but wrong field" (e.g. a title read out of the url slot fails the URL-shape check).

## Teeth-proof

Temporarily mutated the projection to **drop one id** → the `source list` id-set-equality test **FAILED** loudly with an actionable diff (`only-in-CLI=[...]`). Separately **fabricated an id** → the `artifact list` containment test **FAILED** (`recorded LIST_ARTIFACTS ids missing from CLI output`). Both reverted. The cassette-derived assert is a real oracle with teeth, not a tautology.

## Scope / safety

- **Test-only**: no `src/` changes. `audit_public_api_compat.py` stays exit 0 with **0** new allowlist entries.
- `record_mode="none"` — no cassettes recorded or modified.
- Verified green: `pytest tests/integration/cli_vcr/`, full `pytest`, `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy src/notebooklm`, and the guardrails `test_no_cross_test_imports` + `test_no_pinned_cassette_values` (the new asserts PASS the pinned-value lint).

author: rigerc
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause of "Waiting for changes"**: `MarkdownArea.tsx` used `||` to fall back to its own template constant when `initialMarkdown` was empty. After the earlier commit set `EntryView`'s `DEFAULT_MARKDOWN = ''`, every new entry passed `''` to `MDArea`, which silently substituted the template. The initialization effect then called `setMarkdown('')` to clear it, but React's `markdownContent` state was already `''` — so the autosave trigger always saw empty content, stayed `idle`, and never saved.

- **Debounce instability**: `handleEntryUpdated`, `upsertEntry`, and `handleEntryDeleted` in `App.tsx` were recreated on every render. This caused `executeAutosave` (which depends on `onEntryUpdated`) to also be recreated, re-running the autosave timer effect and clearing the debounce on every parent re-render.

- **Missing `group_id` in selections**: `get_entry_selections` SQL was missing `go.group_id`, leaving every `Selection` object with `group_id: undefined` at runtime despite the TypeScript type requiring it.

- **Router using body fields directly**: `update_mood_entry` computed `fields = body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` for the empty check but then passed `body.mood`, `body.content` etc. directly instead of `fields.get(...)`.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/components/MarkdownArea.tsx` | Set `DEFAULT_MARKDOWN = ''`, use `??` instead of `\|\|` for the `markdown` prop |
| `src/App.tsx` | Wrap `upsertEntry`, `handleEntryDeleted`, `handleEntryUpdated` in `useCallback` |
| `api/database_groups.py` | Add `go.group_id` to `get_entry_selections` SQL |
| `api/routers/mood.py` | Use `fields.get()` in service call |

## Test plan

- [ ] Create a new entry: select a mood, type content — status should transition `idle → dirty → saving → saved at HH:MM` within ~1.2s of stopping
- [ ] Edit an existing entry, change content — `PUT /api/mood/{id}` returns 200; selections in response include `group_id`
- [ ] Verify `GET /api/mood/{id}/selections` response includes `group_id` field
- [ ] Rapid typing should debounce correctly (one save per pause, not per keystroke)

author: nicolasalt
body:
## Summary

Production hit 100% disk. The docs/161 disk-tier escalation ladder works, but two gaps let the disk fill anyway: the disk-pressure safety valve was never configured in prod (and its only knobs were absolute bytes, wrong for any non-fixed disk size), and eviction keyed off idle age instead of the much stronger "PR merged = done" signal — so finished work lingered 14 days. This closes both gaps.

## Rationale

- **Fraction-of-disk watermarks over absolute bytes.** `DISK_FREE_LOW_BYTES` / `DISK_FREE_HIGH_BYTES` assume a fixed disk size, so the same prod config is wrong on any other host (self-hosters especially). New `DISK_FREE_LOW_PCT` / `DISK_FREE_HIGH_PCT` (0..1) derive the effective byte marks from the host's total disk at startup. `*_BYTES` still win when set (backward compat); the resolver handles each watermark independently and leaves it unset when neither source applies, so the override's existing "no-op unless both marks resolve" gate is unchanged.
- **Merge is a stronger "done" signal than idle age.** `merged_at` is already populated and already drives docs/161's recently-merged sidebar grouping. Branching the `light → evicted` decision on it lets us reclaim finished work after `DISK_IDLE_EVICT_MERGED_MS` (2d default) while leaving unmerged WIP on the gentle 14d `DISK_IDLE_EVICT_MS` clock. Idle age stays `max(lastUsedAt, lastViewedAt)`, so a merged session you reopened to look at isn't yanked mid-view. All existing guards and the auto-commit + push-before-wipe remediation are untouched — merged sessions re-fetch fresh on reopen, so this is reclaim-only with no data loss.
- **Resolved disk total once at startup**, not per pass — total is a fixed property of the host filesystem, reusing the same `statfs` probe that backs the free-bytes check (`total = blocks × bsize`).

On the affected box, merged-PR sessions accounted for **~94 GB of ~96.5 GB** of reclaimable on-disk session data (148 of 160 on-disk sessions), so keying eviction off "merged" targets exactly the tail that filled the disk.

## Changes

- **`disk-janitor.ts`**: `resolveDiskWatermarks` (per-watermark `*_BYTES`-precedence / `*_PCT × total` derivation), `statfsTotalBytes` probe, and merge-aware `light → evicted` threshold (`idleEvictMergedMs`, default `IDLE_EVICT_MERGED_MS`) inside `escalateDiskTiers`.
- **`sessions.ts`**: `IDLE_EVICT_MERGED_MS = 2d` beside `IDLE_EVICT_MS`.
- **`index.ts`**: parse `DISK_FREE_LOW_PCT` / `DISK_FREE_HIGH_PCT` / `DISK_IDLE_EVICT_MERGED_MS`; resolve effective watermarks against host disk total; thread `idleEvictMergedMs` into the escalation deps.
- **`deployment/vps/docker-compose.yml`**: set `DISK_FREE_LOW_PCT=0.10`, `DISK_FREE_HIGH_PCT=0.20`, `DISK_IDLE_EVICT_MERGED_MS=172800000` on the orchestrator — this is what actually turns the valve on in prod. `DISK_IDLE_EVICT_MS` left at its 14d default.
- **`docs/161`**: documented portable watermarks (+ `*_BYTES` precedence), merge-aware threshold + rationale, and the prod wiring.
- **Tests** (`disk-tier-escalation.test.ts`): resolver cases (bytes precedence, pct derivation, neither-set → disabled, pct-with-unknown-total → disabled) and merge-aware eviction (merged past threshold evicts; unmerged same age does not; merged + recent view protected; merged + dirty committed+pushed before wipe).

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run src/server/orchestrator/disk-tier-escalation.test.ts` — 20 passing (incl. 5 resolver + 4 merge-aware).
- `npx vitest run src/server/orchestrator/disk-janitor.test.ts src/server/orchestrator/sessions.test.ts` — green.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint:dev` — clean.

## Summary
- **sec-U11**: \`putObject\`, \`copyObject\`, and \`putObjectBuffer\` issued PutObjectCommand / CopyObjectCommand without \`ServerSideEncryption: 'AES256'\`. 🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The `check_email` method passed raw user input (`email`) directly into a custom HTTP header (`email_address`). If the user input contained newline characters (`\r` or `\n`), an attacker could inject arbitrary headers or split the HTTP request, leading to HTTP Request Smuggling or Header Injection vulnerabilities.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could perform HTTP Request Smuggling or Header Injection, potentially bypassing security controls or corrupting the HTTP request.
🔧 Fix: Added explicit input validation in `check_email` to reject email addresses containing `\r` or `\n`.
✅ Verification: A new unit test `test_check_email_rejects_newlines` has been added to verify that `ValueError` is raised for invalid email addresses.

## ClickUp Ticket

<!-- Required: Link to the ClickUp ticket -->
<!-- Example: https://app.clickup.com/t/8655600/DUPLOAI-12345 -->

**ClickUp Ticket ID:** DUPLOAI-1591

## Overview

Follow-up to #16 (which added the `pr-review` skill). This adds **Terraform
Plugin Framework schema-correctness** review rules to the skill, graded by
actual impact rather than a blanket severity, plus a small `.gitignore` tidy.

Motivation: a common misconception is "Optional attributes should always be
Computed." That's wrong — `Optional` and `Optional+Computed` mean different
things, and misusing them either breaks `apply` or causes perpetual drift. The
skill now encodes the correct rules so reviews catch these consistently.

## Summary of changes

This PR does the following:

- Add **Schema correctness — apply-breaking** checks to the skill's 🔴 Blocker
  tier: no `Required`+`Computed` combo (framework rejects it); server-defaulted /
  normalized fields must be `Optional+Computed` (not `Optional`-only, which
  triggers "inconsistent result after apply"); `Optional+Computed` needs a
  `default` the server doesn't always return; secret-bearing attributes must set
  `sensitive: true`.
- Add **Schema correctness — drift / update-breaking** checks to the 🟠 Major
  tier: `forceNew` on immutable inputs; `default` must match the server's real
  default; enum fields use `oneOf`; server-normalized Required fields flagged.
- Move cosmetic items (`(known after apply)` churn, type appropriateness) to the
  🟡 Minor tier and add a `schema correctness` line to the "Checks run" summary.
- `.gitignore`: ignore `.DS_Store`.

## Testing performed

- [ ] Using unit tests
- [ ] Using acceptance tests (`TF_ACC=1`)
- [x] Manually, on my local system

Docs/tooling-only change. Re-read the rendered skill to confirm the three
severity tiers stay consistent (no rule duplicated across tiers) and that the
output template and "Checks run" block reference the new schema line.

## Describe any breaking changes

- None. No provider code, schema, or generated artifacts change; the skill is
  review-only and makes no writes.

body:
## Проблема (#351)
`apply_descriptions.py` (`build_patch`) патчил у колонок **только** `description`, а `tags` на уровне колонки молча терял. Per-column теги в YAML (напр. `PII.Low` на колонках с именами игроков) не доезжали в OpenMetadata — у whoscored/understat в каталоге было `tags=[]`.

## Правка
- В цикле по колонкам `build_patch` добавлена генерация JSON-Patch op для `/columns/{idx}/tags` по аналогии с table-level `/tags`: обёртка `{tagFQN, labelType:Manual, state:Confirmed, source:Classification}`, op = replace/add.
- Идемпотентность: op не эмитится, если нужные теги уже присутствуют (`set(col_tags).issubset(existing)`).

author: bndct-devops
body:
Fixes #31. Intended as the **v1.3.1 hotfix** — branched off the `v1.3.0` tag, so it can be released without pulling in the unreleased `#30` work currently on `main`.

## The bug

A library marked **public** was invisible to everyone but its owner. `GET /libraries` only ever returned libraries you owned plus the built-in global (book-type) ones — it never looked at `is_public` or the `library_users` assignment table. So the public/private flag did nothing, and there was no UI to share a private library with individuals (despite the "share individually" copy in the editor).

The reporter was correct on both counts; there was also a third gap (even an admin-assigned private share wouldn't appear, since the list query ignored assignments too).

## The fix

- `list_libraries` now returns **own + global + public + privately-assigned** libraries (admins still see all).
- `book_visibility_filter` (and the two inline copies in `books.py`) now let **members** see books in public libraries too, so a now-visible public library actually shows its contents. The change is purely additive and, because everything routes through the shared filter, propagates consistently to downloads, OPDS, stats, send-to-device and TomeSync.
- **Library owners** (not just admins) can assign/revoke individual users on their own libraries; `/users/list` relaxed to `member` (returns only id/username/role) so the picker can be populated.
- New **"Share with users"** picker in the library editor.
- `LibraryOut` gains a server-computed **`can_edit`** flag; the frontend hides rename/delete/add-to-library controls on libraries you can't manage. This also cleans up a pre-existing wart where members saw dead edit/delete buttons on the global book-type libraries.

All library *mutations* remain owner/admin-gated (`_get_library`), so the widened list can't be used to modify others' libraries — those still 403. No data-loss path.

## Testing

- Full backend suite: **459 passed** (incl. new `tests/test_library_visibility.py`).
- Frontend `tsc -b`: clean.
- Headless-browser (Playwright) end-to-end against a clean two-member instance:
  - a second user sees another user's public library but **not** their private one;
  - the owner's editor shows the **Share with users** picker; after sharing, the second user sees the private library;
  - the second user gets **no** edit/delete controls on a library they don't own, while the owner does.

author: sundeepg98
body:
## Summary

Round-3 audit of the upload/auth/multi-tenant/SSRF spine. The slides→video **frames-upload path** was missing the v2.1 hardening the docx-convert path already has. Fixed by **mirroring the proven `crypto.py` pattern exactly**. **Tool surface unchanged at 57; no scope/consent changes** (verify-last respected).

> **Flagged for operator review — do NOT auto-merge** (prod). **Stacks after #167 → #166 → #168 → #170 → #174.** The `pip-audit (HIGH/CRITICAL gating)` job is **RED** here (pre-existing pyjwt 2.12.1 CVEs) until **#167** merges — expected for a non-dependency diff.

## (1) Frames upload — CONFIRMED REAL, fixed

### (a) No size/count cap → disk-fill DoS
`upload_frame_endpoint` did `body = await request.body()` **unbounded**, and `BodySizeLimitMiddleware` only checks a **declared** `Content-Length` — a chunked / CL-omitting POST falls through to endpoint enforcement that **didn't exist** (the middleware docstring even says so). `stage_frame_bytes` wrote whatever it got, no count limit.
**Fix:** the endpoint now reads via `request.stream()` with a **hard per-frame byte cap** (413 on over-cap, including the chunked case) + a Content-Length pre-check; the staging layer adds **per-batch frame-count + cumulative-byte caps** (`FrameUploadTooLarge` → 413). Caps aligned with `encode_video`'s read-side bounds (200 frames / 250 MiB) — staging now refuses what encode would reject anyway, but **before bytes hit disk**.

### (b) Token not single-use + not user-bound → replay + multi-tenant gap
The frames token signed only `(batch_id, expiry)` and `verify_frames_token` checked **only expiry** — no nonce (replayable across all 9999 indices for the 30-min TTL) and no uid (the v2.1 uid-binding applied to the docx URL was never mirrored).
**Fix (mirrors `crypto.py`):** the token canonical now covers `(batch_id, expiry, nonce, user_id)`; `verify_frames_token` **redeems the nonce** (single-use via a `_FrameBatchNonceStore`) and returns the **bound `user_id`** (str) or `None`. `sign_frames_batch` takes `user_id` (`current_user_id_or_none()` at the `video_deck` mint site; `"operator"` sentinel in stdio mode). Single-use is **per render session** (the renderer POSTs every frame under one token → the nonce binds to its batch and is accepted for that batch's frames; it can't be re-bound to a different batch, and is forgotten on expiry).

**Tests:** oversize (per-frame + chunked) → 413; over-count + over-cumulative-bytes → 413; uid tamper rejected; cross-batch token replay rejected (unit + endpoint level).

## (2) Outbound SSRF — DETERMINED NOT EXPLOITABLE (documented, not over-engineered)

Per the brief, I determined on the fresh tree whether `webapp_url` is attacker-influenceable on a request path. **It is not steerable to an internal/arbitrary host:**
- **Request path** (`docx_import._call_webapp`): the URL comes from per-user `apps_script_url`, which `user_store._valid_gas_url` gates on **both write** (`save_state` raises) **and read** (`get_state` drops tampered values) to `scheme=https` + `host=script.google.com` + `/macros/s/<id>/(exec|dev)`. A user cannot write `http://169.254.169.254/`, `localhost`, a private range, or a foreign host.
- **CLI path** (`cli._ping`): operator-local config, validated to `script.google.com` on save (`_cmd_set_webapp_url`).

So per the brief's decision tree (operator-only / host-pinned → document + lower severity, don't over-engineer), **no private-IP/redirect/scheme guard was added** — it would be redundant against a host-pinned value and unreachable by any test without first defeating the storage-layer validator. Added an **SSRF-posture comment** at `_call_webapp` documenting this and where a guard *would* go if a raw URL ever reaches it.

## Flagged for operator (NOT fixed — design decisions)
- **(a) End-to-end multi-tenant credential isolation** — `signed_url_user_id` → per-user creds dispatch is in place on the convert path, but whether `config.get_webapp_url` (process-global) is ever reachable on a per-user request path deserves an end-to-end audit pass.
- **(b) Vercel-KV nonce single-use-at-scale** — the in-process nonce stores (both the convert path's `NonceStore` and this new `_FrameBatchNonceStore`) are single-instance. Once nonces move to KV across multiple Vercel instances, single-use may not hold without a cross-instance store → a replay window per instance.

## Verification
- `ruff check src/ tests/` → **All checks passed!**
- `pyright src/` → **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations** (CI gate).
- Unit suite (uv venv): **87 passed** across the affected files (frames-staging, encode_video, video_deck, integration upload route, convert multitenancy); full `tests/unit` exit 0, 0 failures; **golden 57-tool surface intact**. The `encode_video` read-cap tests were decoupled from the new upload cap (they now write frame files directly) so each cap is tested independently.

**CI (Linux) is the authoritative gate.**

author: gregpriday
body:
Two bugs in the GitHub token expiry recovery flow.

## Summary

- A GitHub PAT expiry was producing two durable inbox rows plus a toast. `useGitHubTokenHealth`'s backstop used a raw `addEntry` with no `supersedeKey`; `useGitHubTokenExpiryNotification` used `notify()` with `supersedeKey: "github.token"` — so they never suppressed each other. Fix routes the backstop through `notify({ type: "warning", priority: "low", supersedeKey: "github.token", countable: false })`, making it inbox-only and sharing the key so whichever fires second archives the first. Also dropped `correlationId` from the backstop to cut the un-snooze re-toast path on a second expiry cycle.
- The "Reconnect to GitHub" button in `GitHubTokenBanner` dispatched a raw `CustomEvent` without `sectionId`, dropping the user at the top of the Code Forge settings tab. Fix routes through `actionService.dispatch("app.settings.openTab", { tab: "code-forge", subtab: "github", sectionId: "github-token" })` — consistent with every other recovery entry point.

Resolves #9961

## Changes

- `src/hooks/useGitHubTokenHealth.ts` — backstop notification via `notify()` with `priority: "low"`, shared `supersedeKey`, no `correlationId`
- `src/components/Recovery/GitHubTokenBanner.tsx` — reconnect button routes through `actionService.dispatch` instead of a raw `CustomEvent`
- 17 tests updated/added: `supersedeKey` sharing and archival, inbox-only backstop (no toast, no unread count), second-cycle no-retoast regression, replay-path backstop, banner action dispatch (legacy `CustomEvent` path asserted gone)

## Testing

Targeted vitest suite (17 tests) passes. Typecheck, lint, and format clean.

body:
## Summary

Introduce `SigmaController` — a React-free class that owns the imperative Sigma layer (the instance, graph handle, and interaction state the once-registered reducers read) behind a typed, unit-testable API. The ~460-line GraphView mount effect collapses into `controller.mount(container, graph, callbacks)`; GraphView becomes a composition root. **Behavior-preserving** — reducers, interactions, and rendering are unchanged, just relocated.

## Linked spec / issue

OpenSpec change at `openspec/changes/sigma-controller/` (gitignored — full description on the issue).

- Spec: openspec/changes/sigma-controller/
- Closes: #152

## Slice classification

- [ ] `feat`
- [ ] `fix`
- [x] `refactor` — internal change, no behavior delta
- [ ] `test`
- [ ] `docs`
- [ ] `chore`
- [ ] `perf`

## Affected surfaces

- [ ] `packages/core`
- [x] `packages/extension` (VS Code host)
- [x] `packages/extension/src/webview` (React webview)
- [ ] `packages/alfred`
- [ ] `packages/exporters`
- [ ] `packages/mcp`
- [ ] `packages/cli`
- [ ] `packages/web`
- [ ] Build / CI / tooling

## What this delivers (strangler migration, 5 commits)

Built incrementally with the webview suite green at every step:

1. **Camera ops** — `zoomIn/Out/Fit/Reset` onto the controller.
2. **Hover + selection** — neighbourhood state + overlay-push; React stays authoritative for the Inspector, the controller owns the render mirror.
3. **Trace** — phase machine + path sets (`setTracePhase` eager for click routing, `setTracePath` for the React sync).
4. **Reducers** — node/edge reducers as bound fields handed to `new Sigma()`, reading the store + controller fields; `applyTheme` returns its colors for the controller to capture.
5. **Mount/layout/cleanup** — ForceAtlas2, Sigma construction, observers, listeners, afterRender, teardown all in `mount`/`dispose`; React glue passed as a typed `SigmaMountCallbacks` bag.

**GraphView.tsx: 2,051 → 1,654 LOC (−19%); 22 → 9 `useRef`s.** Zero imperative *view-state* refs remain (survivors are DOM-element/handle/toggle refs). Also removed the write-only `lastClickRef` (dead even before this change).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean (both tsconfigs)
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 3/3 packages, `--max-warnings=0`, zero warnings
- [x] `pnpm test` (from `packages/extension`) — **597 passed** (48 files): the 559 prior tests unchanged + **38 new direct `SigmaController` unit tests** (lifecycle, camera math, hover/selection, trace, every reducer branch, mount/dispose). Zero regressions.
- [x] `gitnexus detect_changes` — affected flows are exactly the GraphView/SigmaController render+interaction processes; no unexpected reach. Risk "high" reflects GraphView being the render root (pre-existing), not new fan-out.
- [ ] **Manual QA in a running VS Code extension** — NOT doable headlessly; needs a human to load the build and confirm mount, filters, lenses, depth, hover/selection, trace, zoom, layout presets, and hull toggle all behave exactly as before. The spec flags this as the required acceptance step for this spine change.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits
- [x] Branch follows `feature/slice-<N>-<short>` shape
- [x] `Closes:` references the cluster issue (#152)
- [x] `pnpm format:check` / `pnpm lint` pass (zero warnings)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm test` passes
- [ ] `pnpm build` / `pnpm package` — defer to CI
- [x] Net diff: GraphView shrinks 706 lines; the additions are the extracted controller + its tests. The controller is one cohesive unit (a class + its test); splitting it would break the behavior-preservation guarantee. Flagged per CLAUDE.md.
- [x] No edits to README/CHANGELOG/marketplace metadata
- [x] No edits to `.specify/` or `specs/NNN-*/`
- [x] No `any` introduced without justification (casts are localized `as` at the Sigma boundary, matching the prior inline code)
- [x] No native deps added to `packages/core`
- [x] No `localStorage` in webview code
- [ ] New GitHub Action `uses:` SHA pins — N/A
- [ ] Graph schema — N/A

## Notes for reviewers

- **Behavior-preservation is the bar.** Every one of the 5 commits kept the 559 prior tests green; the reducers were moved branch-for-branch (same hide/dim/emphasis rules). The two-sources-of-truth contract: React owns *display* surfaces (Inspector/banner/rails), the controller owns the *render* mirror, and the handler that sets both lives in one place.

author: singhshivesh
body:
Slice 4 of D-0016 (web-TTY UX), approved as **P-0020 → D-0017**. The interactive-studio seam from the three-seam ladder: a real provider CLI launched in a session's own workspace, streamed to the browser over a PTY, with the human typing every turn.

**Why this is the ToS-clean lane:** unlike `CLIInteractiveExecutor` (the autonomous `run_stream` loop, mode-gated to `personal` by slices 1–3), web-TTY injects no prompt and auto-sends no control commands. Batonkeep is a terminal multiplexer here, not a bot driving the CLI — a human drives each turn (D-0016 posture).

**Locality (D-0017):** the CLI runs in the user-owned session workspace (`sessions_dir`); nothing session-side is persisted Batonkeep-central.

### Backend (slice 4a)
- `app/pty_session.py` — extract the hardened PTY↔WS bridge (fd/reader cancellation race, pts-tree kill) from `console.py` into a reusable `PtySession(argv, cwd, env)`.
- `app/console.py` — `PtyAuthSession` now subclasses `PtySession` (still only ever runs `auth.sh`).
- `app/web_tty.py` — `build_web_tty_session(session, instance)` resolves a CLI instance + session workspace into a launchable session: binary only (no `-p`, no skip-permission flag — the human approves tool use in the CLI), instance config dir exported, `cwd` = workspace. Refuses managed (`plan_cli_allowed`), unknown instance, non-CLI provider, missing/unsafe workspace.
- `app/main.py` — `/ws/tty` token-gated route mirroring `/ws/console`; first frame `{token,session,instance}`, then `input`/`resize`; emits `output`/`exit`/`error`.
- `tests/test_web_tty.py` — 6 builder tests (gating + successful argv/cwd/env). **298 backend tests pass.**

### Frontend (slice 4b)
- `PtyTerminal.tsx` — reusable xterm↔ws bridge extracted from `AuthConsole` (xterm stays in one lazy chunk shared by both consoles).
- `AuthConsole.tsx` / `WebTtyConsole.tsx` — thin wrappers (`/ws/console` vs `/ws/tty`).
- `SessionView` — a `terminal` launcher by the agent switcher (shown only when the web console is available + token set + a session selected); lazy overlay drives the selected instance in the current session workspace.
- **tsc + vite build clean.**

### Gating
Rides the existing web-console gate: `ENABLE_WEB_CONSOLE` + `WEB_CONSOLE_TOKEN`, never in `managed` (`web_console_available`), plus `plan_cli_allowed`.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Live-browser validation against real CLIs (dev-container auth is limited).
- Threads 2 (artifact-centric capture) and 1 (cross-provider memory ledger) per D-0017.
- ⚠ **Concurrent-work note:** a separate branch `agent/claude/d0016-grok-headless-fix` (commit `00328a9`) asserts grok *does* have first-party headless mode and empties the no-headless set. If correct, it moots the D-0017 carry-in about "grok-only scheduled tasks can't be validated." This PR is orthogonal (web-TTY) and branches off the PR #18 merge, not that fix — flagging for reconciliation.

author: vibecoderst
body:
## Summary

The TypeScript suite reimplemented the dashboard's projection/scoring algorithms
as test-local `Mock*` classes and asserted on the copy — tautologies that stayed
green even if the production `GRQValidator` in `docs/app.js` drifted or broke. One
test in `tests/trend_line_extension_test.ts` even **overrode**
`calculateHybridProjectionData` inline and then asserted on the output of that very
function; `tests/integration_test.ts` recomputed formulas inline and asserted on its
own arithmetic (`20.0 ≈ 20.0`, `22.0`).

This change applies resolution **(a)** from the issue (extract the maths into a
module both `docs/app.js` and the tests import) for the core projection/scoring
kernels, and resolution **(b)** (delete the named tautologies) for the inline
method-override and inline-arithmetic steps:

- **New shared module `docs/projection.js`** — a classic-script module published on
  `globalThis` (mirroring `docs/escape.js`), with no module syntax, importable by
  both the browser dashboard and the Deno tests. It exports `setDateToMidnight`,
  `getDaysElapsed`, `calculatePerformanceReturn`, and `buildHybridProjectionData`.
- **`GRQValidator` now delegates** `getDaysElapsed`, the performance-return maths in
  `calculateStockPerformance`, and the hybrid trend-shape generation in
  `calculateHybridProjectionData` to the shared module, so production and tests
  exercise one implementation (no parallel copy to drift).
- **`docs/index.html`** loads `projection.js` before `app.js`, next to `escape.js`.
- **Tests rewritten to drive the real code** — the projection-data tests and the
  integration performance step now import `docs/projection.js` and assert on the
  shipped functions' observable output. A bug in the production trend-shape
  generation now fails these tests.

The remaining mock-validator test files (`realistic_projection_test.ts`,
`chart_data_test.ts`, `basic_score_table_test.ts`, `buy_price_logic_test.ts`,
`current_price_consistency_test.ts`, `hybrid_projection_tests.ts`,
`judgement_hybrid_test.ts`, `portfolio_view_consistency_test.ts`,
`schw_projection_test.ts`) depend on still-stateful logic (`getBuyPrice`,
`calculateTrendLine`, `calculateHybridProjection`, the dilution variants) whose
extraction touches DOM/market-data code paths that cannot be exercised headlessly.
Converting them is larger and riskier than this scope, so it is tracked as
follow-up issue **stSoftwareAU/GRQ-validation#100**.

Closes #80.

## Evidence

This is a test-architecture / CLI change with no visual UI change, so no screenshot
applies. The fix is verified by the rewritten tests, which now exercise the real
shipped code path instead of a local mock:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Before
        T1[TS test] --> M[local Mock* copy]
        A1[docs/app.js GRQValidator] -. never imported .-> T1
    end
    subgraph After
        T2[TS test] --> P[docs/projection.js]
        A2[docs/app.js GRQValidator] --> P
    end
```

The shared module is the single source of truth: `GRQValidator` and the tests both
call into `docs/projection.js`, so a regression in the production maths now breaks
the suite.

## Test Plan

- **`tests/projection_module_test.ts`** (new) — 12 behavioural tests importing the
  real `docs/projection.js`: `getDaysElapsed`, `calculatePerformanceReturn`
  (happy/loss/invalid-buy-price), `setDateToMidnight` (no input mutation), and
  `buildHybridProjectionData` for the `target_based`, `dampened_trend` (incl. no
  trend line) and `realistic_trajectory` methods plus the -100% floor.
- **`tests/trend_line_extension_test.ts`** — projection-data tests now call the real
  `buildHybridProjectionData`; the inline `calculateHybridProjectionData` override
  and the `Mock*` reimplementations were removed. The `calculateTrendLine`
  regression test is retained (that function is extracted in #100).
- **`tests/integration_test.ts`** — the performance step now calls the real
  `calculatePerformanceReturn`; the `20.0 ≈ 20.0` tautology was removed.
- Full Deno suite: `deno test --allow-read tests/*.ts` → **144 passed, 0 failed**.
- `deno fmt`, `deno lint`, `deno check` all clean; `cargo check --all-targets` clean
  (no Rust files changed).

author: eeiaao
body:
## What

Makes VenueType drive behavior instead of being a stored-but-unread label.

- New venue_behavior.h: isDex, and a venueBehavior table that maps a venue type to two flags. usesOrderBook chooses between central-limit-order-book matching with book pricing and AMM reserve pricing. onChainSettlement chooses between the synchronous CEX order lifecycle and the probabilistic on-chain one (pending, reverted, gas-replaced). A centralized exchange uses a book and settles off-chain; an AMM DEX uses neither a book nor off-chain settlement; a hybrid uses a book and settles on-chain.
- SymbolRegistry gains venueTypeForSymbol, which resolves a symbol to its exchange's venue type and defaults to a centralized exchange when the symbol or exchange is unknown.

## Why

The DEX pieces have landed: AMM reserve pricing, the on-chain order lifecycle, and the nonlinear position valuation hook. Nothing yet selected between them per venue. The behavior table is that switch. Routing code reads the two flags rather than branching on the enum in each place, so a new venue type is described once and every routing decision picks it up. An executor or connector that holds a symbol but not its exchange asks venueTypeForSymbol and then reads the flags. Design notes: docs/explanation/venue-types.md.

## Tests

New tests/test_venue_behavior.cpp, 3 cases: isDex classification, the behavior table for all three venue types, and venueTypeForSymbol resolving a registered AMM symbol to AmmDex with an unknown symbol defaulting to CentralizedExchange. Full suite is 115/115.

## MCP impact

None beyond a bundled-data refresh. The new explanation page re-syncs docs.fts.sqlite. The additions are header and registry C++ with no binding surface, so parity, stubs, and the API index are unchanged. No new MCP tools, no live-engine tool changes, no IDL group added.

Adds the `abort_migration(namespace_id)` PyO3 binding, wrapping
`POST admin-api/groups/{namespace_id}/migration/abort` (calimero-client
`abort_migration`, landed in calimero-network/core#2681).

Logically aborts an in-flight namespace migration: flips the group's pending

body: ## Summary - Adds a metadata-only Step Functions state-machine role collector using `states:ListStateMachines`, `states:DescribeStateMachine`, and `states:ListTagsForResource`. - Normalizes Step Functions workflows into AWS identity/workload/resource graph records with `runs_as` relationships to execution roles. - Exposes fixture-backed API and app inventory for success, empty, degraded, partial-failure, and permission-denied states. - Documents permissions, limitations, OpenAPI contract, and the safety boundary that raw definitions, execution history, payload examples, object contents, and secret values are not collected. ## Validation - `go test ./internal/providers/aws ./internal/api ./internal/runtime ./internal/cli` - `go test ./...` - `npm test -- --run productShell.test.tsx api/client.test.ts` from `web/` - `npm run build` from `web/` - `git diff --check` ## AI disclosure No Closes #1483 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds metadata-only inventory for AWS Step Functions state machines and their execution roles to map workflows to IAM roles while keeping definitions private. Restricts collected definition ARNs to allowed integrations and nested workflows, drops payload ARNs, reports target AWS SDK services, and improves retry handling for `DescribeStateMachine` (addresses #1483). - **New Features** - Added `StepFunctionsStateMachineRoleCollector` using `states:ListStateMachines`, `states:DescribeStateMachine`, and `states:ListTagsForResource`; stores a SHA-256 of definitions and preserves role/state-machine metadata when definitions are encrypted or unavailable. - Normalization: emits state-machine resources and workloads, links `runs_as` to execution roles, captures task resources, nested workflows, and logging config; supports partition-aware service integrations; allowlists definition ARNs and strips payload/data-plane ARNs; reports AWS SDK target services. - New API: GET `/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects/{project_id}/aws/stepfunctions-state-machine-roles` with `connector_id` and `fixture_state` (`success|empty|degraded|partial_failure|permission_denied`); wired into router/authz, CLI, runtime; OpenAPI, docs, web client types, and a regression test to guard against reintroducing AWS section copy redundancy (via Vite `?raw` import) are included. - **Bug Fixes** - Propagate retryable `DescribeStateMachine` errors from `ListServiceRoles` to the page retry policy (e.g., `ThrottlingException`, `KMSThrottlingException`, `RequestLimitExceeded`, 5xx/timeouts) with ARN context; only emit `state_machine_describe_failed` for non-retryable errors (e.g., `ValidationException`); do not fall back to metadata on retryable failures. ## Summary

- The `check-preload-backdoors` security gate was only scanning `preload.cjs`, leaving main-process bundles (`main.js`, host entries, split chunks) unchecked for E2E backdoor leakage.
- Closes three list divergences: `DAINTREE_E2E_SIDELOAD_PLUGIN_DIR` was stripped by esbuild but missing from `FORBIDDEN`; `DISABLE_CACHED_VIEW_CPU_THROTTLE`, `CRASH_DUMPS_DIR`, and `DEFER_RENDERER_LOAD` were neither stripped nor checked.
- Extracts `scanBundleForForbidden`, `collectMainBundles`, and `runGate` as testable exports and adds `check-preload-backdoors.test.mjs` with a policy-sync cross-check that parses `build-main.mjs` define keys against `STRIPPED_BY_BUILD`, so list drift is caught automatically in future.

Resolves #10026

## Changes

- `scripts/ci/check-preload-backdoors.mjs` — glob-scans `dist-electron/electron/**/*.{js,cjs}` in addition to `preload.cjs`; all four missing env vars added to `FORBIDDEN` and `STRIPPED_BY_BUILD`; `shouldDeferRendererLoadForE2E` rewritten to read `process.env` directly (zero-arg) so esbuild's define rewrite fires; gate logic extracted into named, exported functions.
- `scripts/build-main.mjs` — `DISABLE_CACHED_VIEW_CPU_THROTTLE`, `CRASH_DUMPS_DIR`, and `DEFER_RENDERER_LOAD` added to the esbuild `define` strip block.

- `scripts/ci/check-preload-backdoors.test.mjs` — 14 unit tests covering bundle scanning, gate logic, and the policy-sync cross-check.

- `npm run check` passes clean (typecheck, lint, format, all CI guards).

- Policy-sync test parses `build-main.mjs` at runtime and fails if `STRIPPED_BY_BUILD` drifts from the esbuild define block.
