author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

Laravel was falling back to SQLite because `config/database.php` defaulted to `sqlite` when `DB_CONNECTION` was not read correctly, causing the "Database file at path /app/database/database.sqlite does not exist" error on Railway. Similarly, `config/cache.php`, `config/session.php`, and `config/queue.php` all defaulted to `database`-backed drivers, which require a `cache`, `sessions`, and `jobs` table to exist before migrations have run — creating a chicken-and-egg failure on first deploy.

## Solution

Changed the hardcoded fallback in `config/database.php` to `pgsql`, so even if `DB_CONNECTION` is somehow unset, Laravel targets PostgreSQL rather than SQLite. Updated `config/cache.php` and `config/session.php` to default to `file`, and `config/queue.php` to default to `sync` — all zero-dependency drivers that work immediately without extra tables or services. Removed all `sqlite` references from `queue.php`'s batching and failed-job config, updated `.env.example` to reflect production-safe PostgreSQL and file-driver defaults, removed the SQLite `touch` command from `composer.json`'s `post-create-project-cmd`, and committed `.gitkeep` files for all required `storage/framework/` subdirectories so Laravel's compiled-views, cache, and session paths exist in the container from the start.

### Changes
- **Modified** `mirleft-backend/config/database.php`
- **Modified** `mirleft-backend/config/queue.php`
- **Modified** `mirleft-backend/config/cache.php`
- **Modified** `mirleft-backend/config/session.php`

- **Created** `mirleft-backend/storage/logs/.gitkeep`

- **Created** `mirleft-backend/storage/framework/views/.gitkeep`

author: alextitanium
body:
## Why

`serve()` ran the **full production build on every save** — ~22s for 172 pages, with zero dev/prod distinction. This makes the dev loop fast (a single content/CSS edit rebuilds in ~1–2s) while keeping the **production build path byte-identical**: every dev behavior is gated behind a `build.run()` option that only `serve()` passes.

A workflow first mapped the real bottlenecks (and busted a few myths): the dominant costs are the **172 synchronous `renderToString` calls** (batch=2) and **`content.loadAll` re-running Shiki on all Markdown every save** — *not* OG images (off by default) and *not* something a bigger render batch fixes (`renderToString` is synchronous; `Promise.all` doesn't parallelize it). So the wins are: skip waste, and **redo only what changed**.

## What

### ① Dev build profile *(small, safe)*
- `build.run()` options widened to `{ outDir?, skipClean?, overrides?, changed? }` (`RunOptions`). `runPipeline` guards `rm -rf outDir` behind `!skipClean` and merges per-run `overrides` into the config clone — **the persisted config is never mutated**.
- `bundle` runs its two `Bun.build` passes **concurrently** (`Promise.all`, CSS dispatched first — keeps the segfault-dodging split; also speeds prod).
- `serve()` applies a dev profile (no minify + feeds/sitemap/og/locale-redirects off) and **skips the clean on rebuilds** → caches/assets survive, no mid-rebuild 404 flash. `ServeOptions { og, sitemap, feeds, localeRedirects }` re-enable any output for a session (a thin consumer script maps `--og` etc.).

### ② Granular incremental rebuild *(the real "instant" win)*
- `serve` threads the **changed file path** (previously discarded) through a coalescing rebuilder into `build.run({ changed })`. `planIncrementalRebuild` classifies paths (`.md`=content, `.css`=style, code=bust, unknown=full) → a reuse plan.
- `content.loadAll({ reuse })` reuses cached articles for non-invalidated slugs — **re-reads + re-runs Shiki only for dirty Markdown** — while recomputing `contentId` ordinals across the full sorted set (order/ids match a full load).
- A cross-run **render cache** (`name␞params␞locale → {dataHash, body}`) skips `renderToString` for any page whose **loaded data is unchanged**, and busts wholesale on a code change / full build. Correct by construction (no dependency graph): an index page's card data changes when an article changes, so it re-renders; untouched pages reuse.

### ③ No-op save drop *(small, safe — the double-Ctrl+S habit)*
- `createChangeGate` gains an optional `fileHash` seam + a committed-hash baseline; a save whose **bytes equal the last successfully-built version** is dropped. `commitBuilt(changed)` baselines **only the paths the just-succeeded build consumed**, so a failed build baselines nothing (retry always rebuilds) and a file edited mid-build is never falsely baselined by another file's success.

## Expected impact

| edit | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| single content (`.md`) | ~22s | **~1–2s** (re-highlight 1 article + re-render affected pages) |
| CSS | ~22s | **~1–2s** (rebundle CSS, cached bodies, reload) |
| code (`.ts/.tsx`) | ~22s | full re-render (safe) — content + bundle still skip waste |
| byte-identical re-save | ~22s | **~0s** (dropped) |
| `bun run build` | baseline | slightly faster (concurrent bundle); **output byte-identical** |

## Tradeoffs (dev-only, documented in JSDoc)
- `skipClean` means a **deleted/renamed** slug's stale page lingers until a restart or production `build`.
- Render reuse assumes a route's render output is a pure function of its `.load()` data (+ params/locale/code) — documented on `RunOptions.changed`. Production omits `changed`, so it's never affected.

## Tests & verification
- **+80 tests** (752 → 755 via vitest): pipeline classifier; content reuse + ordinal-renumber-on-reorder; render-cache hit/miss/per-key-isolation/non-serializable; gate no-op-drop + commit-scoping regression; dev-profile + opt-in wiring; a *discriminating* incremental integration test (mutates the render input so a stale cache fails the test).
- Green: `tsc`, `biome` + `eslint`, `build` (tsdown), `check:bundle` (browser bundle node-free + under budget — the new `node:crypto` use is node-only), coverage (94% stmts / 88% branch / 95% lines, gate 85%).
- An adversarial review workflow (correctness + conventions + test-quality, each finding verified) ran on the diff; its one confirmed correctness bug (`commitBuilt` promoting the whole pending map) and the test-efficacy gaps are fixed in this PR.

## Description

When a custom `PropertyNamingStrategy` (e.g. `SNAKE_CASE`) is configured on the mapper, `ModelResolver` produced **inconsistent** schema property names: most fields were translated, but any property whose member name starts with a `get`/`is` prefix followed by a lower-case letter kept its original camelCase name.

Example (`SNAKE_CASE`, Java record):

```java
public record PidLookupResponse(
    String familyName, String expiryDate,
    String issuanceDate, String issuingCountry, String issuingAuthority) {}
```

Produced:

```
family_name, expiry_date, issuanceDate, issuingCountry, issuingAuthority
```

instead of the expected `issuance_date`, `issuing_country`, `issuing_authority`.

### Root cause

The "avoid clobbering properties with get/is names" hack (added for #415) overwrites the Jackson-resolved property name with the **raw member name** whenever the member name starts with `get`/`is` + lower-case. For record components the accessor's physical name is the bare component name (`issuanceDate`), which starts with `is`, so the hack replaced the strategy-translated `issuance_date` with `issuanceDate`.

### Fix

Only apply the hack when **no** `PropertyNamingStrategy` is configured. When a strategy is active the resolved name is authoritative and must be honored uniformly. The hack was only ever needed to restore raw names in the absence of a strategy:
- **#415** (Scala accessor `is_persistent` wrongly shortened to `_persistent`) — default mapper, no strategy → hack still runs.
- **#2635** (JAXB-renamed `is`-prefixed fields keeping their original name) — JAXB mapper, no strategy → hack still runs.

Both existing test cases continue to pass.

This bug surfaces through springdoc and was traced to swagger-core: springdoc/springdoc-openapi#3293.

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] 🧪 Tests

- [x] I have added/updated tests as needed

## Test evidence

Added `RecordPropertyNamingStrategyTest` (in `swagger-java17-support`, which compiles at Java 17 for records). It fails on `master` (`issuanceDate` not translated) and passes with this change.

Verification done: reproduced on `master`; ran the full test suites for `swagger-core`, `swagger-jaxrs2` (incl. `ReaderTest#testModelResolverXMLPropertiesName` for #2635) and `swagger-java17-support` — all green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced `+=` array concatenation inside loops with direct pipeline assignment in `AzureStealth.ps1`. Removed redundant array accumulation for `Out-GridView`. Added performance explanation comments.

🎯 **Why:** In PowerShell, arrays are immutable. Using `+=` creates a completely new copy of the array on every iteration. For large dictionaries like `$entityDict`, this creates a severe $O(N^2)$ performance bottleneck and excessive memory allocation overhead.

📊 **Impact:** Converts the $O(N^2)$ array building process to $O(N)$. For large Azure AD environments (thousands of users/tenants), this will drastically reduce the time it takes to generate the final CSV reports. Memory usage will also be significantly more efficient.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verify by running the script against an Azure environment with a large number of users (`pwsh -c '. ./AzureStealth/AzureStealth.ps1'`). Measure execution time before and after the change; the report generation phase will be noticeably faster.

author: haroonbuilds
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a critical security/logical bug in the `loginService` flow inside `src/services/auth.service.ts`. 

Previously, the system was checking the account's verification status (`if (user.isVerified === false)`) BEFORE checking if the entered password was valid or not. Because of this incorrect sequence, if an unverified user entered a completely wrong/random password, the server ignored the password completely and threw an unverified exception, which mistakenly redirected them to the OTP state and triggered an email.

**What changed:**
- Reordered the execution flow inside `loginService`. Now, the server first validates the password using `user.comparePassword(password)`. If the password is invalid, it throws an `UnauthorizedException("Invalid email/password")` immediately.
- The `isVerified` check is now performed only after the password has been successfully verified.
- This prevents resource exhaustion attacks (malicious actors repeatedly triggering OTP emails for unverified users without knowing their password).

## Related issues

- Closes #124
- Related to #117 (Different issue but discussed alongside this flow)

## How to test

1. Create a new account but do not verify the email (leave `isVerified: false` in the database).
2. Send a POST request to the login endpoint (`/api/auth/login`) with the unverified email but use a completely WRONG password.
3. **Verify:** The server should now throw an `UnauthorizedException` for invalid credentials. It should NOT trigger any OTP email or proceed to the OTP redirection state.
4. Try again with the CORRECT password for that unverified account.
5. **Verify:** The server should now successfully catch that the password is correct but the account is unverified, throwing the expected email verification error and safely initiating the OTP flow.

Bu PR `flux-agent.md` token sarfini optimize qilishdan boshlanib, dogfooding orqali topilgan runtime semantika muammosini ham hal qiladi. 3 mantiqiy commit.

## 1. Runtime: `=` bind scope semantikasi (asosiy)

**Muammo:** `if`/`each`/`match` blok ichida `=` har doim joriy scope'da yangi local yaratardi. `total = total + x` kabi accumulator pattern tashqi o'zgaruvchini o'zgartirmay, **jim** nil/eski qiymat qoldirardi — agent "ishladi" deb o'ylab noto'g'ri natija olardi.

**Yechim:**
- `if`/`each`/`match` bloklari leksik **shaffof** — ichidagi `=` joriy funksiya ichidagi tashqi o'zgaruvchini yangilaydi (boshqa tillar kabi).
- `fn`/lambda — **izolyatsiya chegarasi**: ichida `=` yangi local (shadowing).
- **Immutability saqlanadi**: tashqi `=` (immutable) ni blok ichidan ham qayta tayinlab bo'lmaydi → aniq xato.
- `<-` (assign) avvalgidek fn chegarasidan o'tib closure capture qiladi.

Texnik: `Scope`'ga `is_fn_boundary` flag, `=` uchun yangi `Interp::bind` metodi. 4 yangi test.

author: jav974
body:
## What

Two features that were hiding under the word "delayed":

### `{ delayed: N }` — deferred run (fresh read)

Run a callback exactly N ms after the **first** fire of a burst, reading live state at run time. It's exact sugar for `{ debounce: N, maxWait: N }` — a combination that already did this but was undiscoverable as an idiom. Now a first-class 5th timing strategy, available on every hook/API that accepts `TimingOptions` (effect, render, memo, watch, store, persist, broadcast).

```ts
useRefSignalEffect(fn, [sig], { delayed: 100 }); // fires once, 100ms after the burst starts
```

### `createReplayRefSignal` / `useReplayRefSignal` — time-shifted value (replay)

A read-only signal that follows its source exactly N ms behind, retracing every update in order — trails, ghosts, delayed playback.

```tsx
const pos = useRefSignal({ x: 0, y: 0 });
const ghost = useReplayRefSignal(pos, 300, (p) => ({ ...p }));

// exactly the live-source effect, pointed at a different timeline
useRefSignalEffect(() => drawGhost(ctx, ghost.current.x, ghost.current.y), [ghost], { frame: true });
```

- **Drain**: one armed `setTimeout` for the head entry's due time — emissions fire at the due moment (not frame-quantized), no timer while the source is quiet, no rAF dependency (node/SSR-safe, keeps progressing in background tabs). Intentionally not configurable: any drain policy would corrupt the "value as it was N ms ago" contract; consumption timing belongs downstream, per consumer.
- **`snapshot` param** (default identity): required for object signals mutated in place (`.current.x = …; .notify()`) — without it the queue holds references to one live object and every emission shows the present. Immutable updates and primitives need nothing.
- **Layering**: framework-agnostic `attachReplay(source, target, ms, snapshot) → detach` engine (mirrors `attachSignalBroadcast`), composed by the `create*` form and attached in a `useEffect` by the hook — so the replay survives StrictMode mount cycles while the returned signal stays stable.

### Why two features, not one option

The timing layer shifts *when* a callback runs — the callback still reads live state. `delayed` = "the present, late". A replay shifts *what you see* = "the past, on time"; that requires value capture, which is only well-defined signal→signal (a `replay:` timing option on `useRefSignalRender` would be unimplementable — the component body reads `.current`). Docs cross-link the two at every touchpoint, including the classic trap called out in patterns.md: reaching for delay to build a trail makes the ghost teleport onto the node.

## Also

- Fixed `useWatchArgs` silently dropping timing keys missing from its rebuild whitelist — `{ delayed }` reached `watch()` but not the React hooks until added there.

## Tests

20 new tests (711 total): due-time precision, emit order, snapshot footgun both directions, idle-drain (`jest.getTimerCount()` asserts zero timers while quiet / one during a burst), dispose, feedback-loop re-entrancy, StrictMode re-attach + no-double-subscription, and `@ts-expect-error` type-level exclusivity (`{ delayed: 100, frame: true }` is a compile error).

`tsc` ✓ · `eslint` ✓ · 711/711 ✓ · `tsup` build ✓ · bundle 4.12 kB within size-limit ✓

body: ## Summary Phase 8 completes full OpenCascade (OCCT) WASM kernel integration for Vertex insole CAD, routing production geometry through the existing `IGeometryKernel` abstraction while preserving the Phase 7 worker preview pipeline as a safety net. ## Architecture ``` Viewer (interacting) → geometry worker (procedural preview, 48×24) Viewer (idle) + OCCT → getKernel().buildInsole() on main thread (rAF-scheduled) Exports / custom GLB → getKernel().buildInsole() (OCCT when loaded) Validation → geometryEngine.validateProductionSolid() (OCCT isClosed + mesh edges) Fallback → ThreeKernel procedural everywhere if WASM fails ``` ## Key changes - **`kernel-build.ts`**: canonical `insoleParamsFromDesign()`, OCCT detection, rAF scheduling, production build helpers - **`geometry-engine.ts`**: `preferKernel` option + `validateProductionSolid()` for OCCT topology checks - **`occt-insole.ts`**: shell printing via `makeThickSolidByJoin` + boolean hollow fallback; clone-before-offset to protect source BRep - **`kernel.ts` / `kernel-store.ts`**: load state tracking (`idle|loading|ready|failed`) - **Flows updated**: `useInsoleGeometry`, `ExportPanel`, `export-service`, `custom-library-service`, `PrintingPanel`, `StatusBar` - **`useSolidValidation`**: debounced OCCT-aware watertight validation for export UI - **Build scripts**: `vertex/package.json` delegates `setup:wasm` / `build:wasm` to repo root - **WASM test**: shell printing mode integration test (`npm run test:wasm`) ## Validation - `npm run test:wasm -- packages/wasm/test/vertex-insole.wasm.test.ts` — 3/3 passed - `vertex npm run typecheck` — pass - `vertex npm run build` — pass (OCCT WASM bundled ~15.9 MB) ## Notes - Custom GLB elements remain excluded from OCCT boolean pipeline (rendered separately) - OCCT idle builds run synchronously on the main thread; complex designs may briefly stall - Skive boolean refinement may leave open BRep; lofted skives + repair remain the primary path

## Skill Improvement ($50-150 Bounty)

### Skill Modified

**Skill path:** `skills/secops/log-analysis/`

### What Was Wrong

The skill asks analysts to define a time window and reconstruct timelines, but it did not require a timestamp trust check before cross-source correlation. That can make SIEM timelines look definitive even when Windows/Sysmon, Linux syslog, CloudTrail, Elastic, Splunk, and collector metadata disagree because of local time, missing year/timezone fields, parser choices, ingestion lag, queue backlog, or host clock skew.

Fixes #1422.

### What This PR Fixes

- Adds `Step 0: Timestamp Normalization and Clock-Skew Gate` before log source taxonomy and correlation.

author: devbrian
body:
## Summary

Comix searches/downloads only ever saw the **~20 chapters the series page renders on first paint** — which are mostly the *newest* chapter's group-uploads (each chapter number has ~12 group rows). So low chapters (e.g. chapter 5 of "The Forgotten Field") were never enumerated, and a chapter search for them returned nothing (#146). Root cause: `solver.fetch_via_browser` is a **one-shot** primitive (goto → wait → evaluate → close) — it can't rewrite the request limit or click pagination.

This makes comix chapter enumeration **always walk the full paginated list**, for every search AND the deferred download resolution.

## What changed

- **New generic, source-agnostic solver primitive** `CloudflareSolver.fetch_via_browser_paginated(url, *, extract, wait_for, next_selector, route_limit_rewrite=None, max_pages=200, timeout=30)` (`framework/antibot.py`):
  - Installs a Patchright `page.route()` handler **before goto** that rewrites a `limit=\d+` query param to a fixed value on requests whose URL matches a caller-supplied substring.
  - Walks pagination **in-page within ONE page lifecycle / ONE `_browser_lock` acquisition**: run `extract`, accumulate rows deduped by `id`, JS-click `next_selector` (bypasses an invisible overlay that defeats Playwright's physical-click actionability), bounded poll until the rendered row set changes; stop on absent/disabled Next, no-new-rows, or `max_pages` (warn guard).
  - Reuses the dead-driver recycle wrapper via a new shared `_goto_and_wait`; the one-shot `_fetch_via_browser_once` is byte-for-byte unchanged.
  - **Stays source-agnostic** (grep-gated in CI): the `/chapters` substring, `100` limit, and `button[aria-label*="Next"]` selector are all passed in from `comix.py`.
- **`comix._series_chapters`** always-walks via the primitive regardless of search type. The desc sort, the 260606-2ff `chapter_matches` result-filter, and the `[offset:offset+feed_limit]` slice are **unchanged** — type=chapter still filters correctly on top of the now-complete list. `_solver_from_ctx` requires both primitives.
- Both the search fan-out and the deferred `fetch_manifest` (`DEFERRED` branch) get the full list; `_resolve_deferred` strict-match verified against the larger list.

## Why this design (proven live in spikes 010/011, PR #148)

Patchright (the gateway's only engine) **suppresses every JS-injection avenue** — `context`/`page` `add_init_script` AND raw CDP `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` — so the keiyoushi `JSON.parse`+`limit→100` proxy is impossible here. `page.route()` is the only lever, and it works: the `_=` request token does **not** bind `limit` (rewrite → 200, not 403), and the server caps `limit` at 100 (`300+` → 422).

## Tests
- Unit test for the primitive's accumulate/dedup/stop-conditions loop (absent-next, no-new-rows, max_pages).
- #146 regression: a low chapter (#5) that appears only on the last page is enumerated.
- No-monkeypatch deferred-path test exercises the real always-walk + `_resolve_deferred`.
- Fake solvers across `test_comix_{slice,search_parallel,recent,download_parallel}.py` extended with `fetch_via_browser_paginated`.
- Full gate green: ruff + ruff format + mypy strict + **pytest 771 passed**.

## Perf (accepted, user direction 2026-06-06)
Always-walk adds a handful of in-page "Next" clicks per comix series — all **within ONE navigation**, so no extra goto/Cloudflare cost; bounded by the 30s timeout and `max_pages=200`.

## Scope
Browser path only. The pure-no-browser path (mint `_=` token + decrypt the `{"e":…}` response) stays in **#147**.

Closes #146

author: edenreich
body:
## Problem

Commits produced by the action carried a malformed identity. The clearest symptom is [`inference-gateway/python-sdk@c2ea888`](https://github.com/inference-gateway/python-sdk/commit/c2ea8889944ec50f4f1eb75aef55e9db875211f2), whose `Co-authored-by:` trailer is a GitHub API **403 JSON** repeated three times:

```
Co-authored-by: {"message":"Resource not accessible by integration",...,"status":"403"} <{...}+{...}@users.noreply.github.com>
```

## Root cause

The `Configure Git` step resolved the bot identity with `gh api /user`:

```bash
BOT_LOGIN=$(gh api /user --jq '.login' 2>/dev/null || true)
BOT_ID=$(gh api /user --jq '.id'   2>/dev/null || true)
```

- `GET /user` ("the authenticated user") is **not accessible to a GitHub App installation token** — exactly the token this action receives — so it returns `403 Resource not accessible by integration`.
- On an HTTP error, `gh api` **skips `--jq` and prints the raw error body to stdout**; `2>/dev/null` only hid the stderr line. So `BOT_LOGIN`/`BOT_ID` captured the whole 403 JSON.
- The JSON is non-empty, so the `-z` check passed and the `github-actions[bot]` fallback was **skipped**.
- `git config user.name/user.email` were set to the JSON. The pre-squash branch commit ([`python-sdk` PR #34 → `ade4a8d`](https://github.com/inference-gateway/python-sdk/pull/34/commits)) was authored/committed by that JSON identity, and GitHub's squash-merge then surfaced it as the malformed `Co-authored-by:` trailer.

## Fix

- Add a `github-app-slug` input.
- Resolve the numeric id via **`GET /users/{slug}[bot]`** (which *does* work with App installation tokens — this is the same pattern already used in `inference-gateway/.github`'s `release.yml`).
- **Validate the id is all digits** before writing the git identity — so an error body can never leak again.
- Fall back to `github-actions[bot]` / `41898282` when the slug is absent or the lookup fails.
- `set -euo pipefail` for safety.

## Backward compatibility / cross-repo impact

`infer-action` is consumed org-wide via the reusable `.github/workflows/infer.yml`. This change is **backward compatible**: callers that don't pass `github-app-slug` get the safe `github-actions[bot]` fallback (never the JSON). To restore correct `infer-bot[bot]` attribution, the reusable `infer.yml` will pass `github-app-slug: ${{ steps.app_token.outputs.app-slug }}` (separate follow-up PR, to be merged after this releases and the pin is bumped).

## Test plan

Ran the exact resolution block under `set -euo pipefail`:

| Case | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real app | `APP_SLUG=infer-bot` | `infer-bot[bot]` / `246577062+infer-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` ✅ |
| No slug | `APP_SLUG=""` | `github-actions[bot]` / `41898282` (fallback) ✅ |
| Forced 403 (JSON on stdout) | `APP_SLUG=infer-bot` | fallback — **no JSON leak** ✅ |
| Unknown app (404) | bogus slug | fallback ✅ |

`gh api "/users/infer-bot[bot]" --jq .id` → `246577062`.

author: matas-offpixel
body:
## Problem

Dropbox rejects `list_folder` with `recursive=true` when a `shared_link` parameter is set:

> "Recursive list folder is not supported for shared link."

Joe organizes files inside V1/V2 subfolders, not in the shared folder root. The previous implementation listed only the root, found zero files, and raised `empty_folder` errors — causing Bournemouth, Newcastle, and Brighton queue rows to fail.

## Fix

Walk subfolders client-side. A new internal `listFolderRecursive()` helper:

1. Lists one path within the shared folder (with pagination via `/continue`)
2. Collects file entries and subfolder paths from the response
3. Recurses **sequentially** into each subfolder (no parallel calls — preserves rate-limit safety)
4. Preserves `path_lower` exactly as Dropbox returns it (required for `get_shared_link_file` compatibility)
5. Caps depth at 5 levels — throws `DropboxFetchError("network", "nesting exceeds 5 levels")` on excess

No version-pick heuristics — all subfolders, all files.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `lib/clients/asset-queue/dropbox.ts` | New `listFolderRecursive()` + `parseEntries()` (replaces `appendFileEntries`); `listDropboxFolderFiles` delegates to recursive helper; depth cap; per-path logging |
| `lib/clients/asset-queue/__tests__/dropbox.test.ts` | 8 new/updated tests for recursive walk; mock routes by URL + request body `path`; all 13 prior tests migrated |

Not touched: `dropbox-auth.ts` (PR #579 refresh-token flow), `fetchDropboxFileContent`, `downloadDropboxFolderFiles`, `prepare/route.ts`, UI components.

## Tests

29/29 pass across both test files:

```
✔ returns root files when root contains only files (backward compatible)
✔ does NOT send recursive=true in any list_folder POST body
✔ aggregates files from V1 + V2 subfolders (multi-level fixture)
✔ returns subfolder files when root has no files (no empty_folder error)
✔ handles deep nesting: root → A → B → file.png (depth 2)
✔ throws network error when depth exceeds 5 levels
✔ paginates within a subfolder (subfolder has_more=true → continue)
✔ paginates root via /continue and recurses into subfolder on page 2
+ all 10 dropbox-auth.test.ts tests
```

## Vercel logs to expect after merge

```
[dropbox-auth] access token fetched { expiresAt: "..." }
[dropbox] list_folder { path: "/", files: 0, subfolders: 2, depth: 0 }
[dropbox] list_folder { path: "/V1", files: 1, subfolders: 0, depth: 1 }
[dropbox] list_folder { path: "/V2", files: 3, subfolders: 0, depth: 1 }
[dropbox] listFolderRecursive completed { totalFiles: 4 }
```

## Success criterion

Prepare succeeds on Bournemouth + Newcastle + Brighton (3 rows).

author: wpinrui
body:
Stores a real `retirementReason` on results (the news reads it instead of inventing one) and makes technical-failure attrition vary by era. Absorbs the per-year reliability item.

## Reason set
- **collision-damage** — all crashes, unified (consistency mistakes #59 + overtake collisions #60).
- **Technical failure** — a specific type picked uniformly from: engine, gearbox, hydraulics, electrical, suspension, brakes, clutch, overheating.

## Per-era reliability (research spike)
New `src/lib/sim/reliability.ts`. The per-car, per-race technical-DNF probability is a smooth function of year: exponential decay + a 2014 turbo-hybrid Gaussian bump + a small mid-2000s dip, converted to a per-lap probability (`1 − (1−pRace)^(1/laps)`, so attrition is circuit-length-independent). Replaces the old flat 0.2%/lap.

Sources for the curve: 1990s ~35–40% DNF, majority mechanical (engine+gearbox ≈ half of all failures — areppim F1 failure-cause histogram 1990–2013); 2014 turbo-hybrid debut spiked retirements to 20.8% (RaceFans); 2024 record ~91.5% finish rate, most DNFs crashes not mechanical (RaceFans 2024 reliability report).

## Calibration (measured, 3 headless seasons per era)
Combined DNFs per race (technical + collision):

| year | DNF/race | DNF% |
|---|---|---|
| 1996 | 8.1 | 37% |
| 2005 | 3.8 | 19% |
| 2014 | 4.0 | 18% (turbo spike) |
| 2024 | 2.1 | 11% |
| 2026 | 1.6 | 7% |

Busy early seasons, sparse modern — matching the issue's goal.

## Wiring
- `types.ts` — `RetirementReason = 'collision-damage' | TechnicalFailure`.
- `race.ts` — `simulateLap` gains a `year` param; per-lap technical roll + sampled failure type; crash channels store `collision-damage`; god-mode force-retire samples a technical failure.
- `race-store.ts` passes the season year; `sim-ahead.ts` is covered (drives via tickLap).
- `race-results.ts` — `crashed` keys off `collision-damage`.
- `news/engine.ts` — reads the stored reason (real failure type / crash phrase), generic fallback only for reason-less archived regen.

Opus-reviewed (approved; fixes for two stale comments + a non-finite-year guard applied). Build + `history:check` green.

Closes #61

author: manojpr-cb
body:
## What

Adds Ed25519 (EdDSA) signing support to the JWT auth path, alongside the existing ECDSA (ES256) keys.

- `generateJwt` now detects the key type and signs accordingly:
  - ECDSA keys (PEM) sign with ES256, same as before.
  - Ed25519 keys sign with EdDSA, accepted either as a PKCS#8 PEM or as the base64 raw key the CDP portal hands out (32-byte seed or 64-byte seed+pubkey). Whitespace in the base64 is tolerated.
- Ed25519 signing uses a small BouncyCastle-backed `JWSSigner`, so no new dependency is needed (nimbus would otherwise require Tink for OKP keys). EC keys are normalized through the default provider so the existing ECDSA path is unchanged.
- Nonce is now a random value instead of the epoch second (the old one repeated for tokens minted in the same second).
- Bumps the version to 0.2.2 and updates `SDK_VERSION` so the User-Agent reports the right version.

## Testing

Verified against the live API with both ECDSA and Ed25519 keys: JWT structural checks (alg, kid, sub, nbf/exp, distinct nonces, signature verifies), a malformed-secret negative case, plus real REST calls all pass.

author: soul2fade
body:
## Summary

Four fixes that close silent failure modes in the Apple Health / Health Connect integration. Two write-path correctness bugs, two read/permission visibility fixes.

- **HealthKit "may be denied" hint** — `requestHealthPermissions` used a successful `getSteps()` probe as the "reads granted" signal. HealthKit silently returns 0 for denied reads (Apple's privacy design), so we marked sync enabled and the UI showed "connected" with 0 steps forever. New return shape `{ granted, mayBeDenied? }` surfaces a Settings → Health hint when the probe returns 0.
- **`saveWorkoutToHealth` trusts the caller's window** — was back-computing `startMs = endMs - max(60s, durationMinutes*60)`, clobbering `payload.startMs` and writing overlapping samples on back-to-back sessions (which double-counted toward Apple Health Activity rings). Now uses the payload's measured window as-is, refuses zero/negative-duration writes, and the post-workout caller clamps to a 1-min minimum to keep unknown-duration workouts from tripping the new guard.
- **Structured `HealthWriteResult` from both writers** — `saveWorkoutToHealth` and `saveMindfulMinutesToHealth` now return `{ ok, reason? }` with a tagged reason union (`not_enabled` | `invalid_window` | `no_module` | `write_failed`). Call sites (`post-workout.tsx`, `breathe.tsx`) log a structured breadcrumb on real failures, filtered to exclude the expected "user didn't opt in" no-op so CatDoes Watch has signal.
- **Health Connect read errors surface as a "reconnect" hint** — `readHealthConnectSnapshot` returned null on errors, indistinguishable from "no data today". A user whose Health Connect permission was revoked saw the same blank state as a user with 0 steps logged. New `readError` field with `'permission' | 'sdk' | 'unknown'` classification (heuristic from the exception message — Health Connect doesn't expose structured codes). Insights renders a TouchableOpacity "tap to reconnect" hint when both reads return null AND `readError` is set, instead of hiding the card.

### Audit refs
Fixes all four "HealthKit/HC correctness" High items.

## Test plan
- [ ] On iOS, accept the HealthKit prompt with Steps allowed — confirm no spurious "may be denied" Alert.
- [ ] On iOS, accept the prompt with Steps denied (or on an iPhone with literally 0 steps today) — confirm the "may be denied" Alert appears pointing to Settings → Health.
- [ ] Complete two short workouts back-to-back, check the Apple Health Activity / Workouts feed — confirm two distinct, non-overlapping workout entries (previously they overlapped).
- [ ] Open Insights with HealthKit/Health Connect connected and reads working — confirm the existing data card renders normally.
- [ ] On Android, revoke MoodRx's Health Connect permission via system Settings → Health Connect → App permissions, reopen Insights — confirm the "Permission was revoked — tap to reconnect" hint appears (previously the card silently vanished). Tap → routes to Settings → toggle off/on → reconnect.
- [ ] Trigger a workout sync with HealthKit access revoked at the OS level — confirm a structured `console.warn` appears with reason `write_failed` (instead of the previous silent swallow).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` clean (verified locally).
- [ ] `npm run lint:ci` no new warnings (verified locally — same 22 pre-existing).

body:
## Implementation plan

Closes #29 (Tier-0 scope). Completes the implicit-framework-error inference for the two
signals still missing from the `ErrorResponseContributor` chain. The 422/401/429 signals
already ship (`Validation`/`Middleware`/`Throws` contributors); this PR adds:

### A. Route-model binding → 404 (Tier-0)
New `Plugins\Core\ErrorContributors\RouteModelBindingErrorContributor`, registered in
`CorePlugin`. Detects URI parameters whose action-signature type is an Eloquent `Model`
subclass (implicit binding) and emits a single `ModelNotFoundException` → 404 `ErrorDescriptor`
from the `exception_responses` map. Pure reflection over `ActionDescriptor::$uriParameters` —
no body parsing.

### B. `can:` middleware → 403 (Tier-0)
Extend `MiddlewareErrorContributor` with a `can` kind (`hasCanMiddleware()`), plus a
`'can' => ['status' => 403, 'description' => 'Forbidden', 'exception' => AuthorizationException::class]`
entry in `config/openapi.php`. `scope:` and `can:` both yield 403; the stage's
first-wins-per-status dedup emits a single 403 when both are present.

### Testing
- `tests/Unit/Core/Inference/RouteModelBindingErrorContributorTest.php` (new).
- Extend `MiddlewareErrorContributorTest.php` for `can:`.
- End-to-end `generateSpec()` assertion (group `openapi`): bound route emits 404 matching
  the standard error envelope.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry; docs update if the error-inference page lists signals.

### Deferred (follow-up)
Tier-1 body-scan from the issue — inline `validate()`→422 and `findOrFail`/`firstOrFail`→404 —
stays out per the tier-0-before-tier-1 program. Will file a follow-up issue.

- **StagesBar**（新组件）：5 个 stage chip（chapters/scenes/characters/beats/refine）。每个 chip 由 `ai_stages_applied + warnings` 推导出三态：
  - **AI**：该 stage 完整跑通 LLM
  - **规则**：该 stage 回退到规则路径（有 `[stage:xxx]` `STAGE_DEGRADED`）
  - **未启用**：用户通过 `STORY2SCRIPT_AI_LED_STAGES` 关掉，或 refine 在默认 mode 下短路

  Headline 显示 `AI · <provider>` / `规则模式` / `AI 不可用`，副标题 `N / 5 个 stage 走 AI 路径`。
- **MetricsRow** 去掉"改编路径"格（已被 StagesBar 顶替），剩 6 格干净；新增 `detection_method === "llm"` → `"LLM"` 显示映射。
- **WarningsList 拆双轨**：内容质量警告（`FEW_CHAPTERS` / `SHORT_CHAPTER` ...）保持突出展示；`STAGE_DEGRADED` 折叠到独立 `<details>` "stage 降级详情 · N 条"，默认收起。StagesBar 已在视觉层告诉用户哪些 stage 降级了，重复占位的 4-5 条警告不再淹没主面板。

### 视觉
- StagesBar chip 用三套语义颜色：AI=`mark-original`（绿）、规则=`mark-merged`（红/橘）、未启用=`ink-mute`（灰）。dot 圆点 + chip border + bg 三层呼应。
- chip 行 `-mx-1` + `py-1` 留出阴影空间。

### 响应式
- StagesBar 在 < 640px 横向滚动（`flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto`），sm 以上 `flex-wrap` 多行。
- MetricsRow `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3` 不变——窄屏两列已可读。
- 顶层 `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_1.15fr]` 在 < 1024px 自动堆叠也不变。

## 实现思路
- 抽 `deriveStageStatuses(applied, warnings)` 纯函数：从 `ai_stages_applied` 和 `[stage:<name>]` regex 反向 derive 每个 stage 终态。该函数完全可单测但本 PR 内联使用，未来拆出来加 unit 时直接 export 即可。
- StagesBar 复用 PR #38 的"防御读"模式（`Array.isArray + ?? null`），老 sessionStorage cache 即便挂着也不会让 chip 行炸。
- `<details>` 原生折叠：免 useState、键盘可访问、reload 复位，省 30 行 state 管理。

## 测试方式
```bash
cd web && npx tsc -b --noEmit         # clean
py -m pytest -q                        # 227 passed（无后端改动）
```
**Chrome DevTools 实测**（截图见评论）：
- 桌面 1280×800：StagesBar 顶部，"AI · deepseek 3/5"，前 3 chip 绿底 AI、beats 红底"规则"、refine 灰底"未启用"。MetricsRow 6 格 + 校验通过。
- 移动 390×844：chip 行横向滚动，滚动条可见；MetricsRow 两列堆叠不挤。
- 点 "stage 降级详情 · 1 条" 折叠条 → 展开看到 `[stage:beats] N 个场景的 LLM 节拍抽取失败，已对这些场景回退到规则节拍提取。`

- 复用 PR #35 引入的 `quality_metrics.ai_stages_applied` / `llm_provider` 字段。
- 复用 PR #36 的颜色 token (`mark-original` / `mark-merged` / `ink-mute`)，不动 `index.css` 调色板。
- 全部业务原创：StagesBar / StageChip / StageDegradedDetails / deriveStageStatuses。

author: shawnyboyiii
body:
**💡 What**: Refactored the `filteredTransactions` `useMemo` hook in `TransactionList.tsx` to use a pre-compiled case-insensitive regular expression instead of dynamically generating arrays, joining strings, and calling `.toLowerCase()` on every transaction during search.

**🎯 Why**: Performing string allocations and transformations (`.join()`, `.toLowerCase()`) inside a loop that iterates over thousands of transactions creates significant main thread blocking and memory pressure, leading to sluggish search input performance.

**📊 Impact**: Local benchmarks indicate string filtering speeds improved ~6x (from ~419ms to ~70ms on a mock 10,000 item dataset). Re-renders when typing into the search bar are noticeably more responsive.

**🔬 Measurement**: To verify, load a large mock dataset of transactions and profile the React render tree while typing rapidly into the search field. The layout calculation time will be visibly reduced.

author: lbds137
body:
## Summary

Second slice of **a3-ii**: the worker re-derives the payload's `message` surface (plus `mentionedPersonas` / `referencedChannels`) from raw envelope inputs. Two commits:

### Commit 1 — shared kernels + relocation (`refactor(common-types)`)

The mention **scan/dedup/cap/placeholder ordering rules** are the drift surface, so they move to `utils/mentionRewriter.ts` and bot-client's `MentionResolver` becomes a thin Discord adapter:

- **`resolveUserMentions`** — content-order unique ids, `MAX_PER_MESSAGE` cap (beyond-cap left raw), in-map targets upsert + persona-resolve, out-of-map ids fall back through a DB lookup seam, bots/unknowns stay as raw tags
- **`rewriteChannelMentions` / `rewriteRoleMentions`** — snowflake-validated scan, per-type caps, unknown-placeholder substitution, driven by a single resolver callback (bot: guild cache; worker: envelope raw lists)
- Bot adapter derives targets with the SAME displayName rule the envelope capture uses (`globalName ?? username`) — identical inputs by construction
- **`MessageLinkParser`** (pure string logic) relocates to common-types
- **Approved behavior change (round 3)**: user-mention ids are now snowflake-validated like channels/roles — the original bot code skipped this for users, so junk ids like `<@1>` cost a DB round-trip on the fallback path. Applied in the kernel, so both sides changed atomically; test fixtures upgraded to valid snowflakes.
- Affected bot tests switch from full package mocks to **partial mocks so the real kernels stay under test** — the 27 MentionResolver tests now exercise actual kernel behavior through the adapter

### Commit 2 — worker content rewriting (`feat(ai-worker)`)

`rewriteRawContent` mirrors the bot's step-5 order exactly: **links → user mentions → channels → roles**.

- **`[Reference N]` link map reconstructed from wire-adopted numbers** (the #1160 design constraint): parse URLs from raw content → messageId → reference number, LAST number wins per messageId (mirrors `trackLink`'s Map.set for multi-snapshot forwards); URLs matching no reference stay raw, like the bot's unfetchable links
- **`ContextDataSource.findUserByDiscordId`** (new seam) — the mention DB fallback
- **Weigh-in jobs skip rewriting wholesale** — mirrors the bot's early return AND avoids upserting mention users for anonymous pokes
- **Shadow gains 3 surfaces** (now 11 total): `messageContent` diffed against the job's `message` field (threaded from `job.data`), `mentionedPersonas` / `referencedChannels` as id-set comparisons

### Documented accepted divergences

1. **Voice jobs: messageContent comparison skipped.** The envelope captured the pre-submission `content` param (transcript); the payload rewrote the *refetched* Discord content (empty for voice). Structurally incomparable until iii-b settles the voice content story — flagged as a cutover design question (worker using the transcript as `message` would currently double it with the attachment-description path in PromptBuilder).
2. **Forwarded triggers**: raw carries snapshot content vs. payload's refetched empty content — rare, counts as real divergence signal.
3. **Mid-flight edits** inside the 2.5s embed-processing delay: the bot rewrites post-refetch content; the envelope is pre-refetch.

## Testing

- `mentionRewriter.test.ts` (15, common-types) — caps/order/placeholder boundaries, bot skip, DB fallback, error tolerance
- `contentRewriter.test.ts` (8, ai-worker) — link-map last-wins, unmatched-URL pass-through, full pipeline order
- `ContextAssembler` +2 (REAL-kernel rewrite-through, weigh-in skip with upsert-count assertion), `shadowAssembly` +3 (content diverge, voice skip, id-set surfaces), `PrismaContextDataSource` +1
- `messageLinkParser.test.ts` relocated intact (22)
- Full suites green: ai-worker 3184, bot-client 4958, common-types 2736; `pnpm quality` green

author: rogerhirano-nw
body:
## Problem
`refresh_dv_attention` and `refresh_dv_ivt` used `DELETE FROM table WHERE date::text = ANY(:dates)` to clear existing rows before reinserting. The `::text` cast prevents index use, so Postgres does a full sequential scan on 270k+ rows — which hits Supabase's statement timeout and writes 0 rows.

## Fix
Switch both functions to use the existing `_safe_replace()` helper, which does TRUNCATE (O(1)) when the schema is unchanged. Both DV tables are always fully rebuilt from all available emails (limit=30), so there's no partial history to preserve.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge and trigger "Refresh DV (Attention + IVT only)" from Actions — confirm rows written > 0
- [ ] Clear Streamlit cache and verify Attention/SIVT/GIVT columns populate

author: gitu
body:
## What

Adds an **Overview** tab as the new default landing view for a project, alongside Network / Timeline / Table / Matrix. It becomes the project's home and consolidates the project-level controls that previously lived as buttons in the desktop-only header (and were unreachable on mobile).

### The Overview page
- **Title + description** — editable inline (`updateProjectMeta`, DB-backed)
- **Key figures** — derived from the existing CPM engine: task / milestone / container / dependency counts, estimated duration + start→finish dates, critical-path size, status breakdown, and weighted progress. Shows a cycle warning when the graph can't be scheduled.
- **AI summary** — on-demand, one-shot LLM call (`stream: false`) reusing the existing provider abstraction (auto-detects Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini). The client builds a compact, token-bounded digest of the plan; the server wraps it in a focused prompt. Auth-gated.
- **Calendar settings** — embedded inline, reusing `ProjectCalendarForm` (the save merge is factored into a shared `applyCalendar` helper used by both the inline form and the old sheet).
- **Project actions** — the relocated Export / Share / Branch controls.
- **Jump-off cards** — into each of the four other views, each with a one-line intro of what it is.

### Relocations
- Export, Share, Branch and Calendar are **removed from the header toolbar**, which now carries just the view tabs + fullscreen.
- Overview is the **default** view: a bare project URL lands on it; `?view=network` is now explicit. The mobile bottom nav and the AI assistant's product description (`ABOUT PERT.LI`) are updated to match.
- The public `/share/<token>` route keeps **Network** as its default and never exposes the Overview (it carries auth-gated controls).

## Tests
- **Unit + fast-check property tests** for the new pure logic: `computeProjectOverview`, `buildProjectDigest` (bounded output), `applyCalendar`.
- **Storybook stories** for `OverviewContent`, `OverviewMetrics`, `OverviewSummaryCard` covering default / empty / cycle / read-only / AI loading-done-error states.
- Full suite green (`pnpm test`: 883 passing), `pnpm check` clean, production build + Storybook build succeed.
- **Real-browser verification** (Playwright against a PGLite dev server) confirmed: Overview is the default landing (no `?view`), key figures / AI card / calendar form / all four jump-offs render, Share + Branch present on Overview, Calendar + Share **removed from the header toolbar**, jump-off navigates to Timeline, and the Overview tab clears `?view`.

> Note: the in-UI description-save round-trip could not be confirmed via automated e2e because local dev (no sync server, `VITE_E2E_DISABLE_SYNC=1`) can't reliably materialize Automerge docs — a documented limitation. The write itself uses the same shipped `updateProjectMeta` server fn as the existing rename dialog.

author: ramahi27
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the fitness app with SVG-based exercise illustrations as a fallback UI component, implements rate limiting for authentication endpoints, improves media resolution with ExerciseDB GIF support, and adds comprehensive input validation across the backend.

## Key Changes

### Frontend
- **Exercise Illustrations** (`ExerciseIllustration.tsx`): Added a new 500-line SVG component that renders 20+ exercise-specific illustrations (dumbbell, barbell, kettlebell, cable machines, cardio equipment, etc.) with a `categorizeExercise()` function to map exercise names to appropriate visuals. Illustrations use the app's color palette and serve as fallbacks when photos are unavailable.
- **Media Resolution** (`media.ts`): Enhanced resolution pipeline to check admin-uploaded media first, then ExerciseDB animated GIFs via `/api/exercise-gif/{name}`, with SVG illustration fallback when both fail.
- **Loading States**: Added skeleton loaders to home and profile screens to improve perceived performance during data fetches.
- **Error Boundaries** (`_layout.tsx`): Implemented React error boundary to gracefully handle and display app-level crashes.
- **Onboarding Flow** (`onboarding.tsx`): Added setup mode to allow profile updates post-signup without re-entering name/email.
- **Image Component Migration**: Replaced React Native `Image` with `expo-image` for better performance and caching across multiple screens.

### Backend
- **Rate Limiting** (`server.py`): Implemented in-memory rate limiter for auth endpoints (10 attempts per 5 minutes per email/IP) to prevent brute-force attacks.
- **Input Validation**: Added strict validation for profile creation/updates:
  - `goal` must be one of: `weight_loss`, `muscle_gain`, `endurance`
  - `level` must be one of: `beginner`, `intermediate`, `advanced`
  - `days_per_week` must be between 1–7 inclusive
  - Sanitized profile fields before LLM interpolation to prevent injection
- **Free Tier Limits**: Added scan limit enforcement (5 free scans per user, unlimited for Pro).
- **Image Size Validation**: Enforced 5 MB per-image and 10-image-per-scan limits.
- **Streak Logic Fix** (`log_session`): Corrected streak calculation to only increment on consecutive days, preventing same-day double-counting.
- **Environment Configuration**: Made Claude model selection configurable via `CLAUDE_MODEL` env var.

### Testing
- **Test Suite** (`test_auth.py`, `conftest.py`): Added comprehensive smoke tests for auth and profile endpoints, including signup/signin flows, duplicate email detection, weak password rejection, and invalid input handling.
- **Mock Database**: Created reusable mock Motor collection and database fixtures for async testing.

## Notable Implementation Details
- SVG illustrations use a 100×100 viewBox with the app's color constants (purple, teal, white) for visual consistency.
- Rate limiter uses a simple in-memory bucket approach with timestamp-based window sliding.
- Media resolution is async and cached in-memory to avoid redundant API calls.
- Streak logic now correctly handles timezone-aware datetime comparisons and only increments on new calendar days.

author: sebtardif
body:
Add two flat-schema batch MCP tools that apply the same operation to
multiple files atomically:

- **batch_replace**: same from/to replacement across a list of files
  (supports regex, case_insensitive, multiline)
- **batch_tidy**: trim trailing whitespace and ensure final newline
  across a list of files

## Why these are different from the removed batch/transaction tools

PR #481 removed batch and transaction MCP tools because agents failed
to compose the 23-variant discriminated union (0-40% success rate).
These new tools have **flat schemas** identical to their single-file
counterparts plus a `files` array. No variant selection, no nested
operation objects.

Under the hood, each tool builds a multi-operation Plan and executes
atomically via the existing tx engine.

## Benchmark results (3 runs, 9 tasks, 3 modes)

**27/27 tasks passed** (zero failures).

| Mode | Median total |
|---|---|
| PL-CLI | 307.7s |
| MCP | 286.8s |
| Native | 233.5s |

The new `multi_file_replace` task (version bump across 3 files):

| Mode | Median | Range |
|---|---|---|
| PL-CLI | 46.1s | 25.8-95.9s |
| MCP | 31.1s | 31.0-39.2s |
| Native | 24.5s | 19.3-26.0s |

MCP `tidy` task (whitespace fix across 3 files) is where batch
tools provide the most value: MCP 43.8s vs Native 83.7s.

## Changes

- Add BatchReplaceParams and BatchTidyParams structs
- Add batch_replace and batch_tidy tool implementations
- Add 5 MCP integration tests (round-trip, regex, empty-reject,
  path-traversal, tidy)
- Add multi_file_replace benchmark task (9 tasks total)

- Add batch tool examples to 08-mcp-tool-call.json
- Update tool selection guide and MCP mode instructions

body:
## 概要

複数のAPIモジュール（articles, tags, comments, auth）に散在していたエラーハンドリングロジックを共通化し、`api-error.ts`に集約しました。これにより、コード重複を削減し、エラーメッセージの抽出と例外スローの処理を統一します。

## 主な変更

- **新規ファイル: `packages/frontend/src/lib/api-error.ts`**
  - `extractErrorMessage(data)`: APIレスポンスボディから`error`フィールド（文字列）を抽出する関数
  - `throwApiError(res, defaultMessage)`: レスポンスボディに`error`フィールドがあればそれを、なければデフォルトメッセージとステータスコードを組み合わせて例外をスローする関数

- **新規ファイル: `packages/frontend/src/lib/api-error.test.ts`**
  - `extractErrorMessage`の5つのテストケース（文字列フィールド、非文字列フィールド、フィールド不在、null、非オブジェクト）
  - `throwApiError`の3つのテストケース（errorメッセージあり、なし、JSON以外のレスポンス）

- **`packages/frontend/src/features/articles/articles.api.ts`**
  - ローカルで定義されていた`extractErrorMessage`を削除
  - 5箇所のエラーハンドリングを`throwApiError`に統一

- **`packages/frontend/src/features/tags/tags.api.ts`**
  - ローカルで定義されていた`extractErrorMessage`を削除
  - 2箇所のエラーハンドリングを`throwApiError`に統一

- **`packages/frontend/src/features/comments/comments.api.ts`**
  - インラインのエラーメッセージ抽出ロジックを削除
  - `throwApiError`に統一

- **`packages/frontend/src/features/auth/auth.api.ts`**
  - ローカルで定義されていた`isErrorResponse`型ガード関数を削除
  - `extractErrorMessage`を使用してエラーメッセージを抽出

## 実装の詳細

- `throwApiError`は`Promise<never>`を返すため、呼び出し後の処理が実行されないことを型で保証
- `extractErrorMessage`は型安全に`error`フィールドを検証し、文字列でない場合は`undefined`を返す
- すべてのAPIモジュールで統一されたエラーハンドリングにより、保守性と一貫性が向上

body:
## Plan only (no implementation)

Design doc for a first-class vsync toggle reachable from every surface and applied **live**. `docs/plans/active/vsync-toggle.md`. Implementation deferred until this plan is approved.

### Design
A tiny GLFW-free Core hub (`smatchet::vsync`, atomic) is the **live runtime source of truth**; persisted `TrackerConfig::VsyncEnabled` is the **durable** source that seeds it at boot. The render loop reads it each frame and calls `glfwSwapInterval` **only on change**.

| Surface | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Preference | "Enable vsync" checkbox, Appearance tab (live + persisted) |
| Command → CLI/MCP/Lua/palette | `config.set vsync on\|off` (one config-set table row — "register once, surface everywhere") |
| CLI flag | `--no-vsync` / `--vsync` (launch override) |
| Env | `SMATCHET_FPS_VSYNC` (reconciled through the hub; from #904) |

**Precedence at boot:** env > CLI flag > persisted config. Runtime: preference/command apply live.

**Non-goals:** adaptive/per-monitor vsync, DX12 swapchain rewrite (Unreal owns present), FPS cap.

### Scope (verified against current code)
~7 files across **strict zones** (Config/, Commands/): `VsyncControl.h` (new), `ConfigManager.h/.cpp`, `BuiltinCommands_Config.cpp`, `SmatchetPreferencesUi_Local.cpp`, `StandaloneAppBootstrap.cpp`, `main.cpp`. All cited integration points (`glfwSwapInterval` sites, `kBoolFields`, config-set table, `ParseStandaloneCli` bool-flag pattern, `DrawAppearance*Section` helpers, `lastAppliedTheme_` live-apply pattern) verified present.

Pure-docs PR. Plan carries the mandatory Perf-gate section (touches Source/Core), Verification, and grill-with-docs items.

Two things in this batch.

## 1. Watering audit + directives (existing roster)
Reassessed every plant on **water demand** for our semi-arid climate. Confirmed all carry the short-card + detailed-care watering structure, and **sharpened the 5 bare card notes** into real directives (red-twig dogwood, garden peony, snapdragon, snow-on-the-mountain, rambling rose). The only genuine "needs constant water" outlier is Mountain alder (riparian) — kept, with a clear "not for dry zones" directive.

## 2. Twelve winter/early-spring pollinator plants (96 → 108)
Bridges the Feb–March forage gap (nothing else on the roster blooms before April). Each has a repo-hosted photo reel, a Front-Range `care` block, a safety-reviewed `edible`/toxicity block, and a fully cited `references` + `fact_src`, plus the agreed watering directive on card + care page.

- **Bulbs/tubers:** snow crocus, snowdrops, winter aconite, dwarf iris
- **True winter bloomers:** Christmas rose, winter heath
- **Late-winter shrubs:** witch hazel, Cornelian cherry, pussy willow
- **Potted/cool-season** (keep in bloom in a pot, set out on warm winter days for bees): rosemary, sweet alyssum, pansy

**Honesty calls baked into the care text:**
- Winter heath is **not ground-hardy** here — grow it in an acid-mix pot (alkaline clay would kill it).
- Witch hazel & pussy willow are **N.-American natives but not Front-Range natives** (marked Non-native, honest `origin`).
- Pussy willow is **dioecious** (buy a named male for the catkins) and a **high-water wetland shrub**.
- Sweet alyssum left **caution / not-food** (no authority documents it culinary); stays a star pollinator plant.

- `check_refs.py` and `check_citations.py` pass on all 12 (29 OK / 0 dead; 1 known false-alarm REVIEW).

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The app starts on port 3000 but crashes on the first request due to two middleware bugs. `GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware` constructs a Serilog file sink pointing at `.\Errors\log.json` — a Windows-style relative path that doesn't exist in the Railway Linux container, causing the constructor to throw and the app to crash. `Culturemiddleware` calls `new CultureInfo(cultureName)` directly on the raw `Accept-Language` header value without any error handling; a malformed or unrecognised culture tag throws `CultureNotFoundException`, which propagates up and kills the request pipeline.

## Solution

In `GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware`, replaced the hardcoded Windows path with `Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Errors")` (cross-platform, absolute), added `Directory.CreateDirectory` to ensure the directory exists before writing, and wrapped the entire logger construction in a try-catch that falls back to a console-only Serilog logger if the file sink fails. The per-request log call is also wrapped in its own try-catch so a logging failure can never crash the pipeline. In `Culturemiddleware`, extracted culture resolution into a `ResolveCulture` helper that handles an empty header, strips quality-value suffixes (`; q=...`) from the first language tag, and catches `CultureNotFoundException` to fall back to `"en-US"`. Added `Serilog.Sinks.Console` 4.1.0 to the project file to support the console fallback logger.

### Changes
- **Modified** `TeenConnect.API/Infrastructure/Middlewares/GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware.cs`
- **Modified** `TeenConnect.API/Infrastructure/Middlewares/Culturemiddleware.cs`
- **Modified** `TeenConnect.API/TeenConnect.API.csproj`

author: stormer78
body:
## Summary

Adds the complete **per-verifier pseudonym (holder-binding) layer** to `affinidi-bbs` — `draft-irtf-cfrg-bbs-per-verifier-linkability` over blind BBS — in a new `affinidi-bbs::nym` module, **byte-exact KAT-gated against the official IETF pseudonym test vectors** (BLS12-381-SHA-256).

This is the BBS-level cryptography for holder binding (#353). A holder commits a `prover_nym`; the issuer mixes in `signer_nym_entropy`; `nym_secret = prover_nym + signer_nym_entropy` is known to neither party alone. At presentation the holder derives a **stable, per-verifier `Pseudonym`** from a verifier `context_id`, bound into the selective-disclosure proof — so one verifier recognises repeat visits, but different verifiers (even colluding) cannot link the holder.

It builds directly on the blind BBS merged in #366 and the pseudonym proof primitive from #358.

## Public API

Issuance:
- `nym_commit(prover_nym, committed_messages)` → `(commitment_with_proof, secret_prover_blind)`
- `blind_sign_with_nym(sk, pk, commitment_with_proof, signer_nym_entropy, header, messages)` → `Signature`
- `blind_verify_with_nym(pk, sig, header, messages, committed_messages, prover_nym, signer_nym_entropy, secret_prover_blind)`

Proof:
- `proof_gen_with_nym(...)` → `(Proof, Pseudonym)` — dual selective disclosure over signer **and** committed messages
- `proof_verify_with_nym(...)`

Plus `Ciphersuite::pseudonym_api_id` and `calculate_pseudonym_generator_with_api_id`.

## Verification

- **NymCommit + BlindSignWithNym + BlindVerifyWithNym** KATs across every committed/signer combination
- **ProofGen/Verify** KATs across all **five** disclosure patterns — both the proof bytes **and** the pseudonym match byte-for-byte, and verify accepts each
- `nym_secret` relationship + a random commit→sign→verify round-trip with tamper rejection
- **78 tests pass**, `clippy -D warnings` clean

## Refactor (additive, no behaviour change)

Extracted generator-agnostic `proof_gen_core` / `proof_verify_core` from the plain-BBS proof impls so the plain pseudonym path and the blind/pseudonym path share the **same verified** blinding + challenge + pairing logic; `compute_challenge` and `calculate_pseudonym_generator` now take an explicit api_id. The unchanged #358 proof KATs validate the refactor. The blind internals from #366 are now `pub(crate)` for reuse.

Implementation notes (one sharp edge): the pseudonym ops namespace generators/hashing under a **third** api_id (`…_H2G_HM2S_PSEUDONYM_`), distinct from both the core and blind api_ids — getting this wrong yields a correct `secret_prover_blind` but a wrong commitment point.

## Versioning

`affinidi-bbs` **0.2.1 → 0.2.2** (patch) — purely additive, so the patch keeps the existing `major.minor` pin valid (`affinidi-data-integrity = "0.2"`); no dependent cascade.

## Next

The **vc-di-bbs document layer** (`0xd95d08`/`0xd95d09`, `context_id` from `verifierId`) composes this crypto into the W3C `bbs-2023` flow — that's the follow-up that **closes #353** (#360).

Proof-bearing crypto over BLS12-381 — covered by the pending BBS security audit (#363) before backing real credentials.

Refs #353, #360

body: ### What does this PR do? Re-lands the `github/review` composite-action hardening onto `main`. These three follow-ups were surfaced by the multi-model review of #900 and were originally opened as #910 — but #910 was accidentally merged into #900's feature branch (`fix/v0.8.4-dbt-review-launch`) *after* #900 had already squash-merged to `main`, so the changes never reached `main`. This PR targets `main` directly and supersedes #910. - **Authenticate the release-version lookup.** The fallback path (non-semver `github.action_ref` — a branch, SHA, or `main`) calls `releases/latest` unauthenticated (IP-limited to 60 req/hr). It now passes `${{ github.token }}`, lifting the limit to 1,000 req/hr so busy runners aren't throttled into the `latest` fallback. - **Never cache a floating `latest`.** When the version resolved to `latest` it was used as a static cache key, so one rate-limited/offline lookup pinned that binary forever. The cache step is now gated with `if: steps.version.outputs.version != 'latest'`; a resolved semver caches normally, `latest` falls through to a fresh install. - **Keep the hosted API key out of `jq` argv.** The credential write read the key via `--arg key "$IN_ALT_KEY"` (visible in `argv`; printed under `ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG` → `set -x`). It now reads from the environment inside the jq program (`$ENV.IN_ALT_KEY`). None of these are regressions; the golden `@vX.Y.Z` path never hits the release-API lookup and is unaffected. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix / hardening (non-breaking change) - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Documentation ### Issue for this PR Closes #909 ### How did you verify your code works? Four adversarial tests in `release-v0.8.5-adversarial.test.ts` (run the action's real shell with fake `curl`/`jq` on `PATH`): - the release lookup attaches `Authorization: Bearer ` when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is present; - it omits the header and still resolves the version when no token is set (verifies the `${AUTH[@]+"${AUTH[@]}"}` empty-array idiom is safe under `set -u`, back to bash 3.2); - the `Cache altimate-code` step is gated on `steps.version.outputs.version != 'latest'`; - the hosted-credential write keeps the API key out of the `jq` argv (asserts the secret is absent from captured args and the program uses `$ENV.IN_ALT_KEY`). Local checks (all green on this branch, cherry-picked cleanly onto current `main`): - `bun test test/skill/release-v0.8.5-adversarial.test.ts` → 13 pass. - `bun run script/upstream/analyze.ts --markers --base main --strict` → ok. - `prettier --check` on the changed test file → clean. Action YAML parses. ### Checklist - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (CHANGELOG) - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Hardens the `github/review` composite action to reduce rate-limit failures, prevent stale binary caching, and keep the hosted API key out of process args. author: mystifii
body:
## Problem

A user saw one playlist stuck at "checked 6 minutes ago" with the default 5-minute interval. Root cause from the logs:

```
Failed to poll …/pl.u-…: Discord bot channel post failed (403): {"message": "Missing Permissions", "code": 50013}
```

The Discord post threw **out of** the poll, so the snapshot was never saved — `lastChecked` froze, and the new tracks were never marked seen, so every subsequent poll re-detected them and **failed again** in a silent loop. The only trace was a log line.

## Fix

Decouple delivery from polling:

- **No new tracks** → advance the snapshot (refresh `lastChecked`, clear any prior error).
- **New tracks** → attempt delivery first; only advance the snapshot **on success**. On failure, refresh `lastChecked` (the poll itself worked) and record `lastError`, but **keep the previous `trackIds`** so the undelivered additions are retried next poll and arrive once the problem is fixed — no silent loss, no frozen time.
- **Fetch/parse failures** still keep a stale `lastChecked` (we genuinely couldn't check) and record the error.

Poll/delivery errors are persisted (`lastError` / `lastErrorAt`) and shown **per playlist in the web UI** (⚠ line), turning a mysterious stale timestamp into an actionable message (e.g. "Discord delivery failed: … Missing Permissions").

## Changes

- `store/state.ts`: `lastError`/`lastErrorAt` on snapshots; `recordPollError()` (fetch failures, keeps stale time).
- `watcher.ts`: `deliver()` + `markDeliveryFailed()`; snapshot advances only on delivered notifications.
- `web/server.ts`: list endpoint returns `lastError`/`lastErrorAt`.
- `web/page.ts`: per-playlist error line.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.
- Reproduced a delivery failure end-to-end (planted baseline so tracks look new + a webhook Discord rejects): 50 tracks detected → `404 Unknown Webhook` → **trackIds NOT advanced** (will retry), **`lastChecked` refreshed**, `lastError` recorded.

author: orizi
body:
## Summary

Fixes an incorrect hex literal in a comment within `add_padding` in `keccak.cairo` (the example for `last_input_num_bytes == 4` showed `0x1000000` and `0xffffff` instead of the correct `0x100000000` and `0xffffffff`), and adds a `# Panics` doc section to `math.cairo` documenting that `extended_gcd` panics for signed types when `a` or `b` equals `T::MIN`, since the absolute value of `T::MIN` is not representable in `T`.

---

## Type of change

Please check **one**:

- [ ] Bug fix (fixes incorrect behavior)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [x] Documentation change with concrete technical impact
- [ ] Style, wording, formatting, or typo-only change

---

## Why is this change needed?

The comment in `add_padding` contained wrong hex values for the 4-byte case — the mask and offset were both one nibble short, which could mislead anyone reading or auditing the padding logic. Additionally, the `extended_gcd` function had no documentation of its panic condition, leaving callers unaware that passing `T::MIN` for a signed type would cause a panic at runtime.

---

## What was the behavior or documentation before?

- The comment in `keccak.cairo` showed `0x1000000 + (last_input_word & 0xffffff)` for the `last_input_num_bytes == 4` example, which is incorrect (off by one byte).
- `math.cairo` had no `# Panics` section documenting the `T::MIN` restriction.

---

## What is the behavior or documentation after?

- The comment now correctly shows `0x100000000 + (last_input_word & 0xffffffff)`, matching the actual 4-byte (32-bit) mask.
- `math.cairo` now includes a `# Panics` section explaining that the function panics for signed `T` when `a` or `b` is `T::MIN`.

---

## Related issue or discussion (if any)

N/A

---

## Additional context

The keccak comment fix is purely cosmetic (the code itself was correct), but accurate comments are important for auditability of cryptographic code. The panic documentation is a concrete correctness concern for callers using signed integer types.

author: runyaga
body:
## Problem

Hosted apps reached through the `/hosted/<workspace-id>/<port>/` proxy (e.g. a marimo notebook) failed in two ways:

1. **Slashless URL → 404.** Visiting `…/hosted/<id>/9001` (no trailing slash) returned 404. The proxy `location` regex `^/hosted/[^/]+/(\d+)/(.*)$` requires a slash after the port, so the request fell through to the klangk app, which has no such route.
2. **"kernel not found" / broken app.** Even with the trailing slash, the page loaded but the app couldn't reach its backend. marimo (and jupyter, vite HMR, etc.) talk to their backend over a websocket, and the hosted proxy block set `proxy_http_version 1.1` but never forwarded the `Upgrade`/`Connection` headers, so the WS handshake never upgraded.

## Fix (`scripts/nginx.sh`)

1. **308 redirect** from the slashless form to the canonical trailing-slash form. A redirect (not just widening the regex) is required because hosted apps emit *relative* asset paths (`./assets/...`) that resolve against the browser's base URL — so the address bar must end in `/<port>/` for assets to resolve.
2. **Forward websocket headers** in the proxy block, reusing the `$connection_upgrade` map already defined for the main `location /` block.

## Verification

Confirmed live after a full `devenv processes up` restart (config regenerated from this script):

```
no trailing slash   →  308  →  Location: …/9001/
  (followed)        →  200   (marimo loads)
with trailing slash →  200
/ws?session_id=…    →  101 Switching Protocols   (kernel websocket upgrades)
```

Before the fix: slashless → 404, and the kernel websocket could not upgrade ("kernel not found").

author: deeli19
body:
## Summary

This PR evolves the HR Analytics project from a traditional marts-focused architecture into a semantic-layer-ready analytics platform.

The primary objective was to align the project with modern dbt semantic modeling practices while maintaining compatibility with warehouse-native BI tools such as Metabase.

Although dbt Core generates a semantic manifest, that manifest is not directly consumable by Metabase. This refactor therefore introduces a dual-purpose architecture:

* Semantic-model-ready foundations for future MetricFlow or dbt Cloud adoption
* Business-facing marts optimized for warehouse-first BI consumption today

---

## Architectural Changes

### Intermediate Layer Redesign

Refactored employee history modeling around snapshots and employee state transitions.

#### Added

* `int_employee_current_state`

  * Current employee dimension foundation
  * One row per employee
  * Serves workforce reporting and dimensional use cases

* `int_employee_state_changes`

  * Historical employee state transition model
  * Derived from `employee_snapshot`
  * Tracks attribute changes across employee lifecycle states

#### Existing Models Updated

* `employee_snapshot`

  * Continues to serve as the historical source of truth
  * Captures workforce state changes using dbt snapshots

* `int_employee_identity`

  * Maintains employee identity resolution logic
  * Supports canonical employee records

---

## Workforce Event Modeling

### Added `fct_employee_events`

Introduced an event-based workforce fact model derived from employee state transitions.

Purpose:

* Workforce lifecycle analytics
* Promotion tracking
* Transfer analysis
* Supervisor change monitoring
* Employee status change analysis
* Future semantic layer metric definitions

Grain:

> One row per employee event

Examples include:

* Employee status changes
* Department transfers
* Division transfers
* Title changes
* Supervisor changes

---

## Monthly Workforce Modeling

### Added `fct_employee_workforce_monthly`

Created a monthly workforce KPI fact model for trend analysis.

Captures:

* Monthly hires
* Monthly terminations

Grain:

> One row per month

Supports:

* Workforce growth analysis
* Hiring trends
* Attrition trends
* Headcount reporting

---

## Employee Archive Improvements

### Enhanced `fct_employee_monthly_archive`

Retained historical employee archive functionality while improving alignment with workforce analytics use cases.

Current grain:

> One row per employee per archive month

Supports:

* Historical workforce snapshots
* Workforce composition analysis
* Longitudinal reporting

---

## Semantic Layer Enablement

Implemented semantic model definitions and metric definitions compatible with dbt's semantic manifest generation.

### Added Semantic Models

#### employee_events

Built on:

* `fct_employee_events`

Provides:

* Employee entity definitions
* Event dimensions
* Organizational dimensions
* Event measures

#### workforce_monthly

Built on:

* `fct_employee_workforce_monthly`

Provides:

* Monthly workforce measures
* Time-based workforce aggregation

### Added Metrics

* `monthly_hires`
* `monthly_terminations`

Result:

* Successful semantic manifest generation
* Future compatibility with MetricFlow-based tooling
* Simplified migration path to dbt Cloud Semantic Layer

---

## Change Detection Improvements

### Enhanced Attribute Change Tracking

Reviewed limitations in the original `detect_attribute_change` macro.

Identified analytical blind spots where multiple employee attributes changed simultaneously.

Rather than replacing the original implementation outright, introduced a versioned enhancement strategy to demonstrate:

* Backward compatibility
* Incremental model evolution
* dbt deprecation patterns
* Controlled migration paths

This preserves historical behavior while providing a path toward richer event analysis.

---

## BI Consumption Strategy

Established a clear separation between:

### Semantic Layer Assets

Used for:

* Metric definitions
* Semantic governance
* Future MetricFlow adoption

### Warehouse Marts

Used for:

* Metabase dashboards
* Ad-hoc analysis
* Direct warehouse consumption

Primary BI-facing models now include:

* `fct_employee_events`
* `fct_employee_monthly_archive`
* `fct_employee_workforce_monthly`
* `dim_active_employees`
* `dim_inactive_employees`

This approach avoids coupling BI tools directly to semantic-layer infrastructure while preserving future flexibility.

---

## Lineage Improvements

The project lineage now follows a more intentional layered architecture:

body:
## Phase C — one-command `verify` gate + `test.yml` collapse

Targets `improve/test-ci-cleanup` (stacked on Phase A #31 + Phase B #32).

### `scripts/verify.ts` (new)

One command that runs every repo gate, **collecting** failures (does not stop
at the first) and naming each failed check in the summary. Exit 0 prints
`verify: all N check(s) passed`; any failure exits 1 with
`verify: FAILED — X/N check(s): <names>`.

Checks, in order: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test` (delegates to `bun run test` —
never re-implements the 3-process `mock.module` split), `check-suppress-comments
--all`, `check-doc-counts`, `check-output-table`, `markdownlint` (folds in the
old standalone markdown job), then the **PR-only** guards `check-stable-exports`
and `check-changelog`.

Each check is spawned as its own `Bun.spawnSync` subprocess with inherited
stdio, preserving each script's exit semantics and the test isolation.

**Flags:** `--base <ref>` (override the PR-only base), `--only <c1,c2>`,
`--skip <c1,c2>`. Unknown `--only`/`--skip` names exit 2 with the known-check
list.

**Base resolution for the PR-only checks:**
- explicit `--base <ref>` wins (CI passes `origin/$BASE_REF`);
- else auto-detect via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD` (→ e.g.
  `origin/main`, fallback `origin/main`); run the PR-only checks only when that
  ref resolves AND `HEAD` differs from it. Otherwise print
  `verify: skipping PR-only checks (no base ref)` and continue (a local checkout
  on the default branch is not a PR — no fail).

### `package.json`

- add `"verify": "bun scripts/verify.ts"`;
- `"prepublishOnly"`: `bun run build && bun run test` → `bun run build && bun run verify`.

### `.github/workflows/test.yml`

- `test` job: replace the `Lint` + `Test` + five `check-*` steps with a single
  verify step — `Verify (PR)` (`bun run verify --base "origin/$BASE_REF"`, keeping
  the `BASE_REF` env indirection so `github.base_ref` can't shell-inject) and
  `Verify (push)` (`bun run verify`, verify auto-skips PR-only internally).
  `fetch-depth: 0` preserved for base diffing.
- **Drop `no-cache: true`** from this job's `setup-bun` (the `file:../..` farm
  that required it is gone as of Phase B) — stale comment deleted too.
- **Fold the standalone `markdown` job into verify** (deleted) — verify now runs
  markdownlint.
- **`semgrep` job kept separate, unchanged** (pip-based, not part of local verify).

### Verification (run locally)

- `bun run verify` (auto-detect base → `origin/main`): exit 0, all 9 checks pass
  (both PR-only checks ran because HEAD differs from origin/main).
- `bun run verify --base origin/improve/test-ci-cleanup` (simulates the CI PR
  invocation): exit 0, all 9 pass — `check-stable-exports` 64→64 no removals;
  `check-changelog` reports `src/ not touched; skipping check` (Phase C touches
  scripts/package.json/test.yml, not `src/`).
- Failure path: injected a scratch type error and ran `bun run verify --only
  typecheck` → exit 1, summary `FAILED — 1/1 check(s): typecheck`; scratch
  removed. `--only nonexistent` → exit 2 with the known-check list. `--only
  typecheck,lint` → exit 0, ran 2.
- `bun run typecheck` exit 0; `bun run lint` (pinned biome + eslint) exit 0;
  `bun run test` exit 0 — 826 tests (804 / 7 / 15), 0 fail, coverage 88.60%
  funcs / 91.08% lines (above the 85% / 89% floor).

**No `src/` change → no CHANGELOG entry** (`check-changelog` only fires on `src/`;
`check-doc-counts` test-count claim of 826 unchanged).
