body: ## Slice 116 — self-healing immunity, with the §1 bound intact **Safety reframe (verify-first, load-bearing):** "autonomously LLM-synthesize a cage rule and hot-load it" is an **Order-2 RSI driver** — the system rewriting its own safety substrate, exactly what the recursion-depth gate severs and the dissertation argues is *unsafe* (and it opens "the adversary writes its own antibody"). Built the safe, dissertation-correct version instead: - **Deterministic synthesis, not LLM** — `extract_signature` analyzes the escape's AST; `synthesize_antibody` emits a **pure structural matcher** keyed on the introspection vector. Not prompt-injectable, no code execution. - **synthesize → validate → SHADOW → operator-promote** — a proposal must block the exact escape + cause **ZERO clean-control false-positives** + only ADD a block (monotonic tighten). Written to a shadow ledger; `promote_antibody` is **fail-closed** (refuses without explicit `operator_approved=True`). The synthesizer never auto-arms the cage. - **Hot-swappable `AntibodyRegistry`** — approved antibodies load live via `reload()` (no restart / no GLS interruption); the cage consults it **additively** on top of the built-in SemanticGuardian patterns (can only add blocks). - **`on_escape`** listener — verified escape → synthesize + propose (shadow only). **9 tests** incl. the **closed-loop siege**: escape passes → synth → operator-promote → hot-swap → the same payload is now **BLOCKED** → clean controls still pass; plus the fail-closed promotion gate + FP-prone-rule rejection. Master §33.1 default-FALSE. **Honest scope:** synthesizer + registry + closed loop verified; wiring `on_escape` into the live Slice-115 escape stream (threading the escape source through `adversarial_sweep`) is a small additive follow-up. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a bounded adaptive immunity layer that deterministically synthesizes “antibodies” from escape ASTs and hot-loads operator‑approved rules to block the exact payload with zero false positives. The system never self-arms and is off by default behind `JARVIS_ADAPTIVE_IMMUNITY_ENABLED`. - **New Features** - Deterministic AST signature extraction and structural matchers (no LLM, no exec). - Propose-only flow: synthesize → validate (must block escape, zero FP) → write to shadow ledger. - Fail-closed promotion: `promote_antibody(..., operator_approved=True)` writes to active ledger. - Hot-swappable `AntibodyRegistry.reload()` adds approved blocks without restart. - `on_escape` listener synthesizes and proposes; never arms. - Tests cover closed loop (escape → promote → reload → blocked) and safety gates. - **Migration** - Default off; set `JARVIS_ADAPTIVE_IMMUNITY_ENABLED=1` to activate proposing. - Optional paths: `JARVIS_ANTIBODY_PROPOSALS_PATH` and `JARVIS_ANTIBODY_ACTIVE_PATH` (JSONL). - Operator flow: review proposal → call `promote_antibody(..., operator_approved=True)` → `AntibodyRegistry.reload()` to apply. Written for commit e76c805fc03551c3ebc36e1a9578d18dc344a072. Summary will update on new commits.

author: ryancheley
body:
## Problem

On the Raspberry Pi (now Python 3.13 / Trixie), `just run` emits:

```
DeprecationWarning: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated and scheduled for
removal in a future version. Use timezone-aware objects to represent datetimes
in UTC: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).
```

`datetime.utcnow()` returns a naive datetime and is deprecated as of Python 3.12.

## Fix

`pytz.utc.localize(datetime.utcnow())` and `datetime.now(pytz.utc)` produce the
same UTC-aware instant, so swap to the latter. No behaviour change — `now` is
still converted to `America/Los_Angeles` immediately after.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff check .` — passes.
- [x] Verified both expressions yield equal UTC-aware datetimes; the new form raises no warning.
- [ ] On the Pi: `git pull` + `just run` — warning is gone.

author: orlandobrunet-sketch
body:
A busca do Histórico não retornava nada (sempre "Nenhuma questão encontrada"). Diagnóstico e correção da causa raiz + botão Buscar.

> ⚠️ Encadeado: baseado na branch do PR #431. Mergear **#431 antes** deste.

## Causa raiz
O explorador de Histórico montava a lista a partir do `questionBank` (deck interno do jogo), cujo schema é **abreviado** — `{id, q, o, a, e, c}`, **sem `qid`** (no deck o valor do qid fica no campo `id`). Como o filtro fazia `seenSet.has(q.qid)`, o `q.qid` era sempre `undefined` → **nenhuma questão casava** → lista vazia, independente do que se digitasse. (A busca em si já disparava no `input`; o problema eram os dados.)

## Correções
1. **Fonte de dados** — o dashboard agora usa sempre `topics` (schema completo: `qid`, `t`, `opts`, `ans`, `cat`, `exp`), que casa com o `seenSet` (povoado por `sr-data` e `mastered`, que guardam o qid). Garante também o carregamento de `topics` via `_loadTopics()` antes de montar a lista.
2. **Gravação upstream** (`game.js`) — `questionHistory.qid` e `nefroquest-all-answered-qids` estavam gravando `question.qid` (`undefined` no deck). Agora usam `question.qid || question.id`, populando o histórico corretamente.
3. **Botão "🔍 Buscar"** ao lado do campo (como você pediu) + busca no **Enter**; a busca ao vivo no `input` continua funcionando.

Bump **v11.64 → v11.65**.

## Como testar
1. Mergear #431, depois este. Hard refresh (footer v11.65).
2. Responder algumas questões (ex.: de DRC).
3. Dashboard → Histórico → digitar "drc" (ou clicar Buscar / Enter) → as questões respondidas aparecem; expandir mostra enunciado, alternativas e explicação.
4. "Apenas Erros Recentes" filtra os erros.

body:
## Summary
Fixes the critical security holes plus a few important consistency issues found during a full project review. **No new environment variables** — reuses existing Supabase/OpenAI/Stripe config.

## 🔴 Critical
- **JWT signatures are now verified.** All four authenticated endpoints (`analyze`, `usage`, `reward`, `referrals`) previously decoded the JWT payload *without checking the signature*, so anyone could forge a token with any `sub`/`email` — bypassing auth and usage limits (unbounded OpenAI spend + user impersonation). They now use a shared `verifyUser()` helper that calls `supabase.auth.getUser()` (the same verified path `subscribe.js` already used).
- **Removed secret-leaking debug logs.** `background.js` was logging the full token-exchange response (access + refresh tokens) and auth URLs; `analyze.js` was logging captured page content.

## 🟡 Important
- Consolidated `FREE_LIMIT` / `PRO_MONTHLY_LIMIT` into `api/_config.js` so the endpoints can't drift; aligned stale `10`-fallbacks in `popup.js` and the schema comment with the real value (`5`).
- Fixed referral link pointing at the dead `studysnap-ai.github.io` domain → `trystudysnap.com`.
- Free-tier usage is now incremented **after** a successful AI call, so a failed capture no longer costs the user a credit.

## Testing
- `node --check` passes on all modified files.
- No new env vars; backend behavior verified against existing Supabase RPCs.

## Notes
- Pre-existing minor race condition in the free-tier limit (concurrent requests) left as-is — can be made atomic in the DB later if desired.

body:
Shared substrate for the learned tier (S19), first PR in the P5 → S19 → E7 chain.

**Segment-aggregate** (`jammi-encoders/aggregate.rs`): `SegmentReduce{Sum,Mean,Max}` over dense segment ids, fully differentiable. Sum = one `index_add`; Mean guards empty `count==0`; Max is tie-safe (positive-band shift + gradient-free membership mask — the `-inf` mask NaNs the backward on empty segments). Empty segment → zero row, a documented NaN-free divergence from the data-plane UDAF's serve-time *null*. Parity-tested against `vector_agg_udaf` within an f32-vs-f64 tolerance, plus permutation-invariance and finite-difference gradient checks.

**Optimizer seam** (`fine_tune/optimizer.rs`): extracts the clip→step logic into `clip_and_step`, now shared by the text trainer's three step sites and the non-text loop (no duplication; the text path's grad-accumulation stays put).

**Non-text loop** (`pipeline/parallel_train.rs`): `train_loop` over precomputed `TensorBatch`es with caller closures — its signature names no tokenizer/`LoadedModel`/`input_ids`, so decoupling from the text path is structural.

Note: corrects a long-standing false spec premise — candle 0.9.2 *does* have `scatter_add`/`index_add`/`scatter` with autograd (caught by the plan pressure-test).

## Verification
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean · `cargo test -p jammi-encoders -p jammi-ai` 333 passed / 0 failed (incl. the text-trainer regression suite) · `cargo fmt --check` clean.

body:
## What

`sdd-tasks` now instructs the executor to emit a `## Review Workload Forecast` block with the exact guard lines the orchestrator parses before launching apply:

- `400-line budget risk: Low|Medium|High`
- `Chained PRs recommended: Yes|No`
- `Decision needed before apply: Yes|No`

## Why

The shared protocol (`sdd-phase-common.md` section F) and the orchestrator's "Review Workload Guard" both **promise** this forecast, but the `sdd-tasks` skill body never told the executor to produce it. Contract↔implementation gap: the guard was documented but never emitted, so the orchestrator's workload gate ran blind.

## How

- Added a forecast step + `## Review Workload Forecast` output block to `sdd-tasks/SKILL.md`, including the chained-PR split recommendation when risk is High.
- Pinned the contract with `TestTasksSkillEmitsWorkloadGuard` in `catalog_test.go` — if the guard lines disappear from the skill, CI fails.

## Test

- RED→GREEN: new test fails before the skill edit, passes after.
- Gate green: `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race ./...` passes.

author: ciprianbodu
body:
## Problema
Pe laptop (`TORINO-ASPIRE5`, fără GPU), START_8000 eșua cu `RC=20` — `verify_imports` cerea `torch`/`neuralforecast` ca REQUIRED, dar nu sunt în venv.

**Cauză:** `.machine_profile` (gitignored, dar **sincronizat de OneDrive**) conținea profilul de pe stația ALF (`NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti`). START citea acest **cache** → credea că laptopul are GPU → profil GPU în `verify_imports` → cerea torch → fail.

## Fix
START apelează acum **MEREU** `:DetectGpu` (nvidia-smi = sursa de adevăr) și rescrie `.machine_profile` cu hardware-ul REAL al mașinii, în loc să creadă cache-ul sincronizat:
- **Laptop** → nvidia-smi absent → `CPU_ONLY` → profil CPU în verify_imports (torch **optional**) → pornește (metode GPU sărite la runtime).
- **ALF** → nvidia-smi prezent → `NVIDIA` → neschimbat.
- **Self-healing**: fiecare mașină își suprascrie profilul la pornire, deci sync-ul OneDrive nu mai contează.

Aceeași clasă de problemă ca `loto_jobs.db` — fișier de stare sincronizat între mașini.

## Workaround imediat (până dai pull)
`del .machine_profile` apoi `.\START_8000.bat` (PowerShell cere `.\`).

author: anshuman3kdka
body:
💡 **What:** Added the roving tabindex accessibility pattern (`tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}`) to custom UI primitives using `role="radiogroup"` and `role="tablist"` (`components/analyzer/ModeToggle.tsx` and `components/analyzer/InputPanel.tsx`). In `ModeToggle.tsx`, also implemented the required `onKeyDown` Arrow key navigation listener on the radio group. Fixed a dynamic `aria-controls` binding bug in `InputPanel.tsx`.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, generic custom tablists and radiogroups mapped all child elements directly into the sequential tab order. This violated ARIA keyboard interaction standards, forcing screen reader and keyboard users to tab through every single unselected option sequentially instead of allowing them to arrow-key between options and tab out quickly. Additionally, the `aria-controls` attribute on the tabs previously referenced the active tab's ID state variable instead of the static option loop value, causing invalid ARIA mapping when inactive tabs were focused.

📸 **Before/After:** No visual changes. Keyboard interaction only.

♿ **Accessibility:**
- Added roving tabindex `tabIndex={0}` to active radiogroup and tab elements, and `tabIndex={-1}` to inactive ones, keeping only the active one in the sequential tab order.
- In `ModeToggle.tsx`, attached an `onKeyDown` listener to manage focus via ArrowRight, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, and ArrowUp.
- Ensured `aria-controls` consistently refers to the correct static target panel id.

author: przemarzec
body:
## What

Generic, public-safe CI hardening — no runtime/package change.

- **`secret-scan.yml`** (new): gitleaks scans full history on push + PR for accidentally committed secrets. Runs the official pinned binary (checksum-verified) in a plain `run:` step, because the repo Actions policy allows only GitHub-owned + verified-publisher actions.
- **`ci.yml`**: new `dependency-audit` job runs `pip-audit --strict` — a dependency with a known CVE (or any audit collection failure) fails the build.
- **`release.yml`**: the publish job now runs `verify_wheel_data.py` after build, before the PyPI upload — a packaging regression (missing bundled data) is caught at the one point it would otherwise ship.
- **CHANGELOG**: maintenance entry under Unreleased.

## Why

Closes the public-repo CI hardening gap: secret detection + dependency CVE gating + wheel-data integrity at publish. All gates are generic (no project-specific patterns).

## Verification (local)

- All workflow YAML parses.
- `pip-audit --strict` → "No known vulnerabilities found".
- `python -m build` + `verify_wheel_data.py` → OK (required data present in wheel + sdist).
- No-release change (`ci:`) → semantic-release will not bump/publish.

### v0.5.13 — Bug fixes + sync/redaction/auth/state-resolution gaps

**Implementation fixes** (three bugs exposed by new tests):
- `m.room.join_rules` redaction: `allow` key was preserved in all room versions; now only preserved in v11+
- `m.room.aliases` redaction: `aliases` key was stripped in all versions (no case existed); now preserved v1–v10 and stripped v11+

author: zoorpha
body:
## Summary

Hardens the CHV repository against accidental breakage, unreviewed merges, unsafe CI defaults, and unsafe release/tag changes. **No product code is modified.**

## Changes

### 1. CODEOWNERS (`.github/CODEOWNERS`)
- Adds ownership mapping for 5 logical teams:
  - `chv-admins` — `.github/`, workflows, `SECURITY.md`
  - `chv-maintainers` — Rust workspace, protobuf, eBPF
  - `chv-frontend` — SvelteKit UI
  - `chv-ops` — deployment, packaging, install scripts, release docs
  - `chv-architecture` — ADRs, component specs, design docs
- Includes prominent comments explaining that teams must exist in the `kubedoio` org and have write access before enforcement works.

### 2. CI Workflow Permissions
- Adds `permissions: contents: read` to `ci.yml` and `proto.yml`, the only two workflows missing explicit workflow-level permission scoping.
- All workflows now follow the principle of least privilege:
  - Workflow default: `contents: read`
  - Publishing jobs elevate only at job level (`contents: write`, `attestations: write`, `id-token: write`) and are gated by GitHub Environments.

### 3. Dependabot Reviewer Placeholders
- Updates commented reviewer placeholders from generic `your-org/chv-maintainers` to actual `kubedoio/*` team names (cargo → maintainers, npm → frontend, actions → admins).

### 4. Governance Documentation
- **`docs/governance/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md`** — required branch protection settings for `main` and tag protection for `v*`, with Rulesets as the recommended alternative.
- **`docs/governance/REPOSITORY_HARDENING.md`** — comprehensive checklist covering:
  - Access control (signed commits, CODEOWNERS, admin enforcement)
  - CI/workflow security (minimal permissions, action allow-list, runner isolation)
  - Release/tag safety (environment gating, changelog validation, smoke tests)
  - Secret leak prevention (scanning, push protection, pre-commit hooks)
  - Supply chain (Dependabot, `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`, pinned actions)
  - Audit and monitoring

### 5. Automation Scripts (`scripts/github-setup/`)
- `apply-branch-protection.sh` — applies the `main` branch protection rule via `gh api`.
- `apply-tag-protection.sh` — applies the `v*` tag protection rule via `gh api`.
- `verify-settings.sh` — local + live verification of all hardening controls; exits non-zero if critical settings are missing.

## Verification

- [x] `bash -n` passes on all new scripts
- [x] `verify-settings.sh` runs locally (live checks skipped when `gh` is unauthenticated)
- [x] No changes to Rust, TypeScript, or shell product code
- [x] No changes to existing CI behavior — only permission declarations added

## Post-Merge Checklist for Admins

- [ ] Create GitHub teams: `chv-admins`, `chv-maintainers`, `chv-frontend`, `chv-ops`, `chv-architecture`
- [ ] Grant teams write access to this repository
- [ ] Apply branch protection: `./scripts/github-setup/apply-branch-protection.sh`
- [ ] Apply tag protection: `./scripts/github-setup/apply-tag-protection.sh`
- [ ] Enable "Require review from CODEOWNERS" in branch protection rules
- [ ] Set default workflow token permissions to read-only (Settings → Actions → Workflow permissions)
- [ ] Enable secret scanning + push protection (Settings → Security)
- [ ] Verify: `./scripts/github-setup/verify-settings.sh`

body:
## Summary

Implements `cc-cache-keys-per-source` (plan `config-v2-coherence`, spec config-distribution-model §7A.4 / D4 / D6, R6): the per-source content cache-key model — the uv-style policy deciding what makes a resolved unit's cached content stale.

## What changed (write scope)

- **`internal/config/cache_keys.go`** — pure policy + data, no git/network/clock:
  - `DefaultCacheKey(kind, inputs)` — kind defaults: `git` → resolved commit; `local` → resolved commit **plus** working-tree state (dirty marker or precise content hash, so uncommitted authoring is a distinct key); `http` → ETag → Last-Modified → content digest; `oci` → manifest digest; unknown kind → content-digest fallback.
  - `EffectiveCacheKey(kind, keys, inputs, opts)` — composes, in priority order: **force escapes** (per-unit `--refresh` via `CacheKeyOptions` and the config-declared `always_revalidate` marker → `AlwaysRevalidate` sentinel) over **per-source override selectors** (`file`/glob, `git:{commit,tags}`, `env`, `dir`-presence) over the **kind default**. Resolved facts come in via `CacheKeyInputs`, mirroring `staleness.go`'s seam shape. Keys are namespaced by kind and deterministic (selectors sorted before hashing).
- **`internal/config/agentsrc.go`** — `Source.cache_keys` (`*CacheKeys`, `omitempty`) so a defaulting source round-trips byte-for-byte.
- **`schemas/agentsrc.schema.json`** — `cache_keys` declared under the `source` object with `additionalProperties:false` (rejects unknown selectors; guards struct↔schema drift).

This is the pure policy/data layer; resolver/fetcher wiring (supplying `CacheKeyInputs`, recording the key in the lock) is a downstream task.

## Verification

- Focused unit tests (`internal/config`): all green; **100% per-file coverage on `cache_keys.go`**, package at 97.7%; per-file 95% gate PASS (enforce).
- CLI-runner: `da config verify` from a project whose sources carry `cache_keys` parses every block (exit 0); a type-mismatched `always_revalidate: "not-a-bool"` is rejected by the real parse path (`cannot unmarshal string into ... CacheKeys.sources.cache_keys.always_revalidate of type bool`), proving the typed field is wired into manifest deserialization (no silent ExtraFields drop).
- `gofmt` clean, `go vet` clean, full `go test ./...` green (45 packages), pre-push gates (build+vet POSIX+windows, coverage, sonar) passed.

Affected platform: CLI (`da config`). No behavior change to existing manifests — `cache_keys` is additive and omitted when absent.

# Phase 08 — Feature: List Detail

Ships the list-detail (list-items) screen end-to-end on **Android (Compose)** and
**iOS (SwiftUI)**, wired to the Phase-05 `ListDetailStore`. This is the app's
most-used surface — every interaction is optimistic and typed-but-unsubmitted text
survives process death.

Three slices, each a `feat` commit (plan synced in-commit) + a `docs(plan):`
SHA-backfill commit, per the Phase 05–07 cadence.

## What's in it

### Slice 1 — Android module + screen
- New **`:features:feature-list-detail`** Gradle module (`fluxit.kmp.feature`
  convention), registered in `settings.gradle.kts` and consumed by `:android-app`.
- `ListDetailRoute` (Koin/ViewModel glue + exhaustive `ListDetailEffect` → nav /
  snackbar / actions-sheet mapping), stateless `ListDetailScreen`, `ListDetailComponents`
  (snackbars, completion header, row variants, list-actions `ModalBottomSheet`,
  `completionFraction`), `ListDetailViewModel`, `ListDetailPreviews`.
- NavHost `list/{listId}` route now renders the real screen (replacing the placeholder).
- Behaviours: optimistic completion toggle, swipe-to-delete + 5s undo, hide/show
  completed, composer submit with inline error, ⋯ menu, back.
- **§5 process-death persistence** via `SavedStateHandle` (keys `composer:{listId}` /
  `showCompleted:{listId}`), replayed into the store as intents on (re)creation.

### Slice 2 — iOS screen
- `ListDetailView` / `ListDetailRow` / `ComposerDock` / `ListActionsSheet`;
  `ContentView` `.listDetail` route renders it and pushes `.itemDetail` on edit.
- Mirrors Android: `FluxItScaffold` + variant-B top bar, completion header +
  `FluxItProgressBar` above a flat `List` (inline non-sticky headers, §13),
  `.fluxItSwipeToDelete` per row, `ComposerDock` in the bottom bar (`.submitLabel(.send)`).
- **§5 persistence** via `@SceneStorage` (per-list keys), replayed as intents.
- `:shared:state` additions: `resolveListDetailStore()` resolver, a
  `ListDetailEffect.NavigateToEditItem.itemId()` Swift accessor, and a `listIdOf(value:)`
  factory (the `@JvmInline` `ListId` ctor isn't Swift-constructible).

### Slice 3 — tests + close-out
- `CompletionFractionTest` (androidUnitTest): empty / partial / full / none cases.
- `MASTER_PLAN.md`: Phase 08 → 🟢 Complete; ▶ Next Step → Phase 09.
- §14 hand-off checklist updated.

### Design-system backfill
- `FluxItToBuyListItem` gained an optional `subtitle` (§2 second line).
- `FluxItCompletedListItem` gained `onTap` + made the trash trailing optional (§2
  trash-removal — swipe handles delete). Applied to **both** Android
  (`FluxItListItem.kt`) and iOS (`FluxItListItem.swift`); the Theme Gallery still passes
  trash so it compiles.

## Scope decisions (documented in `plan/08_FEATURE_LIST_DETAIL.md`)

- **§4 menu — Edit list / Star / Reminders / Delete-list** render **disabled "(coming
  soon)" on Android** and are **omitted on iOS** (`.confirmationDialog` can't show
  disabled rows). The shipped store exposes no intents for them; they land with
  Phases 09/13 (the §6 cross-screen delete-list undo needs `RootStore` glue not yet
  present). Only **Clear completed** is wired (with a confirmation step).
- **Bulk-undo backfill deferred** (§13/§14): `ClearCompletedItems → List<ItemId>`,
  `RestoreItems(ids)`, `softDeleteCompletedByList RETURNING id` — consistent with the
  store's documented data-layer block (no restore primitive). Clear-completed surfaces
  failures only; per-item delete-undo dismisses the snackbar (the soft-delete stands).
- **Snapshot / UI-instrumented tests deferred to v2** by the standing scope decision.
  v1 coverage: `:shared:state` `ListDetailStoreTest`, exhaustive compile-time
  `when`/`switch` effect→nav mapping, `completionFraction` unit tests, `@Preview` /
  SwiftUI previews, and Konsist.
- Composer submit is button-tap only — the DS `FluxItInlineComposer` exposes no
  `ImeAction.Done` / disabled-when-blank wiring yet (store ignores blank submits).

## Testing / gates

Green throughout (per slice):
- Touched-module `:check` (`:features:feature-list-detail`, `:core:core-designsystem`,
  `:shared:state`)
- `:android-app:assembleDebug`
- `:build-logic:test --rerun-tasks` (arch + literal-ban Konsist rules)
- `scripts/test-ios.sh` (`** TEST SUCCEEDED **`)

**Not covered by automation (user's manual step):** on-device/sim visual confirm, the
demo flow (open → toggle → add → swipe-delete + undo → kill/reopen restores composer
text), TalkBack/VoiceOver a11y audit, and the 60fps perf budget.

## Commits

```
feat(list-detail): Phase 08 Slice 1 — :features:feature-list-detail module + Android screen
docs(plan): backfill commit SHA for Phase 08 Slice 1 (module + Android screen)
feat(list-detail): Phase 08 Slice 2 — iOS list-detail screen
docs(plan): backfill commit SHA for Phase 08 Slice 2 (iOS list-detail screen)
feat(list-detail): Phase 08 Slice 3 — completion-fraction tests + close-out
docs(plan): backfill commit SHA for Phase 08 Slice 3 (tests + close-out)
```

body:
## Summary

Replaces the hand-rolled `juce::ArgumentList` CLI parser with **one plain settings struct** (`PluginvalSettings`) that **CLI11 binds to directly**, and adds a new `--config <file.json>` option. CLI + environment-variable behaviour is preserved; the flat flags are unchanged (subcommands are a planned follow-up).

> Note: this PR started on `magic_args` (first two commits) and switched to **CLI11** after review (3rd commit) to remove duplication and avoid the C++23 / macOS 13.3 costs. See history.

## Design
CLI11 binds each option straight to a `PluginvalSettings` member, with the env var on the same line:
```cpp
app.add_option("--strictness-level", s.strictnessLevel, "...")->envname("STRICTNESS_LEVEL");
app.add_option("--sample-rates",     s.sampleRates,     "...")->delimiter(',');           // comma lists
app.add_option("--rtcheck",          s.realtimeCheck,   "...")->transform(CheckedTransformer(...)); // enum
```
- A `--config <file.json>` seeds the struct first; CLI11 only overwrites members whose flag/env was provided, so precedence is **defaults < config < env < CLI** (CLI wins) with no manual layering.
- `nlohmann/json` provides `--config` load + the child-process handoff (an authoritative base64 JSON arg, `--config-base64`, avoiding command-line quoting hazards).
- `PluginvalSettings::toPluginTestOptions()` converts to the existing `PluginTests::Options` at the JUCE boundary (unchanged downstream).

**Adding an option is 3 edits:** a struct member, a `nlohmann` macro entry, and one `add_option(...)` line. No parallel struct, no manual CLI→JSON or ENV→JSON code.

## Key changes
- New `PluginvalSettings.h`, `SettingsParser.{h,cpp}`, `SettingsSerializer.{h,cpp}`.
- `CommandLine.{h,cpp}` reduced to a thin adapter (~395 lines of old parser removed); `--run-tests`/`--strictness-help` dispatched by token scan, `--help`/`--version` handled by CLI11 (auto usage + a footer with env-var/commands notes).
- New `--config <file.json>`; precedence covered by tests.
- `CommandLineTests.cpp` rewritten against the new pipeline (env tests use `setenv`/`unsetenv` since CLI11 reads the real environment).

## Build / deps
- CPM: **CLI11 2.6.2** + **nlohmann/json 3.12.0** (both header-only).
- No language-standard or deployment-target change: stays `cxx_std_20` and macOS `10.11`. (CLI11 needs neither C++23 nor a newer macOS.)

## Testing
- `--run-tests` passes (all 21 CommandLineTests + existing suites).
- Real `--validate` SUCCEEDs on multiple VST3s at strictness 5 and 10 (full build with embedded VST3 validator, macOS 10.11 target).
- `--config` + CLI-override precedence verified by tests.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
Restructure the mode flags into subcommands (`pluginval validate` default / `run-tests` / `strictness-help`), keeping the old flat flags as deprecated aliases for one release. The settings struct + pipeline are designed to be reused unchanged.

author: ssam18
body: The first BGR2Lab or BGR2Luv conversion lazily constructs a softfloat based lookup table, and that construction is the slow part rather than the conversion itself. The 33x33x33 build called applyGamma about 108000 times even though it only depends on 33 distinct values per axis, and the whole cube was built on a single thread. This change memoizes applyGamma over those 33 values and parallelizes the cube loop, which drops the first call from roughly 110 ms to roughly 25 ms on my machine while keeping the per point math unchanged. I verified bit exactness by converting all 16.7 million 8 bit BGR inputs to both Lab and Luv and confirming the output hashes match the previous build exactly. Fixes #29222

author: daishiman
body:
## 概要

issue-1069/1070 で実装済みの tag master update API に対する**操作画面が `apps/web` に存在しなかった**問題を解消する。タグの短い名札（`code`）を後から書き換える専用の管理画面 `/admin/tag-master` を新設し、`code` / 表示名（`label`）/ カテゴリ（`category`）を一覧から選んで編集・保存できるようにする。

- 関連 Issue: #1116（CLOSED issue recovery / `task-issue-1069-followup-001` 消費）
- 種別: VISUAL（admin 新規ページ）/ 既存 API のみ接続（`apps/api` 無改修）

## なぜ必要か（初学者向け要約）

タグには人が見る表示名（例:「英語クラス」）と、コンピュータが使う短い名札（`code`、例: `english`）の 2 つがある。先生が `englsh` と打ち間違えて登録しても、これを**後から書き換える操作画面そのものが無かった**（書き換える仕組み＝API は issue-1069 で完成済みだが、押すボタンが画面に無い状態）。今回その専用管理画面を新設する。

編集中に別の人が同じタグの名札を変えると「他人の変更を上書きして消す」事故になるため、**編集開始時の名札を覚えて照合する仕組み（`expectedCode`、optimistic CAS）**を入れ、競合時は「もう使われている名札」と「古い情報のまま」の 2 種類を**別々のメッセージ**で表示する。

## route 決定（sibling `/admin/tag-master` を採る根拠）

| 観点 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 原典 Issue の想定 | tag master CRUD は `/admin/tags` に置けると想定 |
| 現コード実態 | `/admin/tags` は **tag QUEUE**（タグ提案レビュー）で占有済み（nav id `tag-queue`） |
| 子ルートの問題 | `isNavItemActive` は `pathname.startsWith(href + "/")` で判定するため、`/admin/tags/master` 等の子ルートにすると tag-queue nav が同時 active になる **nav 衝突バグ**が発生 |
| 採用方針 | **sibling ルート `/admin/tag-master`** を新設。接頭辞一致しないため衝突しないことを regression test で固定 |

read は既存 `safeServerFetch('/admin/tags?...')` を再利用し、web proxy は既存 catch-all `apps/web/app/api/admin/[...path]/route.ts` が PATCH を転送するため**新規 proxy 不要**。

## 変更内容

### 新規 component / API client

| 種別 | パス | 役割 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| route | `apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tag-master/page.tsx` | server component。`{ total, items }` を `items ?? []` で `TagMasterPanel` へ渡す |
| client | `apps/web/src/features/admin/components/_tags/TagMasterPanel.tsx` | 一覧テーブル + 行選択 → 編集フォーム表示。成功後 row 反映 |
| client | `apps/web/src/features/admin/components/_tags/TagMasterEditForm.tsx` | `FormField` で code/label/category 入力。行ロード時の `code` を `expectedCode` として保持。`useAdminMutation` で PATCH。409 を分離表示 |
| web API client | `apps/web/src/features/admin/api/tags.ts` `updateTag` | `PATCH /api/admin/tags/:tagId` を proxy 経由送信。変更フィールドのみ同梱し、`code` 変更時のみ `expectedCode` を付与 |
| error parse | 同上 `parseTagUpdateErrorCode` | JSON body の `error` を UI 表示可能な error code へ正規化 |

### nav 配線

| ファイル | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/components/shell/shell-config.ts` | `ShellNavItemId` に `"tag-master"` 追加。admin group に `{ id: "tag-master", href: "/admin/tag-master", label: "タグ管理", icon: "tag-master" }` を追加（`tag-queue`「タグキュー」と並置） |
| `apps/web/src/components/shell/icons.tsx` | nav id と同一キー `"tag-master"` の SVG path を追加 |

> nav label は tag QUEUE（「タグキュー」）と tag master（「タグ管理」）で明確に分け、member tag assignment UI との混同を回避。

## error マッピング（API レスポンス → UI 文言）

| HTTP / body.error | 意味 | UI 文言 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 409 `tag_code_conflict` | UNIQUE(code) 衝突 | この code は既に別のタグで使われています。別の code を入力してください。 |
| 409 `tag_stale_conflict` | optimistic CAS 衝突 | 保存前に別の変更が入りました。画面を更新して最新のコードを確認してください。 |
| 404 `tag_not_found` | 対象 tagId が存在しない | 対象のタグが見つかりません。一覧を再読み込みしてください。 |
| 400 `no_update_fields` | 変更フィールドが無い | 変更内容がありません。少なくとも 1 項目を編集してください。 |
| 400 `invalid_body` | CODE_RE 違反 / `expectedCode` 欠落 | 入力値を確認してください。 |

## 不変条件遵守

- mutation は `@/features/admin/hooks/useAdminMutation` 経由（不変条件 #10）
- 入力は `FormField` 経由（不変条件 #9・`<input>` 直書き禁止）
- 色は OKLch design token（不変条件 #2・HEX 直書き禁止）
- `apps/web` は D1 binding 非接触（不変条件 #5）。`apps/api` は一切変更なし（不変条件 #1 / #7）

## テスト構成

| ファイル | 役割 |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/features/admin/api/__tests__/tags.update.spec.ts` | updateTag 200 / 409 code_conflict / 409 stale_conflict / 404 / no_update_fields |
| `apps/web/src/features/admin/components/_tags/__tests__/TagMasterPanel.spec.tsx` | 一覧描画・行選択・編集到達・差分 PATCH・expectedCode 保持・409 分離表示・ハイフン code validation |
| `apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tag-master/page.spec.tsx` | GET `/admin/tags` の `{ total, items }` shape を page が正しく渡す |
| `apps/web/src/components/shell/__tests__/shell-config.spec.ts` | tag-master nav 追加・`/admin/tags` との active 衝突なし（regression） |
| `apps/web/playwright/tests/admin-tag-master-code-edit-ui.spec.ts` | 一覧・編集フォーム・conflict 表示の local fixture visual |

## スクリーンショット（Phase 11 local fixture）

### タグ一覧
![tag-master-list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daishiman/UBM-Hyogo/004e667e1daebe5745537a6a64808890d0c77ce5/docs/30-workflows/completed-tasks/issue-1116-admin-tag-master-code-edit-ui/outputs/phase-11/screenshots/tag-master-list.png)

### 編集フォーム
![tag-master-edit-form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daishiman/UBM-Hyogo/004e667e1daebe5745537a6a64808890d0c77ce5/docs/30-workflows/completed-tasks/issue-1116-admin-tag-master-code-edit-ui/outputs/phase-11/screenshots/tag-master-edit-form.png)

### code 衝突表示（tag_code_conflict）
![tag-master-code-conflict](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daishiman/UBM-Hyogo/004e667e1daebe5745537a6a64808890d0c77ce5/docs/30-workflows/completed-tasks/issue-1116-admin-tag-master-code-edit-ui/outputs/phase-11/screenshots/tag-master-code-conflict.png)

### 競合表示（tag_stale_conflict）
![tag-master-stale-conflict](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daishiman/UBM-Hyogo/004e667e1daebe5745537a6a64808890d0c77ce5/docs/30-workflows/completed-tasks/issue-1116-admin-tag-master-code-edit-ui/outputs/phase-11/screenshots/tag-master-stale-conflict.png)

> authenticated staging visual capture は staging deploy 後に user-gated で取得し、Gate-C を passed 化する（現状 `implemented_local_evidence_captured`）。

## 品質検証

- `pnpm install --force` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅（全 7 workspace PASS）

body:
## Summary
Replaces the exit-code-3 stub with a real impl built on \`Host\` +
\`QuicRuntime\` — gossipsub RPC frames now traverse a
\`/meshsub/1.1.0\` QUIC stream between the two zig nodes.

## What changed
- **examples/interop_quic_node.zig.** New \`runGossipsubInterop\`.
  Builds a \`Host\` whose \`local_peer_id\` is derived from the cert
  at \`CERT_PATH\` (\`peerIdFromVerifiedCertificate\` on the libp2p
  RFC 0001 extension — same peer id the matrix runner reads off
  \`gen-libp2p-cert\`'s stdout for \`REMOTE_PEER_ID\`), wires it
  through \`QuicRuntime\`, subscribes, and drains swarm events.
- **interop_quic/run_matrix.sh.** \`zig:gossipsub\` removed from
  the skip table. \`rust-libp2p:gossipsub\` stays skipped pending a
  separate mesh-formation timing fix.
- **README.** Refresh — exit code 3 is gone, B3 row notes the
  asymmetry below.

## Known asymmetry vs. go-libp2p
\`QuicRuntime.onPublishCommand\` fans publishes out to
\`outbound_by_peer.keys()\` only. The listener side has no outbound
peers in a 2-node bring-up, so the zig roles are inverted vs. go:

    ROLE=server  → subscribe, count, exit 0
    ROLE=client  → subscribe, dial, publish N, exit 0

Doesn't change today's CI surface — cross-impl runs only on cron +
manual dispatch and is still gated behind the open zquic TLS gaps.
Tracked as a follow-up: let \`onPublishCommand\` reach inbound peers
via \`listener.server\` instead of the outbound slot's
\`nextLocalBidiStream\`.

## Test plan
- [x] \`zig build\` — clean.
- [x] zig matrix \`handshake,ping,reqresp,gossipsub\`: 4/4 ok.
- [ ] CI: same-impl baseline green incl. gossipsub.
- [ ] CI: cross-impl row runs on cron + dispatch only.

## What & why
Phase 4 — the Set-up data model the six-stop happy path promises. Adds an additive `loans_properties` table linking a loan/mortgage account to the property it funds, with the deductible-interest %. **Capture-only**: recording a link does **not** change the indicative position or claim anything — it pre-fills the guided interest/principal split coming in Phase 5 (confirm-each-pattern).

## Layers (mirrors existing properties/accounts CRUD)

author: copilot
body:
The `DartLangModTool` submodule's latest `master` commit (`e24b58a`) has `puredartlua` declared as a local Windows path dependency in `pubspec.yaml`, causing `dart pub get` to fail in CI with exit code 66:

```
could not find package puredartlua at "X:/Big_Code/Latest_ONB_Code/DartLuaLib/lualib"
```

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/build_native.yml`** — adds a step between submodule update and `dart pub get` that writes a `pubspec_overrides.yaml` into the submodule directory, redirecting `puredartlua` to its pub.dev release (`^1.0.8`) instead of the non-existent local path:

```yaml
- name: Override puredartlua path dependency for CI
  shell: bash
  run: |
    cat > src/DartLangModTool-master/pubspec_overrides.yaml << 'EOF'
    dependency_overrides:
      puredartlua: ^1.0.8
    EOF
```

`pubspec_overrides.yaml` is the standard Dart mechanism for overriding dependencies without touching upstream source — appropriate here since `DartLangModTool` is a submodule we don't own.

author: shbmx
body:
Item 4 from the review follow-up. Exposes the motor's read/**write** configuration registers as Home Assistant config entities so they can be changed from the UI instead of being read-only attributes.

## New entities (per curtain, under the device, `EntityCategory.CONFIG`)

| Entity | Type | Register | Purpose |
|--------|------|----------|---------|
| **Reverse direction** | switch | `0x03` | Fix a reversed motor (open/close swapped) **from the UI, no re-wiring** |
| **Hand-pull start** | switch | `0x04` | Enable/disable starting the motor by hand |
| **Passive switch type** | select | `0x27` | Weak-current external switch type |
| **Active switch type** | select | `0x28` | High-current external switch type |

## How it works
- New `DooyaController.write_register()` sends the protocol write command (`0x02`) and confirms a valid framed + CRC-checked ack.
- Entities read their initial value from the device attributes captured once at setup (PR #2) and write back on change, updating local state on a successful ack.
- `select`/`switch` added to `PLATFORMS`; both link to the existing device via `identifiers={(DOMAIN, entry_id)}`. Entity names/options are translated.

The most useful one is **Reverse direction** — previously a wrong-way motor meant re-wiring A/B or re-pairing; now it's a toggle.

## Tests / CI
- +2 tests: `write_register` frame bytes + no-ack failure path. **31 pass.**
- Write-command framing/CRC verified against spec §5.3 (`55 12 34 02 03 01 01` → `9D 5B`, `…02 27 01 02` → `9D 51`).
- `ruff` clean, `py_compile` + JSON valid. Version → 1.3.0.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/ -q` → 31 passed
- [x] `ruff check custom_components/ tests/` → clean
- [ ] Hardware: toggle Reverse direction and confirm open/close swap; change switch-type selects and confirm the motor accepts them.

> Note: config entities reflect the value read at startup; changing a setting via the physical remote requires an integration reload to refresh them (documented in the README).

## Summary

- Add a shared regular-chat KB prompt mode contract in `klai_kb_chat_mode.py`.
- Keep `ChatRetrievalPolicy` narrow: it now returns prompt mode, scope decision, user id, and failure reason only.
- Route the same prompt mode into `KbAnswerPolicy` and `_klai_kb_meta`, then have the citation renderer prefer that mode over legacy `kb_narrow`.
- Add hook and renderer tests for the adversarial review gaps: no-KB plus missing identity, and post-call mode overriding stale/contradictory `kb_narrow`.

## Why

The initial policy object was too broad: several fields looked like enforceable contract but were not consumed by the hook. This version removes those dead contract fields and makes one prompt-mode value flow through pre-call policy, retrieval branch handling, answer policy metadata, and post-call citation rendering.

`kb_narrow` remains in `_klai_kb_meta` for compatibility and existing telemetry, but the renderer now derives strict/open behavior from `chat_retrieval_prompt_mode` when present.

## Purpose

Adds a read-only TerraFusion Sync / DB evidence adapter for the Benton Real Dev Server Readiness gate.

This does not make County Studio production-proof. It gives the readiness gate a way to attempt real Sync/DB evidence reads instead of leaving load batch, seed, truth, canonical, and GIS dependency state permanently opaque.

- Wired `proof:county-studio:benton-real-dev-server-readiness` to use the adapter when no explicit source file is supplied.
- Updated evidence artifacts for the current local state.

## Current evidence posture

- Sync/DB evidence adapter: `SYNC_DB_EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN`
- Benton real dev readiness: `REAL_DEV_SERVER_BLOCKED`
- `realDevServerAllowed=false`

Observed local evidence:

- Drain PID `28503` is not alive.
- DB counts remain `UNKNOWN` because local `psql` is unavailable, so the adapter does not invent counts.

This PR is stacked on PR #898 (`codex/county-studio-real-dev-readiness`) and supports the County Studio proof taxonomy introduced by PR #891. It should not be represented as production proof or operational proof.

body:
### Motivation
- Enable a self-contained GPIDE sequence encoder + FOCOPS-inspired safety/trust-region SAC path configurable from INI files for improved sequence-based navigation.
- Make the AirSim image pipeline robust to occasional empty responses or RPC failures so long training runs do not crash the trainer.
- Separate safety/constraint costs from scalar rewards and provide episode-level metrics and logging to monitor safety performance during training.

### Description
- Updated config templates to enable `temporal_encoder = gpide` and added `GPIDE`, `FOCOPS`, `reward`, `safety`, and `constraint` sections and sensible defaults, plus `image_retry_count` and `print_train_info` options.
- Hardened `gym_env/envs/airsim_env.py` by adding `_sim_get_images_with_retry`, image caching (`last_depth_image`, `last_gray_image`), fallback image generators, `image_retry_count` config handling, conditional per-step HUD logging via `print_train_info`, and an `_add_constraint_info` helper to attach `constraint_cost` and related diagnostics to the environment `info` dict.
- Extended the sequence GPIDE agent in `scripts/utils/sequence_gpide.py` with reward-history scaling, reward clipping for history features in `SequenceReplayBuffer`, improved sampling, a baseline cost penalty (`cost_penalty_coef`) in addition to the adaptive Lagrange multiplier, episode counters and mutually-exclusive episode reason classification, expanded CSV headers, episode CSV and JSON metrics output, and additional state saved into checkpoint payloads.
- Improved training orchestration in `scripts/utils/thread_train.py` to write episode CSV and metrics JSON paths and to save the sequence agent using the agent's `total_steps` value.

### Testing
- Ran a local smoke test that exercised the AirSim image retrieval code with a mocked empty/invalid response to verify retry, fallback, and last-image caching behavior; the fallback path executed and returned valid arrays (success).
- Executed a short end-to-end sequence agent training run with `learn(total_timesteps=1000)` on a CI-like host to verify replay buffer behavior, constraint cost plumbing, CSV/JSON logging and checkpoint saving; training loop completed and produced the expected `episode_log.csv`, `training_log.csv`, and `metrics_summary.json` (success).
- Basic save/load of a GPIDE checkpoint was exercised to confirm the extended payload fields (`reward_history_scale`, `cost_penalty_coef`, and `training_metrics`) round-trip correctly (success).

author: daz-mac
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where species profiles with preferred_tide_phase: ["high"] (including the default general profile) always received a tide score of 30/100. The scoring engine compared preferred_tide_phase values against tide phase strings with a literal match — since TideProxy only produces "rising"/"falling"/"flat", "high" never matched.

**Fix:** Three-layer change:
1. **TideProxy** computes nearest_high_hours[] and nearest_low_hours[] — absolute hours from each timestamp to nearest high/low tide
2. **Scoring engine** handles "high"/"low" via proximity scoring (10 at 0h -> 3.0 at 1.5h). Combined with phase preferences via averaging
3. **Card** shows tide score as colored bar + numeric in row detail

### Files changed
- tide_proxy.py — nearest_high_hours/nearest_low_hours output
- const.py — TIDE_HIGH_WINDOW_HOURS constant
- data_formatter.py — promote proximity fields
- ocean_scoring.py — proximity scoring with averaging
- ocean-fishing-card.js — tide score bar in detail
- test_scoring.py — 11 new unit tests

### Test plan
- 11 new unit tests covering all proximity scenarios
- Verified via smoke test (11/11 pass)
- Existing 160 tests unchanged

author: grumbly4308
body:
## Problem

Streaming chat responses only forwarded `text` events, so during extended thinking / tool / subagent work the wrapper emitted no bytes for minutes. On the heavy `xhigh`/`ultracode` + 1M-context path, an idle-timeout proxy in front of the wrapper severed the chunked response mid-stream. OpenWebUI's aiohttp client surfaced this as a truncated-payload error (`TransferEncodingError: 400, Not enough data to satisfy transfer length header`) — the "error 400 on a simple prompt" symptom.

## Fix

- **Heartbeats:** pump runner events through an `asyncio.Queue`; the consumer races `queue.get()` against a 15s timeout and emits an SSE keep-alive comment (`: keep-alive`) when idle. The queue decouples heartbeats from the generator so a timeout never cancels the `await` inside `run_stream` (which would kill the Claude subprocess and drop the session lock). Interval configurable via `CLAUDE_WRAPPER_SSE_HEARTBEAT` (default 15s).
- **Progress:** forward `thinking` on a separate `reasoning_content` delta channel — live progress without polluting answer content.
- **Cleanup:** cancel the pump on early exit (client disconnect) so subprocess + lock tear down cleanly.
- **docker-compose:** drop duplicate `/data/inbox` mount that broke `compose up`.

## Tests

Added `test_chat_completion_stream_heartbeat` (slow runner, asserts keep-alive fires, thinking lands on the reasoning channel, answer content stays clean, `[DONE]` terminates). Full suite: 49 passed.

## Operational note

The heartbeat removes the idle-timeout failure. Also ensure no hop imposes a *total* request cap below the wrapper's 1800s job ceiling — set OpenWebUI's `AIOHTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` and any reverse-proxy `proxy_read_timeout` to comfortably exceed 1800s.

author: pggpgg
body:
## What

The first-class officer Attack/Defense/Health runtime (Phases 1–4 of `docs/OFFICER_STAT_FORMULA.md`) is **already shipped and green**, but the spec still carried stale `draft — awaiting maintainer input / blocked` headers. This PR corrects the status and ties the three calibration anchors (§261–263) to their real production officers.

- **`tests/officer_stat_calibration_anchors.rs`** (new) — 4 passing tests asserting the LCARS→engine routing and direction of each anchor:
  - **Cadet Kirk** `cadet-kirk-a80563` "Motivational" → crew-wide `officer_stat_all += 0.08`
  - **Marla** `marla-9732c7` "Let Me Help You" → crew-wide `officer_stat_all += 0.50`
  - **Kras** `kras-a47042` "Know your Enemy" → enemy-bridge pending contribution (value 0.20), gated on `DefenderIsPlayerShip` → no-op vs NPC hostiles, active in PvP

  Each test records the engine's *predicted* bonus in its assertion messages.
- **`docs/OFFICER_STAT_FORMULA.md`** — status flipped to "specified and implemented"; the "Examples to validate" section now points at the anchor test with routing locked per anchor.

## Why

The stale headers actively misled about project state (they implied a multi-day implementation was blocked, when in fact it had landed). The anchors do the half of the §261–263 validation that's possible without in-game data: they lock the **routing and direction** of each effect and surface the engine's numbers for later comparison.

## Reviewer notes

- The anchor tests use a **representative** explorer breakpoint table + crew totals (a deterministic stand-in), not a specific in-game ship. They assert direction/routing, not exact magnitude.
- The **one genuinely remaining item** is the in-game *expected damage deltas* for the three anchors (still `_TBD_` in the spec). When those observed numbers are supplied (with the exact ship + crew used), swap the representative ship/totals for the real ones and tighten the `>=`/`<=` asserts to exact equality.
- The Kras test demonstrates the `DefenderIsPlayerShip` gate as the real no-op-vs-hostile mechanism (PvE gated off vs PvP active), rather than a zero-totals proxy.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test officer_stat_calibration_anchors` → 4 passed
- Related suites still green: `lcars_drop_report` (11), `officer_kirk_morale_stat` (3), `officer_stat_building_profile_test` (1)

author: williamthome
body:
# Description

The `h3_*` bench-client tests drive the `quic` dependency's QUIC client against the roadrunner HTTP/3 server over UDP loopback. Under CI load the dependency's handshake intermittently takes longer than a single connect deadline (its lost-packet recovery runs for many seconds, or the connection process is starved before its retransmit timer fires), so the test fails even though nothing is broken. Instead of leaning on one ever-longer deadline, the client now retries the handshake a few times with a fresh connection, which starts with fresh timers and almost always connects right away. The fast HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 tests are untouched.

Follows up #122, which widened the timeout but still hit the deadline mid-recovery.

author: codyswanngt
body:
Updates @codyswann/lisa to 2.142.1 and applies refreshed templates.

## Why this version

This is a source-less repo (no src/, only root-level *.config.ts). Two Lisa fixes in this version range unblock its hooks/CI:

1. **tsconfig files fallback (2.142.0)** — the `ensure-tsconfig-local-files-fallback` migration backfills `"files": []` into tsconfig.local.json. The old `include: ["src/**/*"]` matched zero files, so `tsc --noEmit` failed with TS18003, blocking the pre-commit hook. With `files: []`, TypeScript treats zero sources as intentional. Verified: `tsc --noEmit` now exits 0, no TS18003.

2. **vitest passWithNoTests (2.142.1)** — the forced `test`/`test:unit`/`test:cov` scripts ran `vitest` which exited 1 on "No test files found", failing the pre-push hook. The vitest config factories now set `passWithNoTests: true`, so a zero-test repo passes. Verified: `bun run test:cov` now exits 0.

## Changes
- package.json: @codyswann/lisa ^2.106.0 → ^2.142.1 (devDependencies)
- tsconfig.local.json: `files: []` added by migration
- bun.lock, .claude/settings.json, CLAUDE.md, eslint.ignore.config.json: refreshed by apply

body:
## What

Adds a chain-of-thought **reasoning block**, **trim settings**, a bigger token budget, and a **step-climb visual** — reconciled onto the current propulsion-aware briefing shape.

### Backend (commit 1)
- `max_tokens` 2000 → 4000.
- New `reasoning` block the model populates **first** and treats as the source of truth: weight % MTOW → power margin → derived takeoff power → initial cruise level → step-climb rationale → fuel burn → landing weight → propulsion note.
- The requested hard rules, **scoped to jets** so turboprop/piston handling is preserved: initial-cruise-FL bands by weight % MTOW, the ~87% N1 floor / near-TOGA rule, and a fleet-wide per-100nm fuel-burn table.
- `takeoff.trimSetting` + `approachLanding.trimLanding` with Airbus / Boeing / GA trim guidance.

### Frontend (commit 2)
- `Reasoning` type + the two trim fields on the shared types.
- Collapsible **"Show workings"** panel above the phase cards — collapsed by default, smaller/dimmer than the cards.
- **Takeoff Trim** and **Landing Trim (running)** rows (shown only when populated).
- Step-climb renders as a **horizontal sequence of FL chips** (split on arrows) instead of one text line.

Layout, theming, card structure, and the copy button are unchanged.

## Deviation from the original request

This change request was written against an older, jet-only snapshot (`n1Percent` / `mach` / `cruiseN1` / `initialFL` / `stepClimb`-as-array). Applying it verbatim would have reverted the propulsion-aware refactor now on `main` and broken the build. Instead the field names on `main` (`powerSetting` / `cruiseSpeed` / `cruisePower` / `stepClimb` object) are kept, and the reasoning block is propulsion-aware (e.g. "Power margin / FLEX" covers jet FLEX *and* turboprop/piston derate).

## Notes

- `copyBriefing.ts` left untouched to honor "don't change the copy button" — trim/reasoning aren't in the copied text (easy to add if wanted).
- Not yet exercised against the live model end-to-end; types + build verified.

author: 3leapsdave
body:
## Summary

PR-2 of 4 for `fulpack` — adds **`extract`** with the mandatory security model. Builds on PR-1's read paths (#7).

## What's included

- **`extract(archive, destination, options)`** for tar/tar.gz/zip/gzip.
- **Security (always enforced)** — fails before writing the offending entry:
  - `safe_join`: rejects `../` traversal (`PATH_TRAVERSAL`) and absolute paths (`ABSOLUTE_PATH`)
  - `symlink_escapes`: rejects symlinks whose target escapes the destination (`SYMLINK_ESCAPE`)
  - decompression-bomb guards: `max_size` (1 GiB default) + `max_entries` (10k default) → `DECOMPRESSION_BOMB`
- **Behavior:** overwrite policy (`error`/`skip`/`overwrite`), `include_patterns` glob filter, `ExtractResult` counts; symlinks created on unix, skipped+warned on other platforms.
- Shares `read.rs` `open`/`corrupt` helpers; `ExtractOptions` derives `Default`.
- Docs: README fulpack section + feature-matrix updated.

## Tests

- Unit: `safe_join` (relative ok / traversal / absolute), `symlink_escapes`.
- Integration: fixture round-trip; **`pathological.tar.gz` extracts cleanly** (it's safe-by-construction — simulates attack *shapes* via naming, no real `../`/absolute/escape); **zip-slip rejection** (synthetic `../evil.zip` → `PATH_TRAVERSAL`, nothing escapes); max-entries bomb guard; overwrite policy.

## Verification

`cargo test --all-features` (385 + 75) + fulpack-only + MSRV 1.88 build; clippy `-D warnings`; goneat assess 100%.

## Note

The tar crate's `Builder` refuses to write `..` paths, so the zip-slip test uses a synthetic **zip** (the zip writer stores names verbatim) — which is also the realistic zip-slip vector.

## Next

author: eeiaao
body:
## What

Adds `ConcentratedLiquidityCurve`, a Uniswap v3-style implementation of `IAmmCurve` and the dominant 2026 DEX model (also Orca and Raydium on Solana).

Liquidity sits in price ranges, so the active liquidity `L` is constant only between adjacent initialized ticks. Inside a range the curve is constant-product on the virtual reserves `L/sqrt(P)` and `L*sqrt(P)`; crossing a tick changes `L` by that tick's liquidity. A swap walks the ticks, consuming each range to its boundary, crossing into the next, and stopping when the input is spent or the liquidity runs out, so a swap can fill less than its full size. The state is the current sqrt(price), the active liquidity, and the tick table; the math runs in double, enough for a backtest.

## Tests

A swap inside one range matches `ConstantProductCurve` on the virtual reserves; a known cross-tick swap matches the hand-computed two-segment walk and caps when liquidity ends; applySwap moves the price to the tick boundary; price impact grows with size. Full suite 118/118.

## MCP impact

None beyond a bundled-data refresh: the amm-pricing page gained a concentrated-liquidity section, re-syncing docs.fts.sqlite. Header-only, no binding or IDL surface change, parity unchanged.

Closes #1220

## Summary

- Changed `test_binary_permissions_unix` to check `scripts/install.sh` instead of the root `install.sh` wrapper
- Changed the assertion from `chmod +x` to `chmod 755`, which is what `scripts/install.sh` actually contains (lines 382 and 390)

## Root cause

The test was checking `install.sh` (root), a thin delegation wrapper that contains no `chmod` calls. The actual permission-setting logic lives in `scripts/install.sh`, which sets `chmod 755` on both `perllsp` and `perl-dap` binaries after download.

## User impact

None. The delegation chain was already correct — `install.sh` delegates to `scripts/install.sh` which sets 755. This fix aligns the test with the actual behavior that was always working.

## Verification

`cargo test -p perl-dap --test dap_packaging_tests --features dap-phase3` — all 6 tests pass (previously `test_binary_permissions_unix` was failing with `assertion failed: script_text.contains("chmod +x")`).

author: jburkhardt4
body:
## Summary

Introduces a new Claude agent (`emil-design-eng`) that encodes Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. This agent provides expert guidance on UI polish, animation decisions, component design patterns, and interaction design—helping the team build interfaces where every detail compounds into something that feels right.

## Key Changes

- **New agent file**: `.claude/agents/emil-design-eng.md` (687 lines)
  - Core philosophy section covering taste, unseen details, and beauty as leverage
  - Animation decision framework with frequency-based guidance and easing rules
  - Spring animation patterns for natural motion and interruptibility
  - Component building principles (buttons, popovers, tooltips, blur masking)
  - CSS transform mastery and clip-path animation techniques
  - Gesture and drag interaction patterns with momentum and damping
  - Performance rules (GPU-accelerated properties, CSS variable pitfalls, WAAPI)
  - Accessibility considerations (prefers-reduced-motion, touch hover states)
  - Sonner principles for building loved components
  - Stagger animations and debugging techniques
  - Review checklist with Before/After markdown table format

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Mandatory review format**: All UI code reviews must use markdown tables with `| Before | After | Why |` columns—never list format
- **Animation decision tree**: Frequency-based rules determine whether to animate (keyboard actions: never; 100+ times/day: no animation; occasional: standard; rare: can delight)
- **Easing guidance**: Strong custom curves via `cubic-bezier()` preferred over built-in CSS easings; `ease-in` explicitly discouraged for UI
- **Duration targets**: UI animations should stay under 300ms; specific ranges for buttons (100-160ms), tooltips (125-200ms), dropdowns (150-250ms), modals (200-500ms)
- **Hardware acceleration**: Framer Motion shorthand (`x`, `y`, `scale`) not GPU-accelerated; use full `transform` strings for performance
- **Initial response**: Agent introduces itself on first invocation without a question, then awaits user input

This agent serves as a reference for design decisions across the BKT AI-Apply project and can be invoked for UI code reviews, animation decisions, and component pattern guidance.
